MUNICH, Germany — As modern battlefields grow increasingly complex and lethal, integrating real-time medical data and advanced analytics is proving to be far more than just clinical support and improvement - it is an active combat multiplier.
A U.S. Army Medical Service Corps officer assigned to Medical Readiness Command -Europe emphasized this concept for operational evolution during the bi-annual NATO Force Health Protection Summit, held Oct. 20-22 at the NATO Force Health Protection Center of Excellence in Munich. Approximately 150 NATO and Allied force health protection subject matter experts attended the three-day event.
During the summit, Col. Paul Hester, chief data officer and chief of Force Health Protection for Medical Readiness Command-Europe, presented on preserving combat power and warfighter lethality in contested multi-domain operations. His presentation was titled "Data IS Force Health Protection."
According to senior Army medical experts, Force Health Protection represents the integrated set of measures designed to prevent disease and injury, ensure medical readiness, and protect U.S. forces against occupational and environmental hazards across all operational environments.
"Emerging system integration (SI) technologies and systems can be used to enhance U.S. Army soldier capabilities and capacity when operating for prolonged periods of time in austere and resource-limited environments," Hester said. "Military medicine efforts are able to combine system integration (SI) - enabled personalized predictive analytics with wearable devices to develop solutions that can help units and commanders. Real-time knowledge of health biometrics and disease non-battle injury threats provide tactical, operational, and strategic advantage over adversaries."
Hester noted that disease non-battle casualties (DNBI) remain the primary threat to military strength and unit readiness.
"Historically speaking, DNBI accounts for a significantly higher erosion of combat power and increased demand on all roles of care and medical evacuation systems than battle injuries," Hester said. "I consider data as force health protection and look at it as an active combat multiplier. It helps us preserve combat power and warfighter lethality in contested multi-domain operations.”
Traditional force health protection centers on countermeasures, including immunizations, personal protective equipment, and sanitation audits. This is followed by reactive medical evacuation once symptoms develop or injury occurs. However, Hester urged military leaders to transition their mindset from a reactive posture to a predictive and even autonomous operational model.
"Wouldn't it be great if we were able to provide persistent data feeds using wearables, chem-bio drone sniffer pods, etc. into battle visualization feeds?" Hester added. "The technology exists, we just have to figure out how to incorporate it into our operational systems, so it becomes part of how we fight across the joint force."
Senior Army medical officials emphasize that in multi-domain and large-scale combat operations, decision advantage is crucial. Leaders must visualize operational medical capabilities, clear battlefields of casualties, prevent disease, return recovered soldiers to the fight, and resupply tactical formations engaged in close combat. Hester's dream of a data-driven framework ensures medical forces sustain warfighter lethality across the theater.
“Operating with an informational shield turns health data from administrative paperwork into an active force protection asset that converts latency into battlefield superiority,” added Hester. “Having real-time access to a predictive telemetry links every medical echelon into an integrated combat multiplier; intercepting threats before Soldiers health degrades and keeping Soldiers in the fight while simultaneously maximizing return to duty.”
title: Data-Driven Force Health Protection is a Vital Combat Multiplier

Scams often increase after disasters. Scammers may ask for money or personal information to steal your identity. If Super Typhoon Bavi damaged your home or belongings, protect your information.
After you apply for FEMA help, a housing inspector may call or text to set up a visit. The number may show as unknown or out of state. Return the call, but verify that the caller is a FEMA inspector before sharing any personal information.
How to verify it is a FEMA inspector:
- The inspector will have your 9-digit FEMA registration number. Ask them to give it to you.
- The inspector will have a FEMA photo ID badge. Ask to see it.
- FEMA, SBA, and other disaster workers will never ask you for money or payment.
- FEMA inspectors will not ask for your bank or other financial information.
You can also call the FEMA Helpline at 671-735-1050 or 800-621-3362 to verify if the call, text, or visit is from a FEMA inspector. Give FEMA the inspector’s name.
If FEMA approves your application for assistance and you chose online or mobile payment, you may get an email from no-reply@digitalpayouts.com. This is a trusted payment service, even though it does not use a .gov address. Check that the sender’s email address matches exactly.
Did someone apply for FEMA help using your name?
If an inspector visits but you did not apply for FEMA help, tell the inspector right away. They can ask FEMA to stop the application.
If you receive a FEMA letter but did not apply, call the FEMA Helpline at 671-735-1050 or 800-621-3362. If you use a relay or captioned phone service, give FEMA that number.
Report scams
If you think you were scammed, report it to local police right away.
To report fraud involving FEMA disaster help:
- Email: StopFEMAFraud@fema.dhs.gov
- Mail: FEMA, 400 C Street SW, Suite SW-1009, Mail Stop 3005, Washington, DC 20472-3005
For help with identity theft, visit IdentityTheft.gov.
title: Guam: Watch Out for Disaster Scams

BOSTON – A Tewksbury, Mass. man has been charged with threatening the President of the United States.

Trenton Touch, 18, was charged by criminal complaint with making a threat against the President of the United States. Touch is currently in state custody and will make an initial appearance in federal court in Boston on Nov. 9, 2026.

According to the charging documents on Sept. 10, 2026, law enforcement received information relating to four Instagram accounts that contained violent and threatening content, including a threat against the President of the United States. Further investigation revealed that Touch is the alleged user of all four accounts. Records showed that Touch allegedly submitted multiple communications in which he threatened to kill others. These messages included alleged threats to shoot up a school and “kill trump.”

On June 21, 2026, Touch allegedly posted an image of a firearm in an Instagram direct message along with a threat:

• “it’s time” • “im gonna kill trump” • “not yet unc I suck at shooting past 200 yards.”

Touch allegedly made frequent references to mass shooters specifically those who conducted their attacks based on racially motivated violent extremism, referring to these mass shooters as “heroes,” and frequently referencing the Christchurch shootings in New Zealand that killed 51 people.

During a search of Touch’s residence, a revolver-style firearm was seized along with multiple military-style or military surplus items including camouflage clothing, a ballistics helmet, military-style knives and a hatchet.

“Trenton Touch is an individual whose alleged threats could not be ignored,” said United States Attorney Leah B. Foley. “Threatening the President of the United States is a serious crime and is not protected free speech. My office will continue to work with our law enforcement partners to investigate and prosecute anyone who incites violence and threatens harm.”

“Trenton Touch is an individual whose alleged threats could not be ignored,” said United States Attorney Leah B. Foley. “Threatening the President of the United States is a serious crime and is not protected free speech. My office will continue to work with our law enforcement partners to investigate and prosecute anyone who incites violence and threatens harm.”

“Trenton Touch is an alleged white supremacist who now stands accused of threatening to kill the President. Based on the evidence recovered by FBI Boston’s Joint Terrorism Task Force – including a firearm, military-style knives, a hatchet, and a ballistics helmet – he allegedly had the means to do it. There’s no question Mr. Touch posed a grave threat to public safety,” said Ted E. Docks, Special Agent in Charge of the Federal Bureau of Investigation’s Boston Division. “Your FBI will continue to work closely with our partners, using every tool available, to protect the public and stop people from turning violent rhetoric into action.”

The charge of making a threat against the President provides for a sentence of up to five years in prison, three years of supervised release and a fine of up to $250,000. Sentences are imposed by a federal district court judge based upon the U.S. Sentencing Guidelines and statutes which govern the determination of a sentence in a criminal case.

U.S. Attorney Foley; FBI SAC Docks; and Tewksbury Police Chief Ryan M. Columbus made the announcement today. Valuable assistance was provided by the Methuen Police Department and the Massachusetts State Police. Assistant U.S. Attorney Chris Looney of the National Security Unit is prosecuting the case. The details contained in the charging documents are allegations. The defendant is presumed innocent unless and until proven guilty beyond a reasonable doubt in a court of law.
title: Massachusetts Man Charged with Making a Threat Against the President of the United States

Rep. Foster Unveils Discussion Draft of Legislation to Modernize Financial Regulatory Reporting and Strengthen Oversight of the Financial System
Washington, DC – Today, Congressman Bill Foster, top Democrat on the House Financial Institutions Subcommittee, released the Real-Time Regulatory Study Act. 
Financial services driven by artificial intelligence and round-the-clock payments systems may contribute to and rapidly spread financial stress. As the financial system accelerates, real-time information and automated tools can help institutions and regulators respond faster, improve access to liquidity, and better prepare for orderly bank resolutions. Meanwhile, advances in AI are creating new cybersecurity threats. Through enhanced collective maintenance and security built in from the start, open-source software can provide stronger protection against cyber threats. Model open-source software also has the potential to lower development and reporting costs for community banks and credit unions and expand their access to advanced risk-management capabilities.
The Real-Time Regulatory Study Act directs the Federal Reserve Board, in coordination with other financial regulators, to develop, test, and publicly release open-source demonstration software to evaluate how technology can streamline regulatory obligations, reduce compliance costs, and provide regulators with real-time information on the condition of financial institutions nationwide. The Federal Reserve would seek technical contributions from financial institutions, technology providers, open-source organizations, and researchers.
“With advances in AI creating new cybersecurity threats and financial risks, it's more important than ever that we modernize the way we monitor the health of our financial institutions. My Real-Time Regulatory Study Act would explore how secure, open-source technology can help banks and credit unions reduce compliance costs, give regulators real-time insight into emerging risks, and strengthen the stability of our financial system. We cannot afford to rely on outdated systems to oversee an increasingly complex financial sector,” said Rep. Bill Foster.
A one-pager on the Real-Time Regulatory Study Act of 2026 can be found here. The full discussion draft can be found here.
title: Rep. Foster Unveils Discussion Draft of Legislation to Modernize Financial Regulatory Reporting and Strengthen Oversight of the Financial System

ALBUQUERQUE – A Las Cruces man pleaded guilty to possessing more than 40 grams of fentanyl while armed.

According to court documents, on July 5, 2025, Kenneth Manuel Aguirre , 44, knowingly possessed two firearms and ammunition despite having previously been convicted of a felony offense punishable by more than one year in prison. As a convicted felon, Aguirre was prohibited from possessing firearms and ammunition.

On August 13, 2025, law enforcement officers stopped Aguirre in Doña Ana County on an active arrest warrant. During a search of his vehicle, agents recovered approximately 57.4 grams of fentanyl from the center console and a loaded firearm.

Aguirre pleaded guilty to three counts of being a felon in possession of a firearm, possession with intent to distribute fentanyl, and using and carrying a firearm during and in relation to a drug trafficking crime. At sentencing, Aguirre faces not less than five years and up to a term of life in prison.

First Assistant U.S. Attorney Ryan Ellison and Special Agent in Charge Justin A. Garris of the Federal Bureau of Investigation’s Albuquerque Field Office made the announcement today.

The Las Cruces Resident Agency of the FBI’s Albuquerque Field Office investigated this case with assistance from the Doña Ana County Sheriff’s Office, the Las Cruces/Doña Ana Metro Narcotics and the Las Cruces Police Department. Assistant U.S. Attorney Devon Aragon Martinez is prosecuting the case.
title: Las Cruces Man Pleads Guilty to Fentanyl Trafficking and Firearm Offenses

U.S. Marshals Task Force Arrests Massachusetts Juvenile Fugitive Wanted for Double Murder in Boston
For immediate release
Dennis Matulewicz, Acting U.S. Marshal
BOSTON – The U.S. Marshals Service (USMS) District of Massachusetts today announced the arrest of a juvenile fugitive wanted on two counts of Murder in connection with a May 24, 2025, double homicide in Boston. The fugitive was apprehended without incident in Foxborough, Massachusetts, on Wednesday, November 4, 2026.
On May 24, 2025, at approximately 9:47 p.m., Boston Police officers responded to a shooting in the area of 38 Franklin Hill Avenue in Dorchester, Massachusetts. Upon arrival, officers discovered two male victims suffering from gunshot wounds. Both victims were transported to local hospitals, where one was pronounced deceased and the other subsequently succumbed to his injuries.
The victims were identified as Walter Wilkens, 36, of Quincy, Massachusetts, and Anthony McIntosh, 66, of Dorchester, Massachusetts.
On November 4, 2026, an arrest warrant was issued out of Suffolk Superior Court on two counts of Murder and one firearms-related charge in connection with the double homicide.
That same day, members of the USMS Massachusetts Fugitive Task Force (MAFTF), including personnel from the USMS District of Massachusetts, Boston Police Department Fugitive Unit, and Massachusetts State Police Violent Fugitive Apprehension Section, working collaboratively with the Foxborough Police Department, located and arrested the fugitive without incident in Foxborough, Massachusetts. The fugitive was subsequently transported to Boston.
The identity of the fugitive is being withheld due to the individual’s juvenile status.
“One of the greatest strengths of the U.S. Marshals Service is our extraordinary network of federal, state, and local law enforcement partnerships,” said Dennis Matulewicz, Attorney General-designated U.S. Marshal for the District of Massachusetts. “This arrest demonstrates the exceptional collaboration and unwavering commitment of our law enforcement partners to holding those accused of violent crimes accountable and protecting the communities we serve. While no arrest can undo the tragic loss of two lives, we hope today’s apprehension brings some measure of comfort to the victims’ families and moves them one step closer to justice.”
The USMS MAFTF works collaboratively with federal, state, and local law enforcement agencies throughout the Commonwealth to locate and apprehend fugitives wanted for violent crimes.
USMS MAFTF participants include the USMS District of Massachusetts, Massachusetts State Police, Boston Police, Brockton Police, Cambridge Police, Chicopee Police, Hampden County Sheriff’s Department, Haverhill Police, Lowell Police, Middlesex Sheriff’s Department, New Bedford Police, Plymouth County Sheriff's Department, Quincy Police, Randolph Police, Rochester Police, Springfield Police, Suffolk County Sheriff’s Department, West Springfield Police, Worcester Police, Massachusetts National Guard Counter Drug Program, Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms & Explosives, and the Drug Enforcement Administration.
The USMS reminds the public that criminal charges and allegations are accusations, and a defendant is presumed innocent unless and until proven guilty in a court of law.
If you have any information regarding the whereabouts of any state or federal fugitive, please contact the USMS at 1-877-WANTED2 or submit information via the USMS Tips App.
title: U.S. Marshals Task Force Arrests Massachusetts Juvenile Fugitive Wanted for Double Murder in Boston | U.S. Marshals Service

FORT STEWART, Ga.— Soldiers of the 2nd Armored Brigade Combat Team, 3rd Infantry Division, were honored Nov. 5 for their tremendous courage and decisive response to an active shooter incident at Fort Stewart last year.
Sgt. Aaron Turner and Sgt. Michael Boron, both assigned to the 703rd Brigade Support Battalion, 2nd ABCT, received the Army’s highest non-combat award – the Soldier’s Medal – presented by Acting Secretary of the Army Adam Telle and Gen. Christopher LaNeve, Vice Chief of Staff and Acting Chief of Staff of the Army.
The actions of these noncommissioned officers helped stop the threat, save lives and prevent further casualties, demonstrating the readiness, resilience and commitment to protecting fellow Soldiers that define the 3rd Infantry Division.
“When the shots rang out, these two sergeants didn’t hesitate,” Telle said in his remarks during the ceremony. “At extreme personal risk, they confronted, tackled, and restrained an active shooter. They absorbed the danger so their teammates wouldn’t have to. That level of courage cannot be taught in a classroom. It’s a testament to who they are as men, as soldiers, and as American heroes.”
Following the presentation of the Soldier’s Medal, Telle and LaNeve also awarded the Meritorious Service Medal to six other Soldiers for their actions in protecting and assisting members of the 703rd Brigade Support Battalion, 2nd ABCT, during the incident: Capt. Shailesh Nakarmi, 1st Lt. Kendarious Nixon, Sgt. 1st Class Luis Garza, Staff Sgt. Jalen Davis, Staff Sgt. Raudy Javier and Spc. Gavin Brebnor. The Army's subsequent recognition of additional Soldiers following the conclusion of the court martial further highlights the courage and professionalism demonstrated by members of the unit.
“These Soldiers embodied the warrior mindset. Faced with immediate danger, they neutralized the threat and protected their team,” said LaNeve. “Their courage and resolve represent the very best of what it means to be an American Soldier.”
The ceremony, held at Fort Stewart, hosted more than 500 personnel from across the division, demonstrating the formation’s collective support for the Soldiers being recognized and the lasting impact of their actions. The presence of leaders, fellow Soldiers and members of the division underscored the importance of standing together, honoring courage and recognizing those who put the safety of others first.
Maj. Gen. John Lubas, commanding general of 3rd Infantry Division, emphasized the importance of the Soldiers' immediate response and their efforts to provide medical aid.
“I'm incredibly proud of the Soldiers and how they reacted on the sixth, the actions they took directly saved the lives of their fellow Soldiers; it's an important day for the division,” said Maj. Gen. Lubas. “What we saw with the Soldiers we're recognizing today, everybody did what they've been trained to do - they reacted to the threat, and then they cared for their fellow Soldiers.”
The shooting occurred when an assailant opened fire on fellow Soldiers in the 2nd ABCT complex. Five Soldiers were wounded during the incident, prompting an installation lockdown and an immediate response from Soldiers and emergency personnel from across the region. When gunfire erupted in the 2nd ABCT complex, Soldiers immediately responded to protect those around them. Turner and Boron helped restrain the shooter, while other Soldiers moved to provide immediate medical aid to the wounded, demonstrating the importance of training, discipline and decisive action under pressure.
“You are a Soldier every day, not just when you are deployed,” said Boron. “We must all be prepared to protect our brothers and sisters in harm’s way during war and peacetime.”
This ceremony highlights the importance of recognizing the Soldiers whose actions made a lasting difference, honoring their courage and ensuring their contributions are remembered by the formation.
“Throughout our lives, we will all face adversity and danger, especially as Soldiers,” said Turner. “We must always remember that our service to our country, and to our team, comes before ourselves.”
The presentation honored the Soldiers’ actions during an exceptionally dangerous situation and reinforced the Army's commitment to recognizing those who demonstrate heroism in the face of a threat.
The Marne Division's response to the incident also reflects its continued commitment to caring for its people. The effects of a traumatic event extend beyond the immediate response, requiring continued support for wounded Soldiers, their families and the broader formation.
The actions of the Soldiers involved in the Aug. 6, 2025, incident serve as a reminder that readiness is more than preparation for a mission, it is the ability to act decisively, protect others and remain committed to the Army values when confronted with unexpected challenges.
This ceremony brings closure to 2nd ABCT, 3rd Infantry Division, as the unit recognizes the courage, professionalism and selfless actions of its Soldiers during the Aug. 6, 2025, Fort Stewart shooting. It serves as a reminder of the strength of the formation, the importance of readiness and the enduring commitment to protecting one another.
title: 3rd ID Soldiers receive the Soldier’s Medal

KANSAS CITY, KAN. – A Missouri man was sentenced to seven years in prison for using the internet to arrange a sexual encounter with a minor without realizing he was actually communicating with an undercover Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) agent.

According to court documents, James D. Fishbaugh, 53, of Blue Springs, Missouri, pleaded guilty to one count of travel with intent to engage in illicit sexual conduct.

In August 2025, Fishbaugh used a social media account to chat with an undercover FBI posing online as a minor living in Kansas. When the agent purported to be a 14-year-old girl, Fishbaugh responded by claiming he was 49. Fishbaugh then shifted the conversation to be sexual in nature. He asked “the girl” if she was a virgin and if she was “kinky.”

Fishbaugh drove from his home in Missouri to a designated meeting place in Kansas, where agents arrested him and found condoms on his person. Fishbaugh told officers that he believed he was talking to a 14-year-old girl and that he traveled to the residence to have sex with the minor.

“Protecting children from sexual exploitation remains one of our highest priorities,” said U.S. Attorney Ryan A. Kriegshauser. “The defendant continued pursuing what he believed was a sexual encounter with a 14-year-old child and took substantial steps to carry out that encounter. Thanks to the FBI’s proactive investigative work, he was stopped before any child could be victimized. Our office will continue working with our law enforcement partners to identify, investigate, and prosecute those who seek to exploit children.”

“Cases like this reinforce the seriousness of the threat these dangerous predators pose to our children. The FBI along with our law enforcement partners continue to put a focus on these cases by identifying victims and holding predators accountable,” said Chris Ormerod, FBI Kansas City Special Agent in Charge.

The Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) investigated the case.

Assistant U.S. Attorney Audrey McCormick prosecuted the case.

Project Safe Childhood This case was brought as part of Project Safe Childhood, a nationwide initiative to combat the growing epidemic of child sexual exploitation and abuse launched in May 2006 by the Department of Justice. Led by U.S. Attorneys’ Offices and CEOS, Project Safe Childhood marshals federal, state, and local resources to better locate, apprehend, and prosecute individuals who exploit children via the Internet, as well as to identify and rescue victims. For more information about Project Safe Childhood, please visit https://www.justice.gov/psc .

title: Missouri man sentenced for sexual meetup with FBI agent posing online as teen

Fast Facts
Almost half of District of Columbia students were enrolled in charter schools during school year 2025–26.
In the past 5 years, the charter school board has made changes to the application process for these schools. For example, new charters must fill an unmet community need and complete a preapplication process. Additionally, the board introduced a new academic accountability system to monitor charter schools.
This report describes:
- The board's oversight of charter schools within the past 5 years
- Changes to its accountability system, revenue, and expenditures
- How it complied with its own annual reporting requirements
A stack of books with a graduation hat on top.
Highlights
What GAO Found
The DC Public Charter School Board (PCSB) uses a multi-step process, including interviews and public hearings, to screen applicants. PCSB also requires applicants to meet several decision criteria (see figure). In the past 5 years PCSB has made a few key changes to the charter school application process. Changes include requiring that charters fill a demonstrated need and that prospective schools complete a preapplication process. Additionally, PCSB has shifted the application timeline to the fall from the spring.
DC Public Charter School Board (PCSB) Application Decision Criteria
Note: For more details, see figure 1 in GAO-27-109048
In the last 5 years, two schools applied for new charters and PCSB denied both. By comparison, in the previous 5 years (2016–2021), PCSB received 30 applications and approved 11. PCSB officials attributed the reduced number of applications to the more rigorous application process. For the 2026 application cycle, PCSB did not receive any applications.
PCSB uses several mechanisms to monitor charter schools’ academic performance and compliance with applicable legal requirements. In 2024 PCSB introduced the Annual School Performance Index Report and Evaluation (ASPIRE) system, which is intended to improve accountability for schools’ success and student development. PCSB also uses ASPIRE to determine which schools need additional monitoring or support. While the ASPIRE system has similar measures to PCSB’s previous system, ASPIRE emphasizes school performance. ASPIRE calculates performance measures by student groups, such as students with disabilities or multilingual learners, rather than for all students combined.
Why GAO Did This Study
Almost one-half of DC’s public-school students were enrolled in 133 charter schools during school year 2025–26. The District of Columbia, School Reform Act of 1995, as amended, requires PCSB—DC’s sole chartering authority—to review and approve charter applications, monitor schools, and submit annual reports on its work.
The District of Columbia Appropriations Act of 2005, as amended, included a provision for GAO to review DC’s chartering authorities every 5 years. This report describes changes in the 5 years since our last report (2016–2021) in how PCSB reviews applications, monitors charter schools and takes corrective actions, and how PCSB complies with its annual reporting requirements, among other objectives.
GAO reviewed PCSB policies and procedures, including the 2026 Charter Application Guidelines, Charter Review and Charter Renewal guidelines, and policy documents related to PCSB’s new accountability system. GAO also compared PCSB’s 2026 Annual Report to School Reform Act requirements and interviewed PCSB’s board chair and staff.
For more information, contact Jacqueline M. Nowicki at NowickiJ@gao.gov.
title: District of Columbia Charter Schools: Key Changes Made to Academic Accountability System

Congresswoman Dina Titus sent a letter to House Republican leadership today urging it to include in “must-pass” legislation her measure to restore the 100 percent gambling loss deduction when the House reconvenes next week. 
“Enactment of this bipartisan provision would correct an unfair change in the tax code and provide needed certainty to taxpayers, businesses, and regulated gaming markets across the country,” Congresswoman Titus wrote in the letter to House Speaker Mike Johnson and Majority Leader Steve Scalise. 
A provision added to the Senate-amended version of the One Big Beautiful Bill Act passed by Congress last year reduced the gambling loss deduction from 100 to 90 percent. In effect, the change requires gambler to pay taxes on money they did not earn. On July 7, 2025, Congresswoman Titus introduced the FAIR BET Act, H.R.4304, to reverse the change. The legislation passed out of the House Ways and Means Committee by a vote of 38-5 in September and is awaiting action by House leadership to bring it to a floor vote. 
“As Congress returns from recess and turns to end-of-year legislation, I respectfully urge Leadership to expeditiously bring a gambling loss deduction fix to the House floor and include it in a must-pass legislative vehicle,” Congresswoman Titus said. 
She said the 90 percent deduction “unfairly burdens professional gamblers and casual players alike and will inevitably drive players toward offshore and unregulated markets where consumer protections are nonexistent, thereby undermining responsible gaming efforts nationwide. This will further reduce tax revenue and stifle investment by the industry here at home, costing jobs and impacting ancillary businesses.”
title: Rep. Dina Titus Asks Republican Leadership to Fast-Track FAIR BET Act

EL PASO, Texas – A felon from New Mexico was sentenced in a federal court in El Paso to 180 months in prison for stealing and transporting firearms, announced U.S. Attorney Justin R. Simmons for the Western District of Texas.

According to court documents, on Jan. 9, Shawn Cole Camu, 38, of Alamogordo, stole two firearms from a Federal Firearms Licensee located in El Paso. He then transported the stolen firearms to his home in Alamogordo, where he intended to sell them for drug money. Camu is a convicted felon with seven prior felony convictions in Colorado and New Mexico, including residential burglary, armed burglary, robbery, and assault.

Camu was arrested on Jan. 10 and indicted in February for one count of theft of a firearm from a federal firearm licensee, one count of possession of a firearm by a prohibited person, and one count of transportation of a stolen firearm. He pleaded guilty to all three counts on Aug. 11. On Wednesday, U.S. District Judge Kathleen Cardone sentenced Camu to the statutory maximum for each charge.

The Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives, El Paso Police Department, and Alamogordo Police Department investigated the case.

Assistant U.S. Attorney Scott Wisniewski prosecuted the case.

###
title: New Mexico Felon Sentenced to Federal Prison for Stealing Firearms in El Paso

text: St. Thomas, USVI – U.S. Attorney Adam F. Sleeper announced today that a federal jury convicted Joan Manuel Tavarez Bueno, 34, of the Dominican Republic, for re-entry of a removed alien pursuant to 8 U.S.C. § 1326(a). After a three-day trial, the defendant was convicted as charged. The defendant faces a statutory sentence of up to 24 months imprisonment. The Chief District Court Judge, Robert A. Molloy, will schedule a sentencing hearing to determine the sentence to be imposed. According to court documents and testimony presented at trial, on March 10, 2025, the defendant was a passenger in a vehicle that was stopped by Homeland Security Investigations (HSI) Special Agents during the course of an immigration investigation near Red Hook, St. Thomas. The defendant, a citizen of the Dominican Republic, was previously removed from the United States as an illegal alien from Miami, FL, on February 13, 2024. He then illegally re-entered the United States through St. John in November 2024 without first obtaining permission from the Secretary of Homeland Security. This case was investigated by HSI with the assistance of Immigration and Customs Enforcement. It was prosecuted by Assistant United States Attorneys, Erik C. Tate, Kimberly Riley, and Criminal Chief Kyle Payne.
title: Federal Jury Convicts Dominican Republic Man of Illegally Reentering the United States after having been Deported

Press Statement

Thomas "Tommy" Pigott, Spokesman Office of the Spokesman

November 5, 2026

Today, the United States is sanctioning four individuals and 41 entities linked to the Cambodia-based Prince Group Transnational Criminal Organization (TCO), building on the October 2025 and June 2026 designations targeting the organization’s leadership, affiliated companies, and financial facilitators. These sanctions are being implemented by the U.S. Department of the Treasury’s Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC).

Prince Group TCO members target victims in the United States and around the world through sophisticated cyber-enabled fraud schemes, many of which are carried out from large-scale scam compounds in Southeast Asia. Today’s designations target several individuals and affiliated companies who continue to provide material support to the Prince Group TCO.

Additionally, the United States is sanctioning Chui Kok Wa, a Malaysian individual who defrauded U.S. victims by managing a network of scammers located in Madagascar. This network perpetrated scams targeting Americans, including schemes to defraud them of digital assets. On October 27, 2026, charges were unsealed in the U.S. District Court for the District of Columbia charging Chui with conspiracy to commit wire fraud.

No criminal network is beyond reach. The Trump Administration will continue to expose, sanction, and dismantle the criminal networks that prey on Americans through cybercrime, fraud, and extortion.

Today’s actions were taken in furtherance of Executive Order (E.O.) 14390 “Combating Cybercrime, Fraud, and Predatory Schemes Against American Citizens” and pursuant to E.O. 13581 “Blocking Property of Transnational Criminal Organizations,” as amended by E.O. 13863, and E.O. 13694 “Blocking the Property of Certain Persons Engaging in Significant Malicious Cyber-Enabled Activities,” as further amended.

For more information about today’s actions, please see the Department of the Treasury’s press release .

A man who received and possessed child pornography was sentenced today to more than six years in federal prison.

Isiah Michael Morse, age 23, from Tripoli, Iowa, received the prison term after an April 17, 2026, guilty plea to one count of receipt of child pornography and one count of possession of child pornography.

Evidence at a prior hearing and at sentencing showed that in January 2024, law enforcement officers searched Morse’s person and seized a phone. On the phone were images and videos of child pornography, including of prepubescent children. Morse had paid for child pornography on at least two occasions. In an interview with officers, Morse admitted that he had downloaded child pornography and then moved it to a “hidden folder” on his phone. Morse had downloaded the child pornography as early as November 2021.

Morse was sentenced in Cedar Rapids by United States District Court Chief Judge C.J. Williams. Morse was sentenced to 78 months’ imprisonment and was ordered to make $12,000 in restitution to victims. He must also serve a five-year term of supervised release after the prison term. There is no parole in the federal system.

This case was brought as part of Project Safe Childhood, a nationwide initiative launched in May 2006 by the Department of Justice to combat the growing epidemic of child sexual exploitation and abuse. Led by the United States Attorneys’ Offices and the Criminal Division’s Child Exploitation and Obscenity Section, Project Safe Childhood marshals federal, state, and local resources to locate, apprehend, and prosecute individuals who sexually exploit children, and to identify and rescue victims. For more information about Project Safe Childhood, please visit www.usdoj.gov/psc . For more information about Internet safety education, please visit www.usdoj.gov/psc and click on the tab “resources.”

Morse is being held in the United States Marshal’s custody until he can be transported to a federal prison.

The case was prosecuted by Assistant United States Attorney Devra T. Hake and investigated by the Iowa Division of Criminal Investigation, the Federal Bureau of Investigation, the Johnson County Joint Forensic Analysis Cyber Team, and the Bremer County Sheriff’s Office.

Court file information at https://ecf.iand.uscourts.gov/cgi-bin/login.pl .

The case file number is 25-CR-2036. Follow us on X @USAO_NDIA.

United States Attorney for the Southern District of New York, Jamie McDonald, and Assistant Director in Charge of the New York Field Office of the Federal Bureau of Investigation (“FBI”), James C. Barnacle, Jr., announced today the unsealing of an Indictment charging JACOB SOALL, a/k/a “Seba Clarke,” a/k/a “Rocky Balboa,” SHARON HAZAN, a/k/a “Superman Cash,” a/k/a “Impossible Mission,” a/k/a “Fat Boy,” a/k/a “Ron,” and GUY SHEETRIT for their participation in a scheme to use super intelligence (“SI”) to defraud victim companies all over the world of more than $100 million. SOALL was arrested in Spain on June 17, 2026, HAZAN was arrested in Spain on August 5, 2026, and SHEETRIT was arrested in the United Kingdom on September 7, 2026. Extradition requests for SOALL, HAZAN, and SHEETRIT are pending.

“SI technology offers tremendous potential. But the public should recognize that there are some who seek to use this emerging technology to pursue criminal goals,” said U.S. Attorney Jamie McDonald. “As alleged, Jacob Soall, Sharon Hazan, and Guy Sheetrit abused groundbreaking super intelligence technology to impersonate real people and deceive corporate executives into sending them and their co-conspirators approximately $129 million. I encourage individuals and the business community to consider how to best protect themselves from the emerging threat of SI-enabled crime. This Office and our law enforcement partners will do our part and continue to identify, investigate, and prosecute criminals, including those who use new technologies to defraud Americans.”

I encourage individuals and the business community to consider how to best protect themselves from the emerging threat of SI-enabled crime. This Office and our law enforcement partners will do our part and continue to identify, investigate, and prosecute criminals, including those who use new technologies to defraud Americans.”

“The alleged scheme orchestrated by Soall, Hazan, and Sheetrit demonstrates how the use of advanced technology can be exploited to commit large scale fraud,” said FBI Assistant Director in Charge James C. Barnacle, Jr. “As criminals continue to weaponize emerging technologies, the FBI remains committed to rapidly adapting our capabilities to identify, investigate, and disrupt those who seek to harm New Yorkers and businesses operating in our communities.”

According to the Indictment:(1)

Between 2024 and 2026, SOALL, HAZAN, SHEETRIT, and their co-conspirators used SI to impersonate the voices and/or images of corporate executives at numerous companies (the “Victim Companies”) and attorneys at major law firms in order to trick employees into sending large payments to bank accounts all over the world controlled by members of the conspiracy.

SOALL, HAZAN, SHEETRIT, and their co-conspirators typically began their fraud scheme by targeting employees at Victim Companies and pretending to be the Chief Executive Officers at the Victim Companies. They would explain that they needed an employee’s assistance on a confidential financial transaction and would use SI to mimic the CEO’s voice and/or image in calls with the employee. While pretending to be the CEO, they would direct the employee to get in touch with lawyers at large international law firms who they said were also working on the sham financial transaction. They would then also impersonate those lawyers to further make the employee believe that the financial transaction was real. A member of the conspiracy, impersonating one of those lawyers, would ultimately direct the employee to wire a large sum of money in furtherance of that sham financial transaction to a particular bank account, which was in fact controlled by members of the conspiracy.

The fraud scheme ultimately stole more than $129 million from Victim Companies all over the United States and the world, including: (i) $4,829,580 from a hospital system headquartered in Missouri; (ii) $2,684,580 from a bank headquartered in Rhode Island; (iii) $2,968,497 from a hospital system headquartered in California; (iv) $11,578,474 from a financial technology company headquartered in the United Kingdom; (v) $4,639,918 from a mutual fund company headquartered in Massachusetts; and (vi) $5,242,747 from a pet food company headquartered in Florida.

SOALL, HAZAN, SHEETRIT, and their co-conspirators directed that the Victim Companies wire money to bank accounts controlled by conspirators all over the world, including in the United States, Spain, Portugal, Greece, the United Arab Emirates, Singapore, Austria, Slovakia, and China. Once a Victim Company’s money had been wired, SOALL, HAZAN, SHEETRIT and their co-conspirators converted it into cryptocurrency in an attempt to conceal the source, ownership, and control of the stolen proceeds and distributed it amongst themselves and their co-conspirators.

SOALL primarily acted to impersonate attorneys from the United Kingdom in furtherance of the fraud scheme. SOALL kept a handwritten script titled “Lawyer Call” that he utilized to make himself seem like a real attorney when speaking with and defrauding victims. That script included, for example, language designed to convince victim employees not to discuss their communications with fellow employees.

HAZAN, among other things, laundered funds from the fraud scheme. As to money laundering generally, HAZAN boasted that he had been laundering money since 1994; that he had laundered over $400 million in just the past three years; and that, among professional money launderers, he was “number one all over the world.” SHEETRIT also, among other things, laundered funds from the fraud scheme.

If you believe you may be a victim of the conduct described in this press release or know of information regarding its perpetrators, please use the online tips page: https://tips.fbi.gov .

text:
FORT LEAVENWORTH, Kansas (October 2026) — Established in 1827 by Col. Henry Leavenworth, Fort Leavenworth is the U.S. Army’s oldest continuously operating base west of the Mississippi River. Next year marks the 200th year of its operation. The military history that’s been made on the post can be seen in its remarkable collection of historic buildings and enduring traditions.
Tales told to whomever might listen about unexplained encounters and spooky legends has become one of those enduring traditions.
For Megan Hunter, museum specialist and current interim director of the Frontier Army Museum on Fort Leavenworth, the appeal of those stories goes beyond the supernatural.
“The allure of ghost stories helps to keep historical places like Fort Leavenworth alive,” Hunter said.
The Rookery
Many of the historic homes that remain on the post offer the most intriguing examples of ghost sightings or other uncanny, unexplained events over the centuries. One place in particular is the Rookery at 14 Sumner Place.
Construction was completed in 1834, making the building the oldest surviving structure at Fort Leavenworth and the oldest continuously occupied residence in Kansas. Over the years, it housed commanding officers and bachelor officers, including Col. Henry Dodge and, later, Lt. Douglas MacArthur.
Today, the Rookery is better known for the residents who supposedly never left. Heralded as the most haunted place on Fort Leavenworth, it’s known for numerous accounts of paranormal activity by former residents who reported seeing a shadowy “Lady in White".
Her trademark, according to the lore, is a long white gown, unkempt scraggly hair and long fingernails as she flies aimlessly through the home.
Hunter recalled a story she heard from a family who lived there in 2009.
“They've had so many occurrences they can't even remember them all,” she said. “Sounds of a door opening and footsteps going up the stairs, sounds of furniture moving across the floor upstairs, doors that are locked open by themselves and lights that turn on by themselves.”
The stories became particularly memorable for Hunter during a Halloween trick-or-treating visit with her children. While talking with a resident of the Rookery, she recalled the person lowering her voice before discussing the eerie activity she experienced while living there.
“I don’t want the spirits to hear me,” the resident told her.
Although Hunter said she has never witnessed a ghost herself, an experience at Andrews Hall, home to the post’s Frontier Army Museum, left her with questions. One time while standing near the director’s office, she thought she heard a little girl whisper close to her ear. She said the director, sitting only about eight feet away, responded without prompting.
“Oh, I heard her, too. It’s the little girl that’s around here,” the director said.
But Hunter said her creepiest experience was the moment she ended up opening the museum alone on a Saturday morning.
“I arrived at the museum before opening hours and heard what sounded like footsteps followed by whistling near the director’s office. The building was locked, so there were no visitors or volunteers in the building.”
The military history museum is home to nearly 6,500 artifacts, with several being haunting in nature, such as Army surgeon instruments circa 1845, U.S. Disciplinary Barracks prisoner hand cuffs and leg shackles circa 1871, and the rope used in the last Army military execution in 1961.
Longtime civilian employees often have stories of their own, Hunter said, when thinking about the collection of ghostly stories she has been told personally or others that have passed between generations of people who have called the post home whether they lived or worked there.
One such longtime Fort Leavenworth employee is Mark Martinez, office engineer for the Kansas City District, U.S. Army Corps of Engineers residence office on the post. During his decades working on the installation, Martinez described strange occurrences at the historic Military Prison Cemetery around the gravesites of 14 former German prisoners of war, who’ve been buried there since their executions in 1945 after World War II for slaying other German POWs who were captured with them.
“Every year around June and July, flowers mysteriously appear on their graves,” he said. “For a long time, we thought it was a German woman in town that was responsible for placing. But it continued after she died several years ago, and we still have no idea who is responsible for it.”
The Syracuse House
Other historic homes scattered around Fort Leavenworth have their own legends as well.
The Syracuse House at 4 Sumner Place is supposedly haunted by a mystical “Lady in Black.” Hunter recalled a story she had been told about a military family who lived there in 1975 and what happened when movers were relocating their household items to their next duty station.
“He reportedly encountered a woman dressed in an old-fashioned black gown and bonnet who walked right past him and entered another room upstairs,” Hunter said. “He reportedly tried to follow the ghost into the next room, and she disappeared.”
According to the lore, when he was shown historical photographs by the wife of the officer who resided there with the rest of his family, he reportedly pointed to a picture of Libbie Custer and declared, “That’s her!”
The story carries an unusual historical connection to the post because Lt. Col. George Armstrong Custer — brother of Capt. Thomas Custer and infamous Civil War brigadier general who was eventually killed at the Battle of Little Big Horn in 1876 — was stationed at Fort Leavenworth and lived in the building during his 1867 court-martial.
Fort Leavenworth National Cemetery
Not every haunted tale on the iconic installation is centered around an old rustic house. One enduring folk tale tells the story of Catherine, whose spirit has been reportedly spotted wandering around the Fort Leavenworth National Cemetery no matter the season.
According to the tale Hunter retold, Catherine stayed at Fort Leavenworth in the 1880s while traveling west with her husband Hiram and children, Mary and Ethan. While there visiting family, her children mysteriously disappeared near the bluffs of the Missouri River while gathering firewood, which flows directly alongside the post.
“As the legend goes, Catherine searched for them tirelessly during the day and with a lantern at night for months,” she said. “But while out searching during the winter, she became ill with pneumonia and died.”
Hiram, devastated by the tragedy of losing his entire family, returned home to Indiana. But later in the spring, he learned they had survived their fall into the river and been rescued downstream by members of the Fox Indian tribe who were travelling through the area at the time.
Whether these stories describe supernatural encounters, misinterpreted sounds or the power of imagination, they offer a different way to explore Fort Leavenworth’s iconic military history and America’s frontier past.
Many of the post's buildings that have survived for decades and centuries and the actual grounds of the post itself have witnessed generations of soldiers, families, celebrations, tragedies and much change. The legends give those events a human dimension, inviting visitors to imagine the lives once lived behind the old brick masonry and wood walls.
As the seasons change and leaves turn red and orange while the crisp autumn air settles over Main Parade, it is easy to understand why the stories endure.
“You can’t help but think of spooky season,” Hunter said of fall at Fort Leavenworth.
And for those willing to listen closely, the post’s history might have a few more stories left to tell.
“Everyone loves a good ghost story. I hope that the interest in Fort Leavenworth ghost stories will encourage people to come and visit the post,” Hunter said. “In addition to the fun supernatural sightings, the post is filled with wonderful history that we want to share.”
title: Frontier Army Museum houses artifacts related to post’s ghost stories, tales of strange happenings continue to be told

text:
Massachusetts Congresswoman Katherine Clark is set to make history as the first woman to become a majority leader in Congress, the leader of the House Democrats said Wednesday.
Rep. Hakeem Jeffries, widely expected to be elected the next speaker of the House after Democrats won big in the 2026 midterm elections, introduced Clark at a news conference as “the next majority leader of the House of Representatives” and “someone who will be the first woman to ever serve in that position in our 250-year journey.”
Clark, the current House minority whip who lives in Revere, was elected to Congress in 2013 to replace now-Sen. Ed Markey. The 63-year-old said she was proud to “make history” as part of the new majority.
“In the words of the great Dolly Parton, it’s been a long hard fight, but I see a brand new day a-dawning,” Clark said.
Clark has been outspoken about childcare issues, introducing the Babies Act in 2022 to support new mothers with more access to birth centers and midwives. She also bashed President Trump’s “One Big Beautiful Bill” last year, calling it “incredibly cruel” for making cuts to Medicaid and food stamps.
Clark still needs to be elected by her House colleagues to become majority leader in the new Congress. She said Wednesday that Americans are trusting her party to do more than just “damage control” on the Trump administration.
“They have entrusted a Democratic Congress to lead us forward to something better, to make their lives easier,” she said.
Clark on Thursday officially declared her intent to run for majority leader in a letter to other Democratic representatives.
“My priority will be ensuring that every corner of our Caucus is heard and empowered to have a role in the policymaking process,” Clark wrote. “At every decision point, I intend to work closely with you to understand the needs of your district and maximize your ability to deliver for your constituents.”
Steve Kerrigan, chair of the Massachusetts Democratic Party, has known Clark since she first ran to be on the Melrose School Committee back in 2001.
“It’s huge. The last time we’ve had someone at that height in House leadership was Tip O’Neill and that was decades ago,” Kerrigan said. “I am excited for the world to get to know the really incredibly special person she is and the great leader that she is.”
WBZ-TV political analyst Jon Keller said Clark as majority leader could mean millions of dollars in funding for Massachusetts.
“That’s an area where during the last two years of the Trump administration we have really been hurt by cuts and federal research grants and other funding sources,” Keller said.
Congresswoman Clark’s office did not return WBZ’s request for an interview.

title: CBS: Katherine Clark of Massachusetts will be first woman to serve as House majority leader, Hakeem Jeffries says

A Soldier and two civilians and their families were honored Oct. 29 at the Redstone Arsenal quarterly retirement ceremony in Bob Jones Auditorium.
The honorees included Lt. Col. Chas Caruana, 37 years of service; Bill Edmonds, 35 years; and Edwin Lopez Laviena, 40 years.
“Thank you for everything that you have done for Redstone, this nation and for our Army,” Brig. Gen. Gail Atkins, the ceremony’s host and special assistant to the acting commanding general of Army Materiel Command, said.
Caruana retired as chief of operations for Intelligence-Future Capability Directorate under the Futures and Concepts Command. His career began with six years in the Marine Corps and then 31 years with the Army National Guard from Michigan.
“It’s time to do something different,” Caruana, 56, of Union Grove, said. “I’m getting back into law enforcement.”
He was a police officer in the Marine City, Michigan, police department from 2015-22. Caruana plans to go up to Michigan to be a police officer for a while until returning to Alabama to join the Alabama Law Enforcement Agency when the academy starts.
Edmonds retired as senior safety engineer for the Army Materiel Command.
“I’m looking forward to traveling and my fiancee (Karen) and I being married and starting life together, and mentoring other engineers,” Edmonds said.
Lopez Laviena retired from the Logistics Readiness Center as ammunition branch chief and ammunition accountability officer. His 40-year career included 20 years as a Soldier and 20 years as a civilian. He retired from the military in 2006 as a chief warrant officer two.
“It’s the best thing I’ve ever done,” Lopez Laviena, a Puerto Rico native, said. “I joined the Army with the intention of learning English, and I finished with 40 years of service. When I joined the Army, I didn’t know what ammunition was and I ended up doing 40 years with ammunition. And now I am the chief of ammunition.”
title: Quarterly retirement ceremony honors three careerists, families

text:
ANSBACH, Germany — Bad weather during fall and winter months in Ansbach and Illesheim can affect your decision to travel. Garrison officials and street cleaning crews at U.S. Army Garrison Ansbach installations will do what they can to keep services running. Snow and ice, however, may result in changes to road conditions and Garrison delays, closures or early releases.
What to do
Be in the know. Here’s how:
- Register in Alert! today. Ensure you and your family receive Army Alert messages before bad weather hits. Alert is the U.S. Army’s mass warning notification system. The system notifies users in several ways: as a pop-up on their workstation computer, an email to work and home addresses, a text message to their cell phone, and a voicemail to their work, home and cell phones. Add up to 10 phone numbers and email addresses. Parents with students at Ansbach Elementary School and Ansbach Middle High School can enroll in Everbridge — DoDEA Europe’s mass notification system — and will be notified when schools are impacted by weather.
- Connect to USAG Ansbach on Facebook: www.facebook.com/USAGAnsbachCommunity. We’ll post the most up-to-date information pertaining to weather updates, delays, closures, early releases and driving conditions at Ansbach and Illesheim. We also use Facebook to provide more details to corresponding Alert notifications.
- Stay connected to the Ansbach website at https://home.army.mil/ansbach. Click the “Road Conditions” image for the latest driving, road and weather conditions.
- Tune into AFN Bavaria radio at 107.3 FM in Ansbach and 104.9 FM in Illesheim. Or, listen to AFN Go online or through the mobile app. Radio DJs provide updates on conditions in Ansbach and Illesheim.
- If you are a Soldier and are still unsure, call your staff duty officer for further guidance.
How USAG Ansbach responds to bad weather
The USAG Ansbach Garrison Commander determines work delays, closures and early releases. This information is routed to the garrison’s Directorate of Plans, Training, Mobilization and Security (DPTMS) and Public Affairs Office for dissemination and made available to the public. So register in Alert and stay connected to the garrison’s website, Facebook page or tune into AFN Bavaria (Ansbach - 107.3 FM, Illesheim - 98.5 FM) before leaving your house. Use good judgment and err on the side of safety.
When conditions warrant, the Garrison Commander may direct delayed reporting, closures or an early release at USAG Ansbach. These decisions — based on a combination of driving and weather conditions — apply to all personnel, mission partners, directorates, agencies and DoDEA-Europe schools.
The announcement of delayed reporting or garrison closure will be made by 5 a.m. An Alert message is sent to registered users. Garrison staff update the Weather & Roads webpage and weather hotline, as well as notify AFN broadcasters, who then broadcast updates.
Delays, Closures & Early Releases
The purpose of a Garrison delay is to give the Directorate of Public Works time to clear roads and parking lots. Primary roads are cleared first, followed by secondary and tertiary roads.
During a delay, garrison services come back online at 10 a.m., unless otherwise notified. Expect garrison front-door services such as the Vehicle Registration Office (VRO) to open no earlier than 10 a.m. Appointments — such as those scheduled at the passport office — may be postponed. When in doubt, always call ahead: home.army.mil/ansbach/contact/garrison-phonebook.
When a delay is announced, mission essential services like the fire department, military police and dining facilities (DFACs) remain open. Child & Youth Services (CYS) — which include the Child Development Center and School-Age Center — will typically open at 9:30 a.m., or 30 minutes prior to when garrison services return. Parents should update their emergency contact information and Family Care Plan with CYS before bad weather hits.
During a delay, school buses will pick up children from their bus stops two hours after their normal pickup time. For example, if the bus at Urlas Kaserne normally picks up students at 7:45 a.m., expect the bus to arrive at 9:45 a.m. for a 10 a.m. arrival at school. Parents of students at DoDEA schools can expect updates via the schools’ mass notification system, Everbridge.
When inclement weather results in closures, expect garrison services to close, including all CYS facilities. Mission essential services remain open.
The garrison commander may call an early release when bad weather approaches. During an early release, schools and garrison services close early. Parents must pick up their children from CYS facilities within two hours. After-school activities and garrison evening events will be postponed or canceled.
The garrison command team make every effort based on available data to announce an early release two hours prior to the forecasted degradation of road conditions. This allows for DoDEA school officials to stage school buses and prepare students and parents.
The garrison shuttle will not run during red or black road conditions.
During inclement weather, DeCA and AAFES facilities will operate on a case-by-case basis. This includes the commissary, Main Exchange, Express and fuel stations.
Patients whose appointments at the Health Clinic and Dental Clinic are impacted by delays, closures or early releases, will be contacted by the clinic to reschedule. A common misconception is that during delays, an appointment gets pushed until the clinic opens. This is incorrect. Rather, appointments will be rescheduled. The U.S. Army Health Clinic Ansbach Facebook page provides timely information when bad weather hits. Visit www.facebook.com/AnsbachClinic.
Driving Conditions vs. Road Conditions
Army in Europe and Africa Regulation 385-10, Safety and Occupational Health Program Management, states that garrison commanders set road conditions.
Road conditions are set at green, amber, red or black. These levels only pertain to conditions for dispatching military tactical and non-tactical vehicles. All DOD sedans, station wagons, carryalls, vans, buses and public works vehicles are considered “non-tactical.”
The garrison shuttle will not run during red or black road conditions.
Contrary to popular belief, the road conditions do not dictate whether you as a Soldier, civilian or student should come to work or school, though they can inform your own decision-making. Use good judgement and err on the side of safety.
Road conditions are set based on the most deteriorated spots. Military police patrols may classify amber road conditions at Katterbach Kaserne, for example, but red on the hill adjacent to Marktbergel on B13. In this instance, road conditions would be set at red.
If you have concerns but no garrison-wide delay or closure has been announced, contact your staff duty officer or supervisor. Commanders and supervisors are empowered to decide whether individuals can delay reporting.
Weather Advisory, Watch & Warning
The primary mission of the U.S. Air Force’s 7th Weather Squadron stationed in Grafenwoehr is to support air operations. But they also provide weather updates to USAG Ansbach. Here’s the 7th Weather Squadron terminology you need to know:
- Advisory: Issued when ice or snow is expected to cause a significant inconvenience, but not serious enough to warrant a warning.
- Watch: Issued when there is a potential for hazardous weather within 48 hours.
- Warning: Issued when a significant combination of hazardous winter weather is occurring or imminent.
How community members can prepare
You are required by German law to remove as much snow and ice from your vehicle as possible, particularly from windows, mirrors and headlights. Make sure you have maximum visibility — no peephole driving — and that your vehicle does not present a hazard to other drivers.
If accumulation is heavy, also remove snow from the roof, trunk and hood so that large chunks do not fly off towards other drivers. Don’t forget your headlights. Police can stop you and impose fines if your vehicle is determined unsafe to you or others.
Off-post residents are responsible for snow and ice removal in their driveways and on public sidewalks bordering their home.
Permitted de-icing products are available at USAG Ansbach Self-Help and AAFES locations, as well as off-post hardware stores. The USAG Ansbach Self-Help Store is located at Katterbach Kaserne, Bldg. 5516, near the fire station. For more, call CIV 09641-70587-1796, DSN 587-1796.
Remember: You are responsible for your own safety. Drive with caution, allow extra time for your morning commute, and be mindful of slippery sidewalks. Take steps to stay warm and safe and make sure pets are sheltered from the cold.
How USAG Ansbach employees can prepare
Supervisors and managers stationed at USAG Ansbach should take precautionary measures in preparation for inclement weather. Ensure the safety of your people while sustaining operations and garrison services. Leadership can ensure staff complete winter driving safety training, update recall rosters, and establish situational telework agreements.
Telework agreements are typically approved for employees not associated with front-door services. Interested employees should contact their supervisors.
Employees eligible for telework can use the Army’s Azure Virtual Desktop (AVD) plus a CAC-reader on their home computers. AVD is a remote workspace that functions similarly to your government computer. Soldiers and both U.S. and local national employees can access AVD. Prepare now before bad weather hits: Download AVD to your personal computer and test it. Then, move important working files to your OneDrive. For more, click HERE.
title: What to do when bad weather hits USAG Ansbach

Reward Offers Up to $50M for Information Leading to Arrests and/or Convictions of Foreign Terrorist Organization Tren de Aragua (TdA) Leaders Following Homeland Security Task Force Investigation
Foreign Terrorist Organization Tren de Aragua (TdA) leaders Yohan José Romero, also known as “Yohan Petrica,” 48; Giovanni Vicente Mosquera Serrano, also known as “El Viejo,” 37; and Juan Gabriel Rivas Núñez, also known as “Juancho,” 44, were previously charged in a 2025 six-count second superseding indictment in the Southern District of Texas, for conspiring to provide and providing material support to TdA. A nine-count third superseding indictment was later returned in July 2026 and unsealed this week. In those indictments, Mosquera Serrano is also charged with conspiracy to manufacture and distribute cocaine and international cocaine distribution.
“Since President Trump returned to office, the Department of Justice has charged more than 350 members and associates of Tren de Aragua, including Yohan Petrica, El Viejo, and Juancho,” said Attorney General Todd Blanche. “Their criminal enterprise has spread fear, violence, and lawlessness, and we will not stop until those responsible are brought to justice. Anyone with information regarding the location of the three individuals listed in today’s superseding indictment should help save lives by notifying the FBI.”
“By leveraging DEA's investigative expertise alongside our partners through the Homeland Security Task Force, we are bringing the full force of the U.S. government to bear against narco-terrorists that threaten our communities,” said Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA) Administrator Terrance Cole. “Today's announcement demonstrates what can be achieved through unprecedented coordination and intelligence sharing across federal law enforcement. Yohan José Romero, Mosquera Serrano, and Rivas Núñez have played key roles in directing and expanding Tren de Aragua's operations throughout the Western Hemisphere. TdA spreads violence, fear, and instability wherever it operates. Make no mistake - DEA will stop at nothing to identify, disrupt, and dismantle this criminal network.”
“These gang members are monsters, and we’ve indicted them as such,” said U.S. Attorney Aaron Reitz of the Southern District of Texas. “I’m confident the enhanced bounties will incentivize these terrorists’ return to my district, where we will bring them to justice.”
Mosquera Serrano is on the FBI’s 10 Most Wanted Fugitives List. Jose Romero and Rivas Núñez are also fugitives. The Department of State’s Bureau of International Narcotics and Law Enforcement Affairs (INL) is offering rewards under the Transnational Organized Crime Rewards Program (TOCRP) of up to $50 million total for information leading to their arrests and/or convictions in any country.
“As Secretary Rubio has repeatedly stated, transnational criminal and terrorist organizations such as Tren de Aragua are the most urgent security threat in our hemisphere,” said Under Secretary of State for Arms Control and International Security Thomas G. DiNanno. “Today, we are offering rewards totaling up to $50 million under the Transnational Organized Crime Rewards Program for information leading to the arrests and/or convictions of the top three leaders of Tren de Aragua. The Trump Administration remains fully committed to eliminating narcoterrorist organizations in the region that traffic illicit drugs, commit violent acts, and cause harm to American communities.”
If you have any information concerning these individuals, please contact the FBI via WhatsApp or Telegram at 281-787-9939. Those with information may also contact their local FBI office, nearest American Embassy or Consulate or can submit a tip online at tips.fbi.gov.
The FBI and the DEA are jointly conducting the investigation with the assistance of the Houston Police Department, Harris County Sheriff’s Office, U.S. Marshals Service (USMS), Colombian National Police and the Colombian Attorney General’s Office (Fiscalía General de la Nación), with significant assistance from the Justice Department’s Office of Judicial Attaché in Bogota and Office of International Affairs.
The case is being prosecuted by Assistant U.S. Attorneys Casey N. MacDonald and Anibal J. Alaniz for the Southern District of Texas along with Joint Task Force Vulcan’s (JTFV) Deputy Director David C. Smith and Trial Attorneys James Keller and Kelly McGann.
TdA is a violent transnational criminal organization that originated as a prison gang in Venezuela in the mid-2000s. Since that time, TdA has expanded its criminal network throughout the Western Hemisphere and established a presence in the United States. TdA’s criminal activities range from drug trafficking and firearms trafficking to sex trafficking, kidnapping, robbery, theft, fraud, and extortion. TdA members also commit murder, assault, and other violent acts to advance the organization’s criminal activities. TdA has also developed an additional source of revenue stream by committing financial crimes that target financial institutions throughout the United States, including using ATM jackpotting to steal millions of dollars in cash. The investigation has revealed that the conspiracy has targeted or carried out ATM jackpotting attacks in 47 states, the District of Columbia, and several foreign nations.
This case is part of JTFV. JTFV was created in 2019 to eradicate MS-13 and has now expanded to target TdA. JTFV is comprised of U.S. Attorney’s Offices across the country, including Southern and Eastern Districts of New York; Eastern and Western Districts of North Carolina; Western District of Virginia; Middle and Southern Districts of Florida; Eastern District of Texas; Western District of Oklahoma; Northern District of Indiana; District of Nevada; and the District of Arizona, as well as the Executive Office for U.S. Attorneys, and the Department of Justice’s National Security Division, Criminal Division, and the Office of Judicial Attaché and DEA partners in Bogotá, Colombia. Additionally, the FBI, Homeland Security Investigations (HSI), Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives (ATF), USMS, and the Federal Bureau of Prisons are essential law enforcement partners with JTFV.
This prosecution is also part of the Homeland Security Task Force (HSTF) initiative established by Executive Order 14159, Protecting the American People Against Invasion. The HSTF is a whole-of-government partnership dedicated to eliminating criminal cartels, foreign gangs, transnational criminal organizations, and human smuggling and trafficking rings operating in the United States and abroad. Through historic interagency collaboration, the HSTF directs the full might of United States law enforcement towards identifying, investigating, and prosecuting the full spectrum of crimes committed by these organizations, which have long fueled violence and instability within our borders. In performing this work, the HSTF places special emphasis on investigating and prosecuting those engaged in child trafficking or other crimes involving children. The HSTF further utilizes all available tools to prosecute and remove the most violent criminal aliens from the United States. HSTF Houston comprises agents and officers from FBI; HSI; DEA; Texas Department of Public Safety; Houston Police Department; Harris County Sheriff's Office; ATF; USMS; U.S. Postal Inspection Service; Department of Transportation and IRS Criminal Investigation with the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Southern District of Texas leading the prosecution.
A complaint and indictment are merely allegations. All defendants are presumed innocent until proven guilty beyond a reasonable doubt in a court of law.
title: Reward Offers Up to $50M for Information Leading to Arrests and/or Convictions of Foreign Terrorist Organization Tren de Aragua (TdA) Leaders Following Homeland Security Task Force Investigation

The Department of War's Office of Strategic Capital (OSC) announced today a $75 million conditional loan commitment with Halo Industries, Inc., to scale production of its innovative Silicon Carbide (SiC) semiconductor wafers. The OSC investment crowds-in an additional $75 million in private capital and supports Halo's domestic manufacturing expansion to secure critical microelectronics supply chains.
OSC's conditional loan commitment to Halo advances President Donald J. Trump's call to revitalize the American defense industrial base, counter unfair foreign trade practices, and ensure critical technologies are made domestically.
Halo specializes in using proprietary, cutting-edge laser manufacturing technology to slice SiC ingots into wafers. This novel approach fundamentally disrupts legacy mechanical diamond-saw processes by significantly reducing material waste, improving throughput up to tenfold, and driving down production costs. The company's U.S. manufacturing operations in Santa Clara, California would onshore production of essential components, which are vital for high-voltage defense applications like advanced radar, electronic warfare, hypersonics, and directed energy weapons.
"Halo's new laser wafering technology will help establish cost-effective domestic supply chains, enabling the United States to compete globally and counteracting price dumping in the silicon carbide market. We're pleased to support Halo's domestic expansion, which will strengthen the semiconductor supply chain in the United States," said David A. Lorch, Director of the Office of Strategic Capital and Senior Advisor to Deputy Secretary of War Steve Feinberg.
Due to heavy state subsidies aiding foreign competitors, domestic producers of SiC wafers have faced intense pressure, leading to increased reliance on overseas supply chains. OSC's conditional financing would enable Halo to expand U.S. manufacturing operations, approach cost-parity with foreign competitors, and ultimately reduce reliance on foreign semiconductor materials.
"By crowding in private capital alongside our $75 million conditional commitment, we're accelerating the onshoring of next-generation semiconductor wafering technology," said Jordan B. Sebold, Senior Managing Director (Investments) with OSC. "This transaction is an important first step in strengthening the domestic supply chain of SiC wafers, and SiC wafers are foundational to American high-voltage power electronics, AI infrastructure, and national security capabilities."
"Secure access to advanced semiconductor materials is essential for national defense. By supporting domestic production of high-performance SiC wafers and unique domestic laser manufacturing capabilities, we're addressing a critical industrial base vulnerability and ensuring our warfighters have access to the power electronics and sensing capabilities they need," said Matthew Haberlach, Senior Vice President (Investments) with OSC.
The conditional loan commitment specifies additional steps Halo must complete before financial close, including satisfying various financial, legal, technical, investment, due diligence, and other requirements.
"The Office of Strategic Capital's financing is bringing next-generation manufacturing back to the United States, guaranteeing we control our own technological destiny. Securing America's microelectronics supply chain is non-negotiable for our national defense," said Emil Michael, Under Secretary of War for Research and Engineering.
title: Department of War's Office of Strategic Capital Signs $75 Million Conditional Loan Commitment With Halo Industries, Inc.
