Tallahassee, Florida – Yasir Jaimon Za’Quis Hawkins, 20, of Tallahassee, Florida, pleaded guilty in federal court to illegal possession of a machine gun, possession of Postal Service key, and possession of stolen mail. The plea was announced by John P. Heekin, United States Attorney for the Northern District of Florida.

U.S. Attorney Heekin said: “I commend the Leon County Sheriff’s Office for their excellent work, with support from our federal law enforcement partners, to catch this dangerous criminal and recover the funds stolen from dozens of victims. Now, thanks to the aggressive prosecution by my office, he will find himself behind federal bars where he belongs.”

Court documents reflect that on May 7, 2026, local law enforcement executed a search warrant at the defendant’s residence after the defendant posted numerous images of himself on social media with a firearm equipped with a machine gun conversion device. The machine gun conversion device was found during the search.

Additionally, law enforcement discovered fifty-three stolen checks and money orders in the defendant’s bedroom, along with a Postal arrow key. The checks and money orders totaled approximately $25,000 in stolen funds and originated from at least forty different victims.

Hawkins faces up to 10 years’ imprisonment on the possession of a machine gun count; up to 10 years’ imprisonment on the possession of Postal Service key count; and up to five years’ imprisonment on the possession of stolen mail count.

This case was jointly investigated by the United States Postal Inspection Service, the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives, and the Leon County Sheriff’s Office. Assistant United States Attorney Emma Schwan is prosecuting the case.

Sentencing is scheduled for January 25, 2027, at 3:00pm at the United States Courthouse in Tallahassee before Chief United States District Judge Allen C. Winsor.

Project Safe Neighborhoods (PSN) is the Department of Justice’s nationwide initiative that brings federal, state, local, and tribal law enforcement, prosecutors, and other public safety partners together to coordinate efforts to combat violent crime and make communities safe. Coordinated by U.S. Attorneys’ offices in each of the 94 federal districts, PSN is tailored to particular communities to strategically address specific violent crime and public safety challenges. As a key component of Operation Take Back America, PSN serves a central role in the Department’s commitment to make our country safe. PSN emphasizes three core principles: rapid federal response to violent crime and criminal offenders; strong, strategic partnerships among law enforcement at all levels; and accountability and deterrence through the prosecution of the most serious, readily provable offenses and other strategies. These efforts complement and strengthen President Trump’s Homeland Security Task Forces, ensuring a comprehensive federal response to the most pressing public safety issues facing communities .

The United States Attorney’s Office for the Northern District of Florida is one of 94 offices that serve as the nation’s principal litigators under the direction of the Attorney General. To access public court documents online, please visit the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of Florida website. For more information about the United States Attorney’s Office, Northern District of Florida, visit https://www.justice.gov/usao-ndfl .

SCHOFIELD BARRACKS, Hawaii – The Pacific jungle can be unforgiving. Thick canopy, extreme humidity, sporadic rainfall, and rugged terrain can block communications signals and challenge formations. In this environment, technology alone does not win fights, disciplined Soldiers do. However, when the right innovations are placed into the hands of those Soldiers, it significantly improves both their capability and survivability.
During the reception, staging, and onward integration phase of Joint Pacific Multinational Readiness Center (JPMRC) Rotation 27-01, Soldiers of the 2nd Mobile Brigade, 25th Infantry Division, are continuing to integrate advanced technologies into their tactical formations to create a highly effective combination of combat power.
Over the past year, the 25th Infantry Division has integrated and improved its modern command-and-control systems. The Lightning Surge exercise series continues to lay the foundation for next-generation command and control to ensure operational effectiveness. The Division moved these systems from controlled settings to challenging environments, with thorough field testing from Hawaii to the Philippines. Recently, a 3rd Mobile Brigade test platoon tested the same systems early in Lightning Surge 6, confirming that the mesh networks and rugged end-user devices the 2nd Mobile Brigade now uses are fully operational for combat.
"The feedback from the 3rd Mobile Brigade test element was absolutely vital," said Maj. Brenden Siekman, Lighting Surge 6 lead planner for the 25th Infantry Division. "We were able to ensure the equipment was fully validated before scaling it to the 2nd Mobile Brigade for the JPMRC fight.”
During JPMRC 27-01, the Soldiers of 2nd Mobile Brigade will use advanced tools, which include ruggedized end-user devices, tactical unmanned aerial systems, and resilient mesh networks, to support the close battle. Rather than operating in isolated silos, these systems feed into a common data layer, providing leaders at every echelon with a synchronized, real-time operating picture.
"Having this capability changes how we operate in the jungle," said 1st Lt. Anton Lieb, the company executive officer for bravo Company, 1st battalion-21st Infantry Regiment, 2nd Mobile Brigade. "Our operating picture is faster and we’re able to communicate faster and clearer without giving away our position. It directly improves our survivability and operational effectiveness on the ground."
This integration is part of how the Army is evolving and adapting to contemporary challenges in the Indo-Pacific. By converging sensors, shooters, and command applications into a unified, resilient ecosystem, this architecture enables commanders to make decisions at speed and scale.
Ultimately, JPMRC 27-01 reaffirms that modernization is only effective when it directly supports the warfighter. Technology strengthens combat power only when it is seamlessly integrated with disciplined Soldiers, sound fieldcraft, and effective small-unit leadership.
About the Joint Pacific Multinational Readiness Center:
The Joint Pacific Multinational Readiness Center is U.S. Army Pacific’s premier regional Combat Training Center. Operating across the Hawaiian Islands, Alaska, and exportable locations throughout the Indo-Pacific, JPMRC provides realistic, live, virtual, and constructive training in complex archipelagic, jungle, and arctic environments. The center generates combat-credible forces, validates multi-domain readiness, and deepens interoperability with Joint forces, allies, and multinational partners to uphold a free and open Indo-Pacific.
About the 25th Infantry Division:
The 25th Infantry Division, "Tropic Lightning," is America's Pacific Division, headquartered at Schofield Barracks, Hawaii. As the premier land force in the Pacific, the 25th ID provides combat-ready forces capable of conducting decisive operations across the Indo-Pacific. Through rigorous training and close partnerships with allies and the Joint Force, the division remains committed to warfighting excellence, regional stability, and being a responsible steward of the ‘āina and our local communities across the State of Hawaii.
title: Empowering the Light Fighter: Innovation Meets Fieldcraft at JPMRC 27-01

ESTABLISHING THE OVAL OFFICE NATIONAL MONUMENT: Today, President Donald J. Trump signed a Proclamation establishing the Oval Office as a National Monument to ensure its preservation, proper care, and management.
- The Proclamation proclaims the Oval Office, the Outer Oval Office, and the Cabinet Room as the Oval Office National Monument under the Antiquities Act.
- The Proclamation directs the Secretary of the Interior to develop and implement a management plan with relevant executive departments, agencies, and offices that prioritizes the preservation of the Oval Office, to document, review, and consider alternatives before substantially altering or demolishing the Oval Office, and to ensure that any proposed changes to its historic character are consistent with the Oval Office’s national significance.
- The Proclamation also directs the Secretary of the Interior to coordinate with the Committee for the Preservation of the White House and other appropriate advisory bodies.
PRESERVING THE OVAL OFFICE FOR FUTURE GENERATIONS: President Trump is taking action to ensure that the Oval Office gets the historic recognition and protection it deserves.
- The Oval Office stands as one of the most recognizable and historically significant spaces in the country, serving as the principal working office of the President of the United States for almost a century.
- A symbol of the Presidency of the most powerful nation in world history, the Oval Office has witnessed decisions of profound national and international consequence and history.
- The Oval Office merits more recognition and protective management as a distinct historic structure of national significance than its preexisting National Historic Landmark recognition.
HONORING AMERICA’S PAST AND BUILDING ITS FUTURE: President Trump is protecting and restoring the beauty of America’s capital and historical sites to showcase the greatness and excellence of the most extraordinary nation in the history of the world for generations to come.
- President Trump Made D.C. Beautiful Again, ensuring our nation’s capital is one of the most beautiful cities anywhere in the world by cleaning hundreds of graffiti sites, fixing over 2,300 light fixtures, repairing dozens of fountains, and cleaning and repairing the Reflecting Pool.
- In August 2025, President Trump mandated that Federal public buildings embrace classical architecture to honor tradition, foster civic pride, and inspire the citizenry.
- President Trump fulfilled his campaign promise to “give America’s founding in 1776 the incredible anniversary it truly deserves” by bringing back the National Garden of American Heroes, building a new Triumphal Arch, and holding events that showcase American greatness.
- President Trump has led the charge in building a much-needed White House Ballroom, expanding the East Wing at no cost to the American taxpayer to more than triple the White House’s hosting capacity for major functions for generations to come while preserving the White House’s special history and beacon of American excellence.
title: Fact Sheet: President Donald J. Trump Establishes the Oval Office as a National Monument

WEIDEN, Germany - Nearly 200 local and regional business representatives gathered Oct. 29, 2026, for Vendor Day, hosted jointly by the Chamber of Commerce and Industry (IHK) Regensburg for the Oberpfalz / Kelheim and the County Artisan Chamber Nordoberpfalz.
The event enabled the 409th Contracting Support Brigade to show prospective vendors how to register in the U.S. Army contracting systems and compete for contracts to support the military community in Bavaria.
Experienced vendors also shared lessons learned from working with the U.S. government and explained the importance of meeting American customer expectations.
Kerstin Schug, owner of Delicado Wein Shop & Delicatessen, said American customers often approach shopping differently.
“Americans shop with more enthusiasm,” Schug said. “They expect and love good service and react with, ‘That’s amazing,’ unlike Germans, whose most enthusiastic reaction is more reserved, like: ‘This is not bad.’”
Monika Riedl, with the U.S. Army Garrison Bavaria Directorate of Family, Morale, Welfare, and Recreation, then briefed the attendees on marketing opportunities with the garrison to make their services and businesses known to the Bavarian military communities. Opportunities include sponsoring events and advertising through DFMWR.
German companies bring that customer-focused approach to their work with the U.S. Army, said Lt. Col. Quammie Semper, commander of the 928th Contracting Battalion.
“In my experience, German companies are very willing to go the extra mile to make sure the troops, Soldiers and Families are taken care of over the span of that contract,” Semper said.
Semper said the Vendor Day helps the Army attract more businesses to compete for contracts. More competition gives the Army more options, helps it secure better value and prices, and strengthens its stewardship of U.S. taxpayer funds.
The event strengthened relationships with the local business community and gave prospective vendors a clearer path to pursue U.S. Army contracting opportunities.
title: Vendor Day connects German businesses with U.S. Army opportunities

CMS Final Rule Strengthens Supports Lasting Drug Savings
The Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) is establishing a permanent framework for negotiating prices of high-cost drugs. The final rule sets policies for the Medicare Drug Price Negotiation Program beginning with prices effective in 2029, providing greater predictability for participating manufacturers and supporting continued innovation.
“President Trump directed us to lower drug costs for Americans using every tool at our disposal,” said CMS Administrator Dr. Mehmet Oz. “This rule provides additional tools to help CMS negotiate better deals, achieve greater savings for taxpayers and beneficiaries, and improve health outcomes for seniors who rely on the Medicare Prescription Drug Program.”
By Feb. 1, 2027, CMS will select up to 20 additional negotiation-eligible drugs covered under Part D and/or payable under Part B, as well as select drugs for renegotiation, as appropriate, for the fourth cycle of negotiations. This rule gives patients and manufacturers a clear path forward as the agency builds on the program’s results and continues negotiating prices for high-cost drugs.
The rule finalizes a proposed policy regarding treatment of specific fixed combination drugs that CMS determines are new formulations of existing drugs. To address potential program integrity concerns, CMS believes this policy will avoid creating an incentive for the primary manufacturer to shift patients toward the new formulation and circumvent the application of the maximum fair price (MFP) for such patients.
The rule also implements the Temporary Floor for Small Biotech Drugs, as required by law, which prohibits CMS from offering or accepting a counteroffer for an MFP below a specified floor for certain eligible Small Biotech Drugs for initial price applicability years 2029 and 2030.
The rule also codifies two policies affecting the Medicare Part D benefit, consistent with statutory requirements. These policies require Part D plans to include selected drugs with an MFP in effect on their formularies and limit the negotiated prices plans pay dispensing entities to the MFP plus any dispensing fees.
To view the final rule on the Federal Register, visit: https://www.federalregister.gov/d/2026-22792.
To view a fact sheet on the final rule, visit: https://www.cms.gov/files/document/negotiation-program-final-rule-fact-sheet.pdf
To view Initial Price Applicability Year 2029 Key Milestones and Timeline, visit: https://www.cms.gov/files/document/negotiation-program-final-rule-timeline.pdf.
Additional information about the Medicare Drug Price Negotiation Program, including selected drugs, agreed-upon MFPs, and past program guidance, is available at: https://www.cms.gov/priorities/medicare-prescription-drug-affordability/overview/medicare-drug-price-negotiation-program.
###

title: CMS Final Rule Strengthens Supports Lasting Drug Savings

The fifth annual Celebrate Madison was in full swing Thursday night, Oct. 29 at Toyota Field. The event offered family fun for all ages with trick-or-treating, food samples and patriotic performances.
“Celebrate Madison was just an idea five years ago, and now it’s a community tradition,” Madison Chamber president Michelle Epling said. “This didn’t happen because of one person, organization or business. It happened because people believed Madison is something worth celebrating.”
The air was full of early 2000s tunes, with Ciara’s “1, 2 step” taking the chill from the air and setting the tone for the night as over 900 attendees entered the celebration.
Trick-or-treaters got a bag upon entry and made their way throughout the walking zones of the stadium receiving candy and merchandise from vendors and sponsors. As the festivities began, kiddos took a seat with their treats and watched a 30-minute patriotic presentation.
The celebration also included a special tribute to Team Redstone, as the Arsenal celebrates its 85th year. Madison Celebrates Team Redstone served as the theme for the night.
Honorees from Redstone included Garrison Commander Col. Katie Slingerland, Space Command Maj. Gen. Terry Grisham and Brig. Gen. Katie Trombley, from the Army Reserve.
When presented with their tokens, the stadium echoed with “Thank you, Team Redstone.”
“Thank you seems like such a small token of our appreciation for all of our partners with Team Redstone, for all you do for our city and nation,” Epling said.
Following was an update on Madison City Schools, in which they received a $15,000 check for their Supporting Our Students fund, and the announcement of Madison’s military family of the year. This year, the Wilson family was the honoree.
Andy and Bryana Wilson have served in the Army a combined 26 years. The Wilsons have three kids and the family of five often opens their home to foster children, spends time volunteering and running through the Rocket City.
Their nominator, Amber Moore said, “Their service extends far beyond the military; reflecting a lifelong commitment to their family, neighbors and the Madison community. Their faith has inspired years of service as youth leaders, tutors and mentors.”
After the Wilsons were honored, more music filled the air along with a fireworks show to usher out the minor league baseball stadium’s guests for the night.
title: Madison celebration has salute to Redstone theme

PORTLAND, Ore.— U.S. Attorney Scott E. Bradford announced today that Alec Joseph Adams , 30, of Oregon, has been charged by criminal complaint with possession of child sexual abuse material (CSAM) after federal agents allegedly discovered illicit images and videos on his cell phone during an inspection at Portland International Airport.

“Every image and video depicting child sexual abuse represents a real child victim,” said U.S. Attorney Scott E. Bradford. “The Department of Justice remains steadfast in its commitment to protecting children from exploitation and aggressively prosecuting individuals who possess, produce, or distribute child sexual abuse material.”

According to court documents, on Oct. 28, 2026, Adams arrived at Portland International Airport on a flight from Reykjavik, Iceland. During a customs inspection, U.S. Customs and Border Protection officers learned that Adams was serving a term of probation in Lincoln County, Oregon, following convictions for luring a child and online sexual corruption of a child.

Court documents allege that during a basic media examination of Adams' cellphone, Customs and Border Protection officers discovered suspected child sexual abuse material. Homeland Security Investigations (HSI) agents were notified and conducted a preliminary review of the device.

According to an affidavit filed in support of the criminal complaint, investigators observed multiple images and video thumbnails depicting nude prepubescent and pubescent children engaged in sexually explicit conduct in a hidden folder on Adams' phone.

Federal investigators subsequently obtained a search warrant for the device. During a more extensive review, agents allegedly located additional videos depicting the sexual abuse of young children. Court documents describe videos showing prepubescent children engaged in sexually explicit conduct with adults.

Adams has been charged with one count of possession of child pornography, which is punishable by up to 20 years in federal prison, a fine of up to $250,000, and a lifetime term of supervised release.

The case was investigated by Homeland Security Investigations and U.S. Customs and Border Protection.

The Special Prosecutions Unit for the District of Oregon is prosecuting the case.

A criminal complaint is only an allegation of criminal conduct, and a defendant is presumed innocent unless and until proven guilty.
title: Oregon Man on State Supervision Arrested for Possessing Child Sexual Abuse Material After Arriving at Portland International Airport

ST. LOUIS – U.S. District Judge Joshua M. Divine on Thursday sentenced a convicted felon who was caught with drugs and a gun after fleeing from police to 110 months in prison.

On August 26, 2025, the Missouri State Highway Patrol stopped Wendell Mosley, 36, in a Ford Taurus on U.S. Highway 67 in St. Francois County, Missouri. Mosley showed signs of deception and nervousness when asked about his reason for travelling. At one point, Mosley ran away from the trooper, hopped in his car and sped south on Highway 67. Mosley fled on foot after wrecking the car, discarding a bag before he was arrested. Troopers later found the bag, which contained a 9mm handgun and 232 capsules containing oxycodone.

Mosley, now 36, pleaded guilty in August in U.S. District Court in St. Louis to one count of being a felon in possession of a firearm and one count of possession with the intent to distribute oxycodone.

The Missouri State Highway Patrol and the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives investigated the case. Assistant U.S. Attorney Jolene Taaffe prosecuted the case.

This case is part of Project Safe Neighborhoods (PSN), the Department of Justice’s nationwide initiative that brings federal, state, local, and tribal law enforcement, prosecutors, and other public safety partners together to coordinate efforts to combat violent crime and make communities safe. Coordinated by U.S. Attorneys’ offices in each of the 94 federal districts, PSN is tailored to particular communities to strategically address specific violent crime and public safety challenges. As a key component of Operation Take Back America, PSN serves a central role in the Department’s commitment to make our country safe. PSN emphasizes three core principles: rapid federal response to violent crime and criminal offenders; strong, strategic partnerships among law enforcement at all levels; and accountability and deterrence through the prosecution of the most serious, readily provable offenses and other strategies. These efforts complement and strengthen President Trump’s Homeland Security Task Forces, ensuring a comprehensive federal response to the most pressing public safety issues facing communities.
title: St. Louis Felon Who Fled from Police Sentenced to 110 Months in Prison

FORT LEE, Va. – More than 25 Soldiers assigned to Detachment 1, 54th Quartermaster Company (Fatality Management), 10th Transportation Battalion (Terminal), 7th Transportation Brigade (Expeditionary) were recognized in a deployment ceremony Nov. 2 at the Fort Lee Family Life Center as they prepare to deploy to the U.S. Central Command area of responsibility in support of Operation Spartan Shield.
The detachment, led by 1st Lt. Elhadji Beye and Staff Sgt. Colten Savage, will assume the fatality management support mission in the CENTCOM, charged with returning fallen military members to their next of kin.
“Not everyone can do this work; Detachment 1 has prepared with purpose, they have trained hard on their platoon tasks, built their skills, and learned to operate as one team as well as planned and coordinated the movement that brought them here today,” said Capt. Alexander Young, 54th QM Co. commander. “That work demanded discipline, attention to detail, and trust in one another, they earn the confidence we place in them today.
“Fatality management has a very unique mission that require technical skills, sound judgment, compassion, and the strength to serve with dignity in difficult circumstances,” said the captain. “Detachment 1 has chosen to take on that responsibility, and their service will honor those they support and the families who depend on them.”
Several of the members have deployed to CENTCOM before including Beye who has deployed four times before and Savage who was a team leader in 2023.
“It’s a good feeling, I will be leading troops,” said Staff Sgt. Jamal Crosby who is deploying for the fourth time. “I get another one (deployment) under my belt.”
For many in the detachment, this will be their first deployment, Pfc. Zahnae Johnson says she’s ready to get more experience.
While the Soldiers are deployed, Lt. Col. Zachary Miller, 10th Trans. Bn. commander, assured them that the battalion will not forget their families.
“Our commitment to you does not stop when those busses pull away tomorrow,” said Miller. “I want you to know that my door, our command team, our soldiers, and family support network remain available to you throughout this deployment.
“Your families are the foundation, they deserve the same commitment and dedication that you bring to this mission,” said Miller.
Miller reminded the Soldiers, that it is more than just a deployment; it's about service, sacrifice, family, and a tremendous responsibility they are preparing to undertake.
“You have been entrusted with one of the most important and honorable missions in our U.S. Army; mortuary affairs is not a mission that receives the recognition or attention it deserves, but I would argue that few missions carry a greater responsibility,” said Miller. When our nation calls its sons and daughters to serve, we make a commitment to them and their families; that commitment does not end when a soldier makes the ultimate sacrifice -- it is carried forward by soldiers like you.
“You are entrusted with ensuring that our fallen service members are treated with dignity, respect, and honor; your professionalism provides comfort to families during some of the most difficult moments of their lives,” said the colonel. “You represent the Army's final commitment to those who have given everything for our nation and that is a tremendous responsibility, and you have been trained and certified to carry it out to the families, to the spouses, children, parents, and loved ones.”
The 54th QM Co. is the Army’s only active-duty fatality management unit. Through Operation Spartan Shield, Task Force Spartan maintains a U.S. military posture in Southwest Asia sufficient to strengthen our defense relationships and build partner capacity.
title: 54th QM Co. Soldiers deploy to CENTCOM AOR

Lawmakers amplify concerns raised by state student loan ombudspersons in 7 states and D.C.
“Failures in federal student loan servicing have repeatedly posed severe and costly problems for American families.”

“Failures in federal student loan servicing have repeatedly posed severe and costly problems for American families. . . .Rather than tackle these servicing failures, the Trump administration has enabled more to occur,” wrote the lawmakers.
In September 2026, the Student Loan Ombudspersons in Massachusetts, Washington, California, Oregon, Nevada, Connecticut, the District of Columbia, and Illinois sent a letter to Secretary McMahon highlighting “recurring systemic problems involving income-driven repayment (IDR) plans and Public Service Loan Forgiveness (PSLF) that materially affect borrowers’ payment obligations, loan balances, and access to forgiveness.” The Ombudspersons raised a host of specific issues, including inaccurate calculations of monthly payments, loan balances, and IDR payment counts, and severe delays in the processing of IDR applications.
“The scale and severity of the errors documented by the Student Loan Ombudspersons—and their recommended solutions—demand immediate consideration and a meaningful response,” concluded the lawmakers.

A man with a prior federal drug conviction who was selling drugs again was sentenced on November 4, 2026, to more than three years in federal prison.

William Robertson, age 64, from Cedar Rapids, Iowa, received the prison term after a May 21, 2026, guilty plea to one count of distribution of a controlled substance near a protected location.

In a plea agreement, Robertson admitted he distributed controlled substances on four separate occasions between October and November 2024. On the first occasion, Robertson admitted that he distributed a mixture or substance containing heroin, flourofentanyl, and fentanyl, as well as a mixture or substance containing cocaine base. On the second occasion, Robertson admitted that he distributed a mixture or substance containing fentanyl and a mixture or substance containing cocaine base. On the third occasion, Robertson admitted that he distributed a mixture or substance containing cocaine base. On the fourth occasion, Robertson admitted that he distributed a mixture or substance containing cocaine. Robertson admitted that the first three distributions took place within 1,000 feet of a school in Cedar Rapids. Robertson was previously convicted of conspiracy to distribute five grams or more of cocaine base within 1,000 feet of a protected location in 2008 in the United States District Court for the Northern District of Iowa.

Robertson was sentenced in Cedar Rapids by United States District Court Chief Judge C.J. Williams. Robertson was sentenced to 41 months and 15 days’ imprisonment. He must also serve a 10-year term of supervised release after the prison term. There is no parole in the federal system.

Robertson is being held in the United States Marshal’s custody until he can be transported to a federal prison.

The case was prosecuted by Assistant United States Attorney Adam J. Vander Stoep and was investigated by the Cedar Rapids Police Department.

Court file information at https://ecf.iand.uscourts.gov/cgi-bin/login.pl .

The case file number is 25-CR-29.

Follow us on X @USAO_NDIA.
title: Man With Prior Federal Drug Conviction Sentenced to Federal Prison for Selling Drugs Again

With small UAS, or drones, taking a large role in the future of warfare, the Joint Modernization Command recently took a look at a Multi-Functional Reconnaissance Troop’s role in a European exercise to assess how the unit will be able to use Army drones for reconnaissance missions in the future.
The MFRT of the 1st Armored Division participated in the Combined Resolve multinational training exercise in late October at the Joint Multinational Readiness Center in Hohenfels, Germany. JMC teamed up with personnel from Transformation and Lessons Learned-Armor Maneuver to assess the troop’s ability to adapt to modern warfare concepts.
The assessment teams saw Army units innovating and exploring ways to adapt their formations to an era of UAS-dominated warfare. The troop had to find ways to use their technology in ways that kept them concealed from the opposing forces. Cpt. Kevin Rincon, commander of the MFRT, was impressed at how his Soldiers faced the challenge.
“I think there’s been a significant amount of growth in how the MFRT had been employed from the last rotation to now in the sense of being able to rely on the squadron to provide security and allowing us to keep our assets alive and shape the battlefield,” Rincon said. “So, overall, I’m extremely impressed. Impressed with the operators down to the lowest level.”
Rincon said the team’s initiative and teamwork was a good example of leadership in action, setting clear goals and trusting the Soldiers to get the job done. By combining raw skill with smart battery and energy management, the platoon kept their small UAS flying for more than 80 hours across 219 flights in 10 days. This constant eye in the sky allowed them to spot targets for a major portion of the operation’s artillery strikes and successfully carry out 19 direct drone attacks with confirmed hits.
Through Army exercises small and large, JMC experimentation and assessments push forward on Army modernization. The lessons learned inform the recently published “How the Army Fights” guidance, with an effort to get robotics, autonomous systems and super intelligence into formations at scale.
title: Joint Modernization Command looks at unit's future role in drone warfare

- For Immediate Release:
The U.S. Food and Drug Administration today granted accelerated approval to Rybrevant Faspro (amivantamab and hyaluronidase-lpuj) for the treatment of adults with recurrent or metastatic head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC) whose disease has progressed on or after platinum-based chemotherapy and immunotherapy. HNSCC is an aggressive, life-threatening disease for which there is a high unmet need for effective therapies.
Rybrevant Faspro is not indicated as a treatment for patients with oropharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma that is associated with human papillomavirus (HPV).
Approval was based on trial results showing that more than double the percentage of patients responded to the drug compared to currently approved therapies. This is the first approval in 10 years of a drug for patients with recurrent or metastatic HNSCC who had received prior platinum-based chemotherapy.
“Today’s approval represents a meaningful step forward for patients with head and neck squamous cell carcinoma, a disease where treatment options have historically been limited and outcomes remain poor,” said Angelo De Claro, M.D., director of the FDA’s Oncology Center of Excellence. “This therapy offers patients and their physicians a new option with the potential to make a real difference in people’s lives.”
The Accelerated Approval Program allows for earlier approval of drugs that treat serious conditions and fill an unmet medical need based on surrogate or intermediate endpoints. In this case, accelerated approval of Rybrevant Faspro was granted based on overall response rate and duration of response. Since it is not yet confirmed whether this will translate into a clinically meaningful benefit in long-term outcomes, the FDA has required confirmatory studies to verify and describe clinical benefit.
In an open-label, multicenter clinical trial involving 102 patients with recurrent or metastatic HNSCC, Rybrevant Faspro had an overall response rate of 42%, meaning these patients saw their tumor either decrease in size or disappear. Of those patients who had a response, 56% had a response lasting six months or longer. Currently approved therapies are associated with an overall response rate of around 20% or less and poor outcomes.
The prescribing information for use as a single agent includes warnings and precautions for hypersensitivity and administration-related reactions, interstitial lung disease (ILD)/pneumonitis, dermatologic adverse reactions, ocular toxicity, and harm to an unborn baby.
The FDA granted Rybrevant Faspro Breakthrough Therapy designation for this indication. The approval was granted to Janssen Biotech, Inc.
The FDA, an agency within the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services, protects the public health by assuring the safety, effectiveness, and security of human and veterinary drugs, vaccines and other biological products for human use, and medical devices. The agency also is responsible for the safety and security of our nation’s food supply, cosmetics, dietary supplements, radiation-emitting electronic products, and for regulating tobacco products.

BILLINGS – A Billings man who was driving around town unlawfully carrying a firearm was sentenced today to two years and six months in prison, followed by three years of supervised release, U.S. Attorney Scott Twito said.

U.S. District Judge Kathleen S. Lane presided.

Chase Ryan Daniel Hooper, 27, pleaded guilty in July 2026 to unlawfully possessing a firearm.

The government alleged in court documents that Hooper fled from Yellowstone County Sheriff’s deputies driving a motorcycle without a license plate. When deputies caught up to Hooper, they discovered ammunition in his pockets and a 9mm handgun in the saddlebag of his motorcycle. Hooper had previously been convicted of a felony and was prohibited from possessing a firearm.

Assistant U.S. Attorney Tom Godfrey prosecuted the case. The ATF conducted the investigation.

Project Safe Neighborhoods (PSN) is the Department of Justice’s nationwide initiative that brings federal, state, local, and tribal law enforcement, prosecutors, and other public safety partners together to coordinate efforts to combat violent crime and make communities safe. Coordinated by U.S. Attorneys’ offices in each of the 94 federal districts, PSN is tailored to particular communities to strategically address specific violent crime and public safety challenges. As a key component of Operation Take Back America, PSN serves a central role in the Department’s commitment to make our country safe. PSN emphasizes three core principles: rapid federal response to violent crime and criminal offenders; strong, strategic partnerships among law enforcement at all levels; and accountability and deterrence through the prosecution of the most serious, readily provable offenses and other strategies. These efforts complement and strengthen President Trump’s Homeland Security Task Forces, ensuring a comprehensive federal response to the most pressing public safety issues facing communities.
title: Billings man sentenced to more than 2 years in prison for unlawfully possessing handgun

TOPEKA, KAN. – An illegal alien from Mexico who has been deported six times was sentenced to 108 months in prison for returning to the United States without permission.

According to court documents, Ysidoro Martinez-Arguello, 57, pleaded guilty to one count of unlawful reentry after deportation.

Martinez-Arguello was deported from the United States three times in 2010 and again in 2015, 2016, and 2023, and had been convicted and incarcerated seven times on charges related to driving under the influence of alcohol or drugs between 1993 and 2018.

Martinez-Arguello came to the attention of law enforcement after being involved in a fatality traffic accident in Manhattan, Kansas, in August of 2025, which did not involve alcohol or drugs.

“As Judge Tony Mattivi stated at sentencing in this matter, more lenient sentences have tried and failed for Mr. Martinez-Arguello,” said U.S. Attorney Ryan A. Kriegshauser. “With his numerous offenses, removal alone will not keep the public safe given Mr. Martinez-Arguello’s numerous re-entries after deportation and other crimes. Illegal aliens who ignore our laws and harm our communities will be prosecuted before they are removed.”

Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) investigated the case.

Assistant U.S. Attorney Duston Slinkard prosecuted the case.

title: Illegal alien deported six times sentenced to prison

IR-2026-133, Nov. 5, 2026
WASHINGTON — The Internal Revenue Service today announced the tax year 2027 annual inflation adjustments for almost 70 tax provisions, including the tax rate schedules, standard deduction amounts and other tax changes. Revenue Procedure 2026-35 PDF provides details about these annual adjustments.
Taxpayers continue to benefit from the Working Families Tax Cuts
“Hardworking American taxpayers will continue to benefit from the Working Families Tax Cuts (WFTC) and will see WFTC credits and deductions increase with this adjustment,” said IRS Chief Executive Officer Frank J. Bisignano. “American individuals and businesses will see increased tax benefits next tax year ranging from an increase in the standard deduction and the Child Tax Credit for families, and a boost to the amount that can be expensed by businesses.”
The tax year 2027 adjustments described below generally apply to tax returns filed in 2028. The tax items for tax year 2027 of greatest interest to most taxpayers include the following dollar amounts:
- Standard Deduction. For tax year 2027, the standard deduction increases to $33,200 for married couples filing jointly, up $1,000 from 2026. For single taxpayers and married individuals filing separately, the standard deduction rises to $16,600 for tax year 2027, and for heads of households, the standard deduction will be $24,925.
- Marginal Rates: For tax year 2027, the top tax rate remains 37% for individual single taxpayers with incomes greater than $661,375 ($793,650 for married couples filing jointly). The other rates are: 
35% for incomes over $264,550 ($529,100 for married couples filing jointly);
32% for incomes over $208,325 ($416,650 for married couples filing jointly);
24% for incomes over $109,125 ($218,250 for married couples filing jointly);
22% for incomes over $52,025 ($104,050 for married couples filing jointly);
12% for incomes over $12,800 ($25,600 for married couples filing jointly).
The lowest rate is 10% for incomes of single individuals with incomes of $12,800 or less ($25,600 for married couples filing jointly).
- The maximum amount of the child tax credit for 2027 is $2,300, an increase of $100 from 2026. For tax year 2027, the amount of credit that may be refundable is $1,800, also up $100 from 2026.
- Alternative Minimum Tax Exemption Amounts. For tax year 2027, the exemption amount for unmarried individuals is $93,000 and begins to phase out at $515,950 ($144,700 for married couples filing jointly for whom the exemption begins to phase out at $1,031,900).
- Estate Tax Exclusion. Estates of decedents who die during 2027 have a basic exclusion amount of $15,480,000, up from a total of $15,000,000 for estates of decedents who died in 2026. For calendar year 2027, the first $20,000 of gifts to any person are not included in the total amount of taxable gifts made during the year – up from $19,000 for calendar year 2026.
- Annual Exclusion for Gifts. For calendar year 2027, the annual exclusion for gifts increases to $20,000, up from $19,000 for calendar year 2026. (However, the annual exclusion for gifts to a spouse who is not a citizen of the United States increases to $201,000 for calendar year 2027, up from $194,000 for calendar year 2026.)
- Expensing. For tax year 2027 taxpayers can expense up to $2,640,000 of section 179 property, up from $2,560,000 for tax year 2026. The limit for sport utility vehicles for tax year 2027 is $33,100, up from $32,000 for tax year 2026.
- Adoption Credits. The maximum credit allowed for adoptions for tax year 2027 is the amount of qualified adoption expenses up to $18,250, up from $17,670 for 2026. For tax year 2027, the amount of credit that may be refundable is $5,280.
- Employer-Provided Childcare Tax Credit. The WFTC significantly enhanced an important credit for employers; For tax year 2027, the maximum amount of employer-provided childcare tax credit rises to $515,943.67 up from $500,000 for 2026 ($619,132.40 if the employer is an eligible small business).
Other notable items affected by indexing
- Earned Income Tax Credits. The tax year 2027 maximum Earned Income Tax Credit (EITC) amount is $8,496 for qualifying taxpayers who have three or more qualifying children, up from $8,231 for tax year 2026. Revenue Procedure 2026-35 contains a table providing maximum EITC amount for other categories, income thresholds and phase-outs.
- Qualified Transportation Fringe Benefit. For tax year 2027, the monthly limitation for the qualified transportation fringe benefit and the monthly limitation for qualified parking increases to $350, up $10 from 2026.
- Health Flexible Spending Cafeteria Plans. For tax years beginning in 2027, the dollar limitation for voluntary employee salary reductions for contributions to health flexible spending arrangements increases to $3,500, up $100 from the prior year. For cafeteria plans that permit the carryover of unused amounts, the maximum carryover amount is $700, an increase of $20 from tax years beginning in 2026.
- Medical Savings Accounts. For tax year 2027, participants who have self-only coverage in a Medical Savings Account, the plan must have an annual deductible that is not less than $3,000, up $100 from tax year 2026 – but not more than $4,550, an increase of $150 from tax year 2026. For self-only coverage, the maximum out-of-pocket expense amount is $6050, up $200 from 2026. For tax year 2027, for family coverage, the annual deductible is not less than $6,050, up from $5,850 for 2026; however, the deductible cannot be more than $9,050, up $300 from the limit for tax year 2026. For family coverage, the out-of-pocket expense limit is $11,050 for tax year 2027, an increase of $250 from tax year 2026.
- Foreign Earned Income Exclusion. For tax year 2027, the foreign earned income exclusion is $137,300 up from $132,900 for tax year 2026.
Items unaffected by indexing
By statute, certain items that were indexed for inflation in the past are currently not adjusted.
- Personal Exemptions. For tax year 2027, personal exemptions remain at 0, as in tax year 2026. The elimination of the personal exemption was a provision in the Tax Cuts and Jobs Act of 2017 and was made permanent by the WFTC. (The personal exemption described here does not include the senior deduction added by the WFTC.)
- Itemized Deductions. The limitation on itemized deductions was previously eliminated for tax years 2018 - 2025. The elimination of the limitation was made permanent by the WFTC, although it imposes a limitation on the tax benefit from itemized deductions for those taxpayers in the highest tax bracket (37%).
Lifetime Learning Credits. The modified adjusted gross income (MAGI) amount used to phase out the Lifetime Learning Credit has not been adjusted for inflation for tax years beginning after Dec. 31, 2020. The Lifetime Learning Credit is phased out for taxpayers with MAGI between $80,000 and $90,000 ($160,000 and $180,000 for joint returns).
title: IRS releases tax inflation adjustments for tax year 2027; taxpayers continue to benefit from the Working Families Tax Cuts

Texas Man Indicted for Sex Trafficking and Obstruction Offenses
A federal grand jury in the Northern District of Texas returned an eight-count superseding indictment charging Felix Omoruyi, 39, of DeSoto, Texas, with sex trafficking by force, fraud, or coercion, sex trafficking of a minor, and related charges.
According to court documents, from December 2007 through November 2025, Omoruyi compelled five adult women to perform commercial sex acts in Texas and elsewhere for his financial benefit. Omoruyi trafficked one of those women beginning when she was a minor. After he was arrested on the initial indictment in November 2025, he also corruptly attempted to destroy evidence and obstruct and interfere with his prosecution by contacting victims and witnesses to influence their statements and testimony.
Omoruyi is charged with sex trafficking by force, fraud, or coercion; sex trafficking of a minor; attempt to destroy, alter, or conceal a document or object; and obstruction and interference with the enforcement of the sex trafficking statute. If convicted of sex trafficking by force, fraud, or coercion, he faces a minimum penalty of 15 years in prison and a maximum penalty of life in prison along with mandatory restitution.
Assistant Attorney General A. Tysen Duva of the Justice Department’s Criminal Division; U.S. Attorney Ryan R. Raybould for the Northern District of Texas; and Acting Special Agent in Charge Jeffrey A. Grimming of Homeland Security Investigations (HSI) New England made the announcement.
The HSI New England Field Office is investigating the case with assistance from HSI Dallas and the Barnstable Police Department.
Trial Attorney Matthew Thiman of the Criminal Division’s Human Rights and Special Prosecutions Section and Assistant U.S. Attorney Brandie Wade for the Northern District of Texas are prosecuting the case.
Anyone who has information about human trafficking should report that information to the National Human Trafficking Hotline toll-free at 1-888-373-7888, which is available 24 hours a day, seven days a week. For more information about human trafficking, please visit www.humantraffickinghotline.org. Information on the Department of Justice’s efforts to combat human trafficking can be found at www.justice.gov/humantrafficking.
An indictment is merely an allegation. All defendants are presumed innocent until proven guilty beyond a reasonable doubt in a court of law.
title: Texas Man Indicted for Sex Trafficking and Obstruction Offenses
