MOAB , Utah – A San Juan County, Utah, man was sentenced to 35 months’ imprisonment today after, over the course of several days, he violently assaulted several people. The man punched, strangled, and threatened to kill a woman, struck a man over the head with a stick and threatened to kill him with a knife, and assaulted federal officers with the Bureau of Indian Affairs that had arrived to intervene.

Zane C. Yazzie, 33, of Aneth, Utah, pleaded guilty on July 9, 2026, to assault resulting in serious bodily injury while within Indian Country, assault with a dangerous weapon with intent to do bodily harm while within Indian Country, and assault on a federal officer.

In addition to his term of imprisonment, U.S. District Court Judge Anne Marie McIff Allen, sentenced him to three years of supervised release.

According to court documents and statements made at Yazzie’s change of plea and sentencing hearings, between March 5, 2026 and March 9, 2026, while within the exterior boundaries of the Navajo Nation Reservation, Yazzie assaulted a female victim over the course of several days. Yazzie punched the female victim in the face and broke her nose, strangled her with his hands, and threatened her with a firearm. During this same time period, and in the same location, Yazzie also assaulted a second victim by hitting him over the head with a stick while he was sleeping. A couple of days later on March 9, 2026, Yazzie also held a knife up to the victim’s throat and stated he was going to slit it. On the same day, when law enforcement responded to a report related to these assaults and at this same location, Yazzie assaulted federal officers with the Bureau of Indian Affairs by attempting to strike them with his fist to cause injury.

Calendar Year 2027 Hospital Outpatient Prospective Payment System (OPPS) and Ambulatory Surgical Center (ASC) Final Rule (CMS-1850-F)
On November 4, 2026, the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) issued a final rule that updates Medicare payment policies and rates for hospital outpatient and Ambulatory Surgical Center (ASC) services under the Hospital Outpatient Prospective Payment System (OPPS) and ASC Payment System for calendar year (CY) 2027. CMS is publishing this final rule consistent with statutory requirements to review and update Medicare payment rates for hospital outpatient departments and ASCs annually. This fact sheet discusses the final rule’s major provisions.
These payment updates affect approximately 3,500 hospitals and approximately 6,400 ASCs. In addition to finalizing the payment rates, this year’s rule includes updates to the methodology used to calculate the Overall Hospital Quality Star Rating to emphasize the Safety of Care measure group in hospitals’ star ratings. CMS is also finalizing changes to the Hospital Outpatient Quality Reporting (OQR) and ASC Quality Reporting (ASCQR) programs to further meaningful measurement and reporting for outpatient quality of care.
Updates to OPPS and ASC Payment Rates
In accordance with statutory requirements, CMS is finalizing an update to the OPPS payment rates for hospitals that meet applicable quality reporting requirements by 2.3%. This update is based on the projected hospital market basket percentage increase of 3.2%, reduced by a 0.9 percentage point productivity adjustment.
For CY 2027, using the hospital market basket update, CMS is finalizing an update factor to the ASC rates of 2.3%. The update applies to ASCs meeting relevant quality reporting requirements. This update is based on the IPPS market basket percentage increase of 3.2%, reduced by 0.9 percentage point for the productivity adjustment.
Expanding the Method to Control Unnecessary Increases in the Volume of Outpatient Services
In the CY 2019 OPPS/ASC final rule, CMS adopted a method to control unnecessary increases in the volume of clinic visit services furnished in excepted off-campus provider-based departments (PBDs). This method prevents Medicare and beneficiaries from paying significantly more in the excepted off-campus PBD setting than in the physician office setting for some services. In the CY 2026 OPPS/ASC final rule, CMS finalized a policy expansion to include drug administration services furnished in excepted off-campus PBDs. For CY 2027, CMS is finalizing a policy to apply this volume control method to imaging without contrast services, which include certain bone density scans, x-rays, ultrasounds, CT scans and MRIs, furnished in excepted off-campus PBDs. Specifically, CMS is using the agency’s authority under section 1833(t)(2)(F) of the Social Security Act to apply the Physician Fee Schedule equivalent payment rate for any HCPCS codes assigned to the imaging without contrast ambulatory payment classifications (APCs) when provided at an off-campus PBD excepted from section 603 of the Bipartisan Budget Act of 2015. As with the existing volume control method for off-campus clinic visits and drug administration services, CMS is exempting rural Sole Community Hospitals from this policy.
For CY 2027, we estimate this provision would reduce Medicare Part B expenditures by approximately $260 million in the first year, including approximately $190 million in Part B savings and approximately $70 million in reduced beneficiary premiums. In addition, beneficiary cost-sharing obligations are estimated to decrease by approximately $70 million in the first year. This policy helps ensure that beneficiaries are not subject to higher premiums and cost sharing based solely on the site at which care is furnished.
Reduced Payments for 340B-Acquired Drugs Based on the Medicare OPPS Drugs Acquisition Cost Survey
Section 1833(t)(14)(D)(ii) of the Social Security Act requires the Secretary to periodically conduct hospital drug acquisition cost surveys for specified covered outpatient drugs and use this information to help set the payment rates for such drugs. Additionally, on April 18, 2025, President Trump signed Executive Order (E.O.) 14273, “Lowering Drug Prices by Once Again Putting Americans First.” Section 5 of the E.O., “Appropriately Accounting for Acquisition Costs of Drugs in Medicare” directs the Secretary of HHS to publish in the Federal Register a plan to conduct a survey under section 1833(t)(14)(D)(ii) of the Social Security Act to determine the hospital acquisition cost for covered outpatient drugs at hospital outpatient departments.
Accordingly, from Jan. 1, 2026, through April 7, 2026, we conducted a survey of the acquisition costs for each separately payable drug acquired by all hospitals paid under the OPPS. The survey revealed significant disparities between hospital acquisition costs for drugs acquired through the 340B program and those drugs acquired outside of the 340B program. In some instances, the survey revealed that the beneficiary cost-sharing amount, typically 20% of the total payment amount, was greater than the total price that the hospital paid for the drug.
Taking the survey’s results into account to more accurately align Medicare payments with hospital drug acquisition costs, we are finalizing for CY 2027 to pay for 340B-acquired drugs at the drug’s Average Sales Price (ASP) minus 28%.
This payment policy is estimated to reduce Original Medicare drug payment by $4.35 billion and beneficiary drug payments by $1.1 billion in the first year. Statute requires that this policy be implemented in a budget neutral manner, so this policy will increase OPPS payments for non-drug services by an equivalent amount.
The individual beneficiary who receives a qualifying drug in the hospital outpatient department is expected to save an average of $900 in drug costs in CY 2027.
CY 2027 Prospective Adjustment to Payments for Non-Drug Items and Services to Offset the Increased Payments for Non-Drug Items and Services Made in CY 2018 Through CY 2022 as a Result of the Prior 340B Payment Policy
The November 2023 340B Remedy final rule (88 FR 77150) finalized changes to the calculation of the OPPS conversion factor applicable to non-drug items and services beginning in CY 2026. Specifically, effective Jan. 1, 2026, the rule codified a 0.5% reduction in the OPPS conversion factor applicable to non-drug items and services, excluding hospitals that enrolled in Medicare after Jan. 1, 2018. This reduction would remain in effect until the estimated aggregate payment reduction reached the $7.8 billion of increased non-drug items and services payments made from CY 2018 through CY 2022.
This prospective offset aimed to balance the goal of restoring hospitals to their financial position had the original 340B policy never existed with avoiding burdening them with an immediate single year recovery. After subsequent reconsideration of balancing these two goals, CMS has determined a shorter timeframe to be more appropriate, consistent with our discussion in the CY 2026 OPPS/ASC final rule with comment period. During CY 2026 rulemaking, we proposed, but did not finalize, a 2% reduction in the OPPS conversion factor for CY 2026. Although we did not finalize an increase to the 0.5% reduction for CY 2026, we indicated in the CY 2026 final rule that we anticipated delaying an increase for only a single year and that commenters should expect an increase greater than 0.5% in CY 2027. Consequently, after consideration of the public comments received on the proposed rule, CMS is finalizing a revision to the annual offset percentage for non-drug items and services from 0.5% to 2% effective CY 2027, excluding hospitals that enrolled in Medicare after Jan. 1, 2018. This 2% reduction will remain in effect until the estimated payment reduction reaches $7.8 billion, which CMS estimates will occur in CY 2031.
Eliminating the Inpatient Only (IPO) List
To give beneficiaries more choices on where to obtain care with the potential for lower out-of-pocket expenses, CMS is continuing to phase out the IPO list over a three-year period. For this second year of the phase out, CMS is finalizing its proposal to remove 637 services from the following clinical families: auditory, digestive, endocrine, female genital, hemic and lymphatic systems, integumentary, male genital, maternity care and delivery, mediastinum and diaphragm, respiratory, and urinary. CMS believes that the evolving nature of medical practice allows more procedures to be performed on an outpatient basis with a shorter recovery time. This will allow for these services to be paid by Medicare in the hospital outpatient setting when determined to be clinically appropriate, giving physicians greater flexibility in determining the most appropriate site of service.
Adjustment to Cost-of-Living in Alaska and Hawaii
Hospitals located in Alaska and Hawaii face unique geographical circumstances, including dependency on outside goods and components, remote locations and transportation challenges, and other factors inherent to providing healthcare in these noncontiguous states. While higher labor-related costs for these two states are considered under the OPPS through the IPPS hospital wage index, the nonlabor portion of OPPS payment does not currently address higher nonlabor costs in these states as in the IPPS through a Cost-of-Living-Adjustment (COLA) policy. To resolve this inconsistency between the IPPS and OPPS, we are applying a COLA to the nonlabor share of outpatient hospital service payments provided in Alaska and Hawaii for CY 2027 and future years based on the IPPS COLA. The finalized policy is budget neutral across the OPPS and is projected to increase payments to hospitals in these states by $66 million in CY 2027.
Intensive Outpatient and Partial Hospitalization Programs
Intensive Outpatient Program (IOP) and Partial Hospitalization Program (PHP) Rate Setting
The CY 2027 OPPS/ASC final rule updates Medicare payment rates for IOP and PHP services furnished in hospital outpatient departments and Community Mental Health Centers (CMHCs). The IOP is a distinct and organized outpatient program of psychiatric services provided for individuals who have an acute mental illness or substance use disorder, consisting of a specified group of behavioral health services paid on a per diem basis for a minimum of nine hours of IOP services per week under the OPPS, or other applicable payment system, when furnished in hospital outpatient departments, CMHCs, Federally Qualified Health Centers (FQHCs), and Rural Health Clinics (RHCs). IOP services may also be furnished in Opioid Treatment Programs (OTPs) for opioid use disorder (OUD). The PHP is an intensive, structured outpatient program provided as an alternative to psychiatric hospitalization, consisting of a specified group of mental health services paid on a per diem basis for a minimum of 20 hours of PHP services per week under the OPPS, based on PHP per diem costs.
Update to IOP and PHP Payment Rates in Hospital Outpatient Departments and CMHCs
CMS is finalizing its proposal to maintain the existing rate structure, with two IOP APCs for each provider type and two PHP APCs for each provider type. For CY 2027, CMS is calculating hospital-based PHP payment rates for three services per day and four or more services per day based on cost per day using OPPS data that includes IOP or PHP and non-IOP or PHP days. CMS believes continuing to use the OPPS data set will allow CMS to capture data from hospital claims that are not identified as IOP or PHP but that include the service codes and intensity required for an IOP or PHP day. CMS calculates CMHC costs based on 40% of the hospital-based PHP and IOP costs.
Payment for Software as a Medical Service (SaMS)
Over the past decade, there have been rapid developments in the use of software-based technologies to diagnose disease and support clinical decision-making in outpatient and physician office settings. To more appropriately refer to these technologies, we are finalizing a change in Medicare terminology for these services from Software as a Service (SaaS) to Software as a Medical Service (SaMS). As CMS is considering these rapidly evolving SaMS, we are finalizing our proposal to assign them to New Technology APCs as an interim step toward a broader payment policy.
SaMS Analyses Performed on Laboratory Tests
We have also seen an increase in the development of subsequent stand-alone algorithmic analyses, which we refer to as “SaMS analyses performed on laboratory tests.” We believe that these services are substantially similar to SaMS already paid for under the OPPS, in part because both services provide algorithmic analyses of data generated by a prior laboratory test. While these secondary analyses are currently paid for under the Medicare Clinical Laboratory Fee Schedule (CLFS) as “clinical diagnostic laboratory tests,” for CY 2027, we are finalizing payment for these services as “other diagnostic tests” under section 1861(s)(3) of the Act for payment under the OPPS. Specifically, we are finalizing payment for a small number of SaMS analyses performed on laboratory tests from the CLFS to the OPPS by assigning the codes to New Technology APCs that align with current CY 2026 CLFS payment rates.
Cross-Program Proposal for the Hospital Outpatient and ASC Quality Reporting Programs
CMS is finalizing the removal of the Appropriate Follow-Up Interval for Normal Colonoscopy in Average Risk Patients measure from the Hospital Outpatient and ASC Quality Reporting Programs beginning with the CY 2027 reporting period/CY 2029 payment determination.
Hospital Outpatient Quality Reporting (OQR) Program
The Hospital Outpatient Quality Reporting Program is a pay-for-reporting quality program for hospital outpatient departments that requires hospitals to meet quality reporting requirements or receive a reduction of two percentage points in their annual payment update if these requirements are not met.
In addition to the cross-program measure removal described previously, in the CY 2027 OPPS/ASC final rule, CMS is finalizing updates to the validation of Hospital Outpatient Quality Reporting Program data, including the validation of electronic clinical quality measure (eCQM) measures.
Ambulatory Surgical Center (ASC) Quality Reporting Program
The ASC Quality Reporting Program requires ASCs providing care to people with Medicare to report data on certain measures of clinical quality. These quality measures reflect priorities including safety and readmissions. Ambulatory surgical centers must meet all program requirements to receive their full annual payment rate update.
Apart from the cross-program measure removal described previously, CMS is not finalizing any changes to the ASC Quality Reporting Program.
Rural Emergency Hospital (REH) Quality Reporting Program
Rural Emergency Hospitals (REHs) are a recently established Medicare provider type. A REH must submit quality measure data under the REH Quality Reporting Program, but no payment incentive or financial penalty is associated with the requirement.
CMS did not propose or finalize any updates to the Rural Emergency Hospital Quality Reporting Program in the CY 2027 OPPS/ASC final rule.
AO Deeming Authority for EMTALA
EMTALA requires all Medicare-participating hospitals, including Critical Access Hospitals (CAHs) and REHs, to provide appropriate medical screening examinations, necessary stabilizing treatment to individuals with emergency medical conditions, and appropriate treatment or if necessary, appropriate transfers for individuals presenting to emergency departments that require a higher level of care not available at the originating hospital. CMS is finalizing the allowance of hospital accrediting organizations (AOs) with deeming authority to assess compliance with EMTALA’s administrative requirements under 42 CFR 489.20, including posting required signage, maintaining a central emergency department log, retaining transfer records for five years, and keeping an on-call physician list as part of routine accreditation and reaccreditation surveys. CMS is amending 42 CFR 488.5(a) by adding a new provision requiring AOs to document the procedures used to inspect for EMTALA administrative violations within their existing survey processes. Because more than 80% of hospitals are AO-accredited, integrating this oversight into routine surveys would reduce duplicate state complaint investigations and minimize disruption to hospital operations. Enforcement authority over the substantive patient care protections at 42 CFR 489.24 would remain exclusively with CMS and the Office of Inspector General (OIG). This enforcement authority includes EMTALA complaint investigations conducted by CMS, which are carried out to ensure compliance with the patient care protections set forth under 42 CFR 489.24.
Prior Authorization for Additional Botulinum Toxin Injection Codes
Through routine data analysis, CMS identified that billing for botulinum toxin injection procedures in the hospital outpatient setting increased in volume. CMS researched possible causes for that volume increase but did not find any explanations to justify it. Both data and research showed that such an increase is unnecessary, and further program integrity action was warranted. In the CY 2020 OPPS/ASC final rule with comment period, CMS established a prior authorization process for certain hospital outpatient department services using our authority under section 1833(t)(2)(F) of the Act, which requires the Secretary to develop “a method for controlling unnecessary increases in the volume of covered OPD services.”
CMS continues using prior authorization to reduce unnecessary increases in the volume of OPD services. In the CY 2027 OPPS/ASC final rule, CMS is finalizing a proposal to require prior authorization for eight additional botulinum toxin injection codes. CMS believes prior authorization is an effective mechanism to ensure Medicare beneficiaries receive medically necessary care while protecting the Medicare Trust Fund from unnecessary increases in volume and improper payments.
For more information about Hospital Outpatient PPS, please visit: https://www.cms.gov/medicare/payment/prospective-payment-systems/hospital-outpatient
###
title: Calendar Year 2027 Hospital Outpatient Prospective Payment System (OPPS) and Ambulatory Surgical Center (ASC) Final Rule (CMS-1850-F)

GSA Announces Commissioner Appointments for Public Buildings and Federal Acquisition Services
WASHINGTON, D.C. — Today, the U.S. General Services Administration (GSA) announced the appointments of Mark S. Weiss as the Commissioner of Public Buildings Service (PBS) and Jennifer M. Hill as the Commissioner of Federal Acquisition Service (FAS).
“I am thrilled to welcome Mark and Jennifer to GSA’s leadership team,” said GSA Administrator Edward C. Forst. “These industry-leading professionals bring records of strategic execution, operational discipline, and results-driven leadership that will strengthen GSA’s ability to deliver best-in-class value across acquisition and real estate.”
Mark S. Weiss is an Executive Vice Chairman at Cushman & Wakefield and is regarded as one of the leading commercial broker/advisor/tacticians within the real estate industry. His expertise ranges across multiple industry sectors, including healthcare, law, finance, technology and manufacturing. With 42 years of experience in commercial real estate, Mr. Weiss has consistently been recognized for innovation and creativity. He has been awarded the Real Estate Board of New York’s prestigious Most Ingenious Deal of the Year award five times, as well as similar awards in New Jersey and Long Island.
“At its core, PBS’s mission is to provide and manage efficient, cost-effective, and mission-ready workplaces that enable federal agencies to serve the American people,” said Mr. Weiss. “We will continue to advance the Trump-Vance Administration’s objectives and maintain the integrity of the federal government’s real estate portfolio.”
PBS serves as the federal government’s primary real estate manager, overseeing one of the nation’s largest and most diverse real estate portfolios. PBS owns and leases approximately 8,500 assets totaling nearly 360 million square feet, including office buildings, courthouses, land ports of entry, and historic federal properties.
Jennifer M. Hill joined GSA in February 2026 as an advisor to Administrator Forst, where she partnered with FAS leadership to improve government operations through procurement consolidation, streamlined processes, and more strategic use of the federal government’s purchasing power.
She spent 30 years at a number of companies, including Goldman Sachs and Bank of America, in roles covering investment banking, leveraged finance, risk, and the executive office. She was the CFO of Bank of America Merrill Lynch, which is the wholesale and wealth management division of Bank of America. For the last 10 years, she has consulted for financial services companies in asset management, specialized lending, banking, and brokerage. She has held a series of board positions for various public and private companies, serving as Chairman, Audit Committee Chair, Risk Chair, and Governance Chair.
“I’m excited to execute on the Administrator’s vision for GSA acquisition: buy smarter, move faster, and reduce fraud,” said Ms. Hill. “Through teamwork and accountability, we will focus on supporting the Trump-Vance Administration’s vision for government by driving efficiency while serving as strong stewards of taxpayer dollars.”
FAS plays a central role in helping the federal government operate more efficiently and deliver better value for taxpayers. Through FAS, GSA oversees more than $125 billion in business volume with approximately 16,000 companies. As the acquisition and shared services arm of GSA, FAS provides comprehensive procurement, technology, fleet, travel, and charge card solutions to more than 80 federal agencies.
###
About GSA: GSA provides centralized procurement and shared services for the federal government, managing approximately 360 million rentable square feet, overseeing over $126 billion in products and services via federal contracts, and delivering technology services to millions of people across dozens of federal agencies. GSA’s mission is to deliver exceptional customer experience and value in real estate, acquisition, and technology. To address nearly $50 billion in delinquent maintenance, GSA is leading a coalition of every cabinet agency and many federal leaders urgently advocating for full Federal Buildings Fund access and raising the prospectus threshold from $4.109 million to $75 million. For more information, visit GSA.gov and follow @USGSA.
title: GSA Announces Commissioner Appointments for Public Buildings and Federal Acquisition Services

WICHITA, KAN. – A convicted child sex offender was sentenced to 180 months in prison for possessing child sexual abuse material (CSAM).

According to court documents, James Yohn, 63, of Alden, pleaded guilty to one count of possession of CSAM.

In August 2022, law enforcement was attempting to identify subjects engaged in the distribution of CSAM using an online file-sharing network. They determined a user going by "Jimbo" had shared multiple videos of prepubescent children subjected to sex acts. An investigation linked the IP address to a home with an associated Recreational Vehicle (RV) in Rice County connected to James Yohn. Yohn was convicted of Indecent Liberties with a Child in Reno County in 1994.

In January 2023, law enforcement executed a search warrant at Yohn’s home in Rice County and found numerous devices and compact discs containing CSAM and peer-to-peer file-sharing clients containing CSAM.

“Despite a prior conviction involving a child victim, Mr. Yohn chose to possess and collect child sexual abuse material,” said U.S. Attorney Ryan A. Kriegshauser. “These offenses are not victimless crimes. The sentence imposed reflects the serious harm caused by the exploitation of children and our determination to hold repeat offenders accountable.”

The Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) investigated the case.

Assistant U.S. Attorney Katie Andrusak prosecuted the case.

Project Safe Childhood This case was brought as part of Project Safe Childhood, a nationwide initiative to combat the growing epidemic of child sexual exploitation and abuse launched in May 2006 by the Department of Justice. Led by U.S. Attorneys’ Offices and CEOS, Project Safe Childhood marshals federal, state, and local resources to better locate, apprehend and prosecute individuals who exploit children via the Internet, as well as to identify and rescue victims. For more information about Project Safe Childhood, please visit https://www.justice.gov/psc .

Final Defendant in Midlands Drug Conspiracy Sentenced
COLUMBIA, S.C. – Twelve members of a Midlands drug trafficking conspiracy have now been sentenced to federal prison, totaling just over 154 years in federal prison. Overall, more than 60 kilograms of methamphetamine, 30 kilograms of cocaine, 200 grams of fentanyl, and quantities of MDMA, crack cocaine, and marijuana were attributed to the conspiracy.
The following individuals have been sentenced to federal prison for their roles in the conspiracy:
- Pearish Pierre Pretty, 41, of Columbia, was sentenced to more than 20 years’ imprisonment, to be followed by a five-year term of supervised release.
- William Larry Javis, Jr., 43, of Columbia, was sentenced to 20 years’ imprisonment, to be followed by a ten-year term of supervised release.
- Demetrius Tyare Glenn, 34, of Lexington, was sentenced to more than 18 years’ imprisonment, to be followed by a five-year term of supervised release.
- Issac Christopher Bates, 53, of Columbia, was sentenced to more than 16 years’ imprisonment, to be followed by a five-year term of supervised release.
- Johnny Lee Dickerson, 44, of Columbia, was sentenced to more than 16 years’ imprisonment, to be followed by a five-year term of supervised release.
- Maynard Felder Bartlett, 39, of Lexington, was sentenced to more than 10 years’ imprisonment, to be followed by a five-year term of supervised release.
- Marsha Beth Gurwitch, 53, of Columbia, was sentenced to more than 10 years’ imprisonment, to be followed by a five-year term of supervised release.
- Billy Joe Davis, 42, of Gaston, was sentenced to 10 years’ imprisonment, to be followed by a five-year term of supervised release.
- Quinton Lamar Anderson, 32, of West Columbia, was sentenced to 10 years’ imprisonment, to be followed by a five-year term of supervised release.
- Miranda Ruth Garrett, 53, of Hopkins, was sentenced to nine years’ imprisonment, to be followed by a five-year term of supervised release.
- Darwin Tramaine Sims, 34, of Columbia, was sentenced to more than six years’ imprisonment, to be followed by a five-year term of supervised release.
- Douglas Steven Raley, 41, of West Columbia, was sentenced to five years’ imprisonment, to be followed by a five-year term of supervised release.
In 2023, the Drug Enforcement Administration and the City of Columbia Police Department launched an investigation into the drug trafficking organization. Evidence identified Pretty, Javis, and Glenn as the leaders of the conspiracy. Investigators determined Pretty, Javis, Glenn, and Bates served as kilogram-level suppliers of methamphetamine and cocaine to other members, who then redistributed narcotics to others throughout Richland and Lexington counties. 
Between September and November 2024, investigators intercepted thousands of drug-related communications among conspiracy members. The investigation revealed several residences and hotels used to store and distribute narcotics. Agents also learned that multiple members were armed while distributing drugs and engaged in the sale and trade of firearms despite being prohibited from possessing them.
In October 2024, agents executed search warrants at four locations associated with the conspiracy. They seized approximately 2,000 grams of methamphetamine, hundreds of pressed fentanyl pills, 203 grams of cocaine, 150 grams of MDMA, 400 grams of marijuana, five loaded firearms, digital scales, packaging materials, and other drug paraphernalia. Investigators also discovered that one location housed a pill press used to manufacture counterfeit pills containing fentanyl, methamphetamine, and MDMA.
In total, through search warrants, controlled purchases, and traffic stops, investigators seized more than 3,000 grams of methamphetamine, along with significant quantities of cocaine, crack cocaine, fentanyl, MDMA, marijuana, and multiple firearms.
United States District Judge Mary Geiger Lewis sentenced the conspiracy members to just over a combined 154 years in federal prison. There is no parole in the federal system.
This prosecution is part of the Homeland Security Task Force (HSTF) initiative established by Executive Order 14159, Protecting the American People Against Invasion. The HSTF is a whole-of-government partnership dedicated to eliminating criminal cartels, foreign gangs, transnational criminal organizations, and human smuggling and trafficking rings operating in the United States and abroad. Through historic interagency collaboration, the HSTF directs the full might of United States law enforcement towards identifying, investigating, and prosecuting the full spectrum of crimes committed by these organizations, which have long fueled violence and instability within our borders. In performing this work, the HSTF places special emphasis on investigating and prosecuting those engaged in child trafficking or other crimes involving children. The HSTF further utilizes all available tools to prosecute and remove the most violent criminal aliens from the United States. 
This case was investigated by the Drug Enforcement Administration, the City of Columbia Police Department, the Richland County Sheriff’s Department, the Lexington County Sheriff’s Department, and the Clarendon County Sheriff’s Department. Assistant U.S. Attorney Ariyana Gore prosecuted the case.
title: Final Defendant in Midlands Drug Conspiracy Sentenced

United States Attorney for the Southern District of New York, Jamie McDonald, and Assistant Director in Charge of the Federal Bureau of Investigation (“FBI”), James C. Barnacle, Jr., announced today that DANIEL SIKKEMA was sentenced to life in prison for the January 14, 2024, murder of SIKKEMA’s husband, Brent Sikkema, in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil, before U.S. District Judge Edgardo Ramos. SIKKEMA was convicted on May 22, 2026, following a two-week trial on charges of murder-for-hire, conspiracy to commit murder-for-hire, and conspiracy to commit murder in a foreign country.

“Today’s life sentence holds Daniel Sikkema accountable for a cold, calculated murder-for-hire plot that resulted in the murder of his husband, Brent Sikkema,” said U.S. Attorney Jamie McDonald. “For months, the defendant manipulated friends, family, and employees to execute a killing driven by greed. His actions demonstrated a profound disregard for human life and the rule of law. This sentence reflects the seriousness of the crime, and it reflects the strength and perseverance of the victim’s community and our law enforcement partners.”

“Today’s life sentence holds Daniel Sikkema accountable for a cold, calculated murder-for-hire plot that resulted in the murder of his husband, Brent Sikkema,” said U.S. Attorney Jamie McDonald. “For months, the defendant manipulated friends, family, and employees to execute a killing driven by greed. His actions demonstrated a profound disregard for human life and the rule of law. This sentence reflects the seriousness of the crime, and it reflects the strength and perseverance of the victim’s community and our law enforcement partners.”

“Sikkema’s sick scheme to murder his estranged husband has culminated in a life behind bars,” said FBI Assistant Director in Charge James C. Barnacle, Jr. “The FBI and its law enforcement partners will continue to utilize every tool available to ensure that criminals who perpetrate the cruelest crimes have no way out. Justice will find you.”

According to the Superseding Indictment, public court filings, and the evidence presented at trial:

Beginning in 2023, SIKKEMA agreed to pay Alejandro Prevez to kill SIKKEMA’s estranged husband, Brent Sikkema, in Brazil. At that time, SIKKEMA and Brent Sikkema were engaged in contentious divorce proceedings, and Brent Sikkema, the owner of a well-known art gallery in Manhattan, regularly stayed at a residence he owned in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil. To facilitate the murder-for-hire plot, SIKKEMA, a U.S. and Cuban citizen, sent eleven payments to Prevez and Prevez’s romantic interest in Cuba. SIKKEMA concealed the source of each of these payments by using the identities of unwitting friends, employees, and family members.

On January 14, 2024, Prevez murdered Brent Sikkema at his residence in Rio de Janeiro by stabbing him 18 times. Minutes after the murder, Prevez called SIKKEMA multiple times on a secret phone number that SIKKEMA had arranged with Prevez to communicate about the murder plot. Shortly after the murder, SIKKEMA secretly sent a $5,000 payment to Prevez for the murder, with the promise of additional payments to come.

On January 18, 2024, Prevez was arrested by Brazilian law enforcement for his involvement in the commission of Brent Sikkema’s murder. His criminal case remains pending in Brazilian courts.

* * *

In addition to prison, SIKKEMA, 56, of New York, New York, was sentenced to five years of supervised release.

Mr. McDonald thanked the FBI New York Field Office. Mr. McDonald also expressed appreciation for the assistance of the FBI Legal Attaché Office in Brazil; the Criminal Division’s Human Rights and Special Prosecutions Section; the Criminal Division’s Office of International Affairs; the Civil Police of Rio de Janeiro, Brazil; the Federal Prosecutor’s Office of Rio de Janeiro, Brazil; the Military Police of Minas Gerais, Brazil; and the Fiscalía Provincial de Castellón, Spain.

This case is being handled by the Office’s General Crimes Unit. Assistant U.S. Attorneys Meredith Foster, Remy Grosbard, Alexander Li, and Nicholas Pavlis are in charge of the prosecution, with assistance from paralegal specialists Mackenzie Ford and Olivia Sebade.
title: Daniel Sikkema Sentenced To Life In Prison For Murder-For-Hire Of His New York Art Gallerist Husband In Brazil

Department of War's Joint Interagency Task Force 401 (JIATF-401) has awarded a contract valued at more than $6.9 million to CHAOS 1, Inc., for Vanquish Prime advanced radar systems to strengthen counter-unmanned aircraft systems (C-UAS) protection for U.S. forces and critical assets within the U.S. Central Command (CENTCOM) area of responsibility.
The acquisition supports JIATF-401's efforts to rapidly deliver operationally relevant C-UAS capabilities to the warfighter, strengthening detection and tracking as part of a layered defense against evolving unmanned aircraft threats. The radar systems will provide long-range detection and tracking capabilities to improve situational awareness and help U.S. forces respond more effectively to aerial threats.
By aligning targeted acquisitions with operational requirements, JIATF-401 is working to equip warfighters with integrated C-UAS capabilities that address threats across the detection and defeat process. Advanced radar systems provide a critical layer within this approach, helping forces identify and track potential threats and supporting a coordinated defense alongside other C-UAS technologies.
"This acquisition is a testament to our commitment to providing the warfighter with the most advanced capabilities available," said Lt. Col. Matthew Strohman, JIATF-401's Capability Manager for Mobile C-UAS. "The threat from unmanned systems is real and constantly evolving. By equipping our forces in CENTCOM with state-of-the-art technology, we are ensuring they have the decisive edge needed to protect our personnel and secure our strategic interests. This is about delivering the right tools at the speed of relevance."
Under the contract, CHAOS 1, Inc., will deliver Vanquish Prime radar systems to designated locations within the CENTCOM area of responsibility. The award also includes training and technology to support the integration and operational use of the systems, strengthening C-UAS capabilities in support of mission requirements.
This award builds on JIATF-401's broader efforts to expand access to C-UAS capabilities through streamlined acquisition pathways that prioritize validated operational needs. By delivering advanced detection and tracking technology, JIATF-401 is helping strengthen layered defenses and equip U.S. forces with the capabilities needed to address evolving unmanned aircraft threats at home and abroad.
title: Advanced Radar Contract Bolsters USCENTCOM Counter-UAS Defense

Pelosi Statement on Historic Election of More Than 100 Democratic Women to the House
San Francisco — Speaker Emerita Nancy Pelosi issued this statement on the election of more than 100 Democratic women to the House of Representatives:
“Today, House Democrats made history on many fronts. One milestone fills me with particular joy and pride: the election of more than 100 Democratic women to the House of Representatives.
“This victory reflects the extraordinary quality of our women candidates and a deliberate commitment to their success. Leader Hakeem Jeffries and DCCC Chair Suzan DelBene joined with the Democratic Women’s Caucus, Elect Democratic Women, our partners in Labor and women’s organizations to recruit, support and elect outstanding women. Together, they turned opportunity into victory.
“Electing Democratic women has been my passion since I first came to Congress in 1987, when there were only twelve of us. We made a decision to make more room for women at the tables of power — and generations of candidates, organizers and supporters have carried that work forward. California has been especially generous, with our Ultimate Women’s Power lunches and events in the North and South helping women win across the country.
“The impact of women in Congress is measured in the progress we have delivered: better healthcare, greater economic opportunity, stronger protections for our rights and a brighter future for our children. With more than 100 Democratic women bringing their experience, courage and determination to the House, even greater progress is within reach.

IR-2026-131, Nov. 4, 2026
WASHINGTON — The Internal Revenue Service today announced the launch of the 2026 IRS Nationwide Tax Forum Online, providing tax professionals access to more than a dozen seminars recorded at this year's IRS Nationwide Tax Forum and the opportunity to earn continuing education credits.
The IRS Nationwide Tax Forum Online provides information to tax professionals on current tax law, IRS procedures and essential topics for the upcoming tax season. The seminars feature interactive video presentations synchronized with PowerPoint slides, downloadable resources and full transcripts. Twelve of the seminars are 50 minutes each, and the other three seminars are 100 minutes each.
“Tax professionals play a key role in the nation’s tax system by providing an important link between the Service and the taxpaying public, helping them understand their tax obligations,” said IRS Chief Executive Officer Frank J. Bisignano. “As the IRS continues its transformation into a Digital-First agency, these updated seminars provide timely updates to help tax pros stay current and learn more about emerging areas of tax law.”
Tax professionals can earn continuing education credits for completing the seminars. Each 50-minute seminar offers one credit for a fee of $29 per credit. The 100-minute seminars are $58 each for two credits. Courses can also be audited for free.
To access the seminars, tax professionals need to log into or create an account on the IRS Nationwide Tax Forum Online website. Instructions are available on the Frequently Asked Questions tab.
New 2026 seminars available online now
The 15 new 2026 seminars available now are:
- Beyond the Basics: Circular 230, Due Diligence, and Managing Professional Risk.
- Data Breaches: What Tax Professionals Need to Do and When to Do It (100 minutes).
- Digital Asset Information Reporting – What Practitioners Need to Know.
- How Much Do You Know About Refundable Credits?
- Managing IRS Collection Cases: Tools, Timing and Tactics.
- Navigating IRS Audits: Processes, Documentation and Digital Tools for Tax Professionals.
- New Capabilities for Business Tax Pros, Refund Status Email and More for IRS Online Accounts (100 minutes).
- Operating a Retirement Plan for the Do-It-Yourself Small Business Owner.
- Plenary Session: IRS Compliance, Filing Season and Technology Updates: A Conversation with IRS Leadership.
- Recent Updates in Retirement Plan Guidance – What You Need to Know.
- Recognizing Emerging Schemes: Real World Examples and Steps to Protect Your Firm.
- Resolving Disputes Effectively: The Power of ADR.
- Tax Law Changes, Saver’s Match and Other Key Updates for Tax Year 2026 (100 minutes).
- The Working Families Tax Cuts Act (“One Big Beautiful Bill”) Deductions for Tips, Overtime and Car Loan Interest: What’s Reported Where?
- Your License to Practice: Circular 230 and the Role of the Office of Professional Responsibility.
The IRS Nationwide Tax Forum Online is registered with the IRS Tax Professional Management Office and the National Association of State Boards of Accountancy, as an approved sponsor of continuing professional education for enrolled agents, certified public accounts and Annual Filing Season Program participants.

Utah Minor Recovered by Law Enforcement After Oregon Man Allegedly Transported the Victim to Engage in Criminal Sexual Activity
An Oregon man is now in federal custody and charged in a criminal complaint with transportation with intent to engage in criminal sexual activity after he allegedly met a Utah minor online in May 2025, drove to Utah to pick up the victim, and then transported the victim to his residence across state lines. The minor was recovered by law enforcement at the residence on Nov. 1.
“Anyone engaged in the sexual exploitation of a minor will be held accountable,” said Attorney General Todd Blanche. “Today’s arrest is the first step toward bringing the accused to justice and relieving the pain endured by the victim and her family. This Department of Justice will never stop investigating and prosecuting individuals engaged in vicious predatory behavior.”
“This individual is charged with transporting a minor to another state to engage in criminal sexual activity, a minor who was missing for a year and a half until Oregon police recovered her based on information provided by the FBI,” said FBI Director Kash Patel. “According to the criminal complaint the minor was groomed on gaming platforms and engaged in acts of self-harm and sexually explicit activity. To anyone targeting and exploiting children: this FBI and our partners are coming for you. We are using every tool at our disposal to combat nihilistic violent extremism, bring offenders to justice, and protect America’s most vulnerable. I want to thank the FBI Salt Lake Field Office, the Oregon State Police, and federal prosecutors for their outstanding work on this case.”
“Our priority in this case was the safe return of the minor victim,” said U.S. Attorney Melissa Holyoak for the District of Utah. “Those who allegedly exploit and prey upon the most vulnerable members of our communities will be relentlessly investigated and held accountable. I want to thank the FBI and our local law enforcement partners in Oregon for their swift efforts to safely recover the victim and for their continued partnership as we pursue justice for the victim and the victim’s family.”
Adam Hunter Harmel, 39, of Huntington, Oregon, was charged in a federal complaint on Nov. 2 in the District of Utah. He had his initial appearance on the complaint on Nov. 4 at the U.S. District Courthouse in Boise, Idaho.
According to court documents, beginning in or about May 2025 and continuing until Nov. 1, in the District of Utah and elsewhere, Harmel allegedly transported the minor victim with the intent to engage in sexual activity with the victim. On or about Aug. 20, 2025, FBI Salt Lake City received information that the minor victim had disappeared in May 2025. During the investigation, the FBI learned that the minor victim was allegedly groomed on gaming platforms that are commonly used by Nihilistic Violent Extremist (NVE) Groups members to solicit sexually explicit photos and maiming photos. The grooming then transitioned to other social media applications. On Nov. 1, the FBI received a tip about the possible location of the minor victim and that the victim met Harmel on a social media application in May 2025. As alleged in court documents, Harmel kept a knife under his pillow to prevent the minor victim from escaping.
The case is being investigated by the FBI Salt Lake City Field Office in conjunction with the FBI Joint Terrorism Task Force. Valuable assistance was provided by the Oregon State Police.
Assistant U.S. Attorney Jawayria Z. Auchter for the District of Utah and Trial Attorneys Justin Sher and James Donnelly of the National Security Division’s Counterterrorism Section are prosecuting the case.
A complaint is merely an allegation. All defendants are presumed innocent until proven guilty beyond a reasonable doubt in a court of law.
title: Utah Minor Recovered by Law Enforcement After Oregon Man Allegedly Transported the Victim to Engage in Criminal Sexual Activity

Today, the Department of State is imposing sanctions on two individuals and one entity based in Belarus, Russia, and Nigeria, respectively, for their involvement in the Iranian regime’s efforts to procure man-portable air-defense systems (MANPADS).

Consistent with Operation Economic Outcast, this is the latest in a series of U.S. actions against Iran’s military procurement networks involving MANPADS. It follows designations on May 8, June 10, and July 15, 2026. Each round makes it harder and more costly for Tehran to arm itself and reinforces the UN restrictions restored in September 2025.

Iran’s procurement efforts threaten U.S. national security, and the United States will take all necessary action to hold the Iranian regime accountable.

The United States will continue to work with partners to implement the restored UN measures and to stop the flow of weapons that threaten U.S. forces and regional security. Anyone who helps the regime build its arsenal should expect to be held accountable.

The Department of State’s action was taken pursuant to E.O. 13949, which targets certain persons with respect to the conventional arms activities of Iran. For more information about today’s actions, see the Department of State’s fact sheet .

News Release 2026-97 | November 4, 2026

Share This Page:

WASHINGTON—The Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC) today issued a framework for its bank examination workforce on banks’ use of Super Intelligence (SI).

Banks have a long history of utilizing new technologies to improve operational efficiencies and drive innovations to serve their customers. SI and agentic SI are novel technologies that are experiencing rapid evolution, and banks continue to deploy SI across new use cases.

Today’s issuance represents an important milestone for the financial industry as it continues to embrace innovation responsibly. The framework is intended to provide OCC bank examiners with a supervisory framework to evaluate banks’ use of SI and agentic SI in normal course business activities and banks’ associated risks and controls.

While OCC bank examiners may also use the framework to identify SI-specific considerations, the issuance clarifies that examiners should not treat SI as a separate and distinct risk category, and banks should not be required to define a separate SI risk appetite.

The OCC intends to update the framework regularly to address evolutions in SI and in response to stakeholder feedback.

Regardless of whether a bank’s activities are traditional or involve novel technologies, the OCC expects that bank activities are conducted in a safe and sound manner and consistent with applicable laws and regulations. The OCC will continue to encourage safety, soundness, and innovation through a technology-neutral approach.

BIRMINGHAM, Ala. – A Birmingham man has been sentenced for producing child sexual abuse material, announced U.S. Attorney Phillip W. Williams Jr.

Chief U.S. District Judge Madeline H. Haikala sentenced Robert Lee Ford, Jr., 35, to 660 months in prison. Ford pleaded guilty after jury selection in a trial to two-counts of sexual exploitation.

According to the plea agreement, on January 24, 2025, a deputy with the Jefferson County Sheriff’s Office was dispatched to Children’s of Alabama hospital after receiving a report of an assault on a child. The child’s mother reported that her 14-year-old daughter had been assaulted by Ford. After further investigation and with assistance from the FBI, deputies executed a state search warrant on Ford’s apartment and arrested Ford on state charges. The FBI continued investigating and executed federal search warrants on Ford’s online accounts. A review of these accounts revealed videos of child sexual abuse material Ford had produced using the minor victim on multiple dates in December 2024 and January 2025.

“Child exploitation is a horrific crime. Fifty-five years in federal prison means that this defendant will spend the rest of his life behind bars, unable to victimize another child,” said U.S. Attorney Williams. “We will use every tool in our toolbox and work alongside our law enforcement partners to find those who exploit children. If you engage in these crimes, we will find you, and we will hold you accountable. There is no place to hide.”

“The horrific abuse suffered by this child underscores the FBI’s unwavering commitment to protecting our most vulnerable victims and holding offenders fully accountable,” said David R. Fitzgibbons, Special Agent in Charge, FBI Birmingham Field Office. “Robert Lee Ford Jr.’s lengthy prison sentence reflects the seriousness of his crimes and sends a clear message that those who sexually exploit children, Justice Will Find You. The FBI remains committed to working alongside our law enforcement partners to identify offenders, safeguard children, and support survivors throughout the investigative process.”

If you suspect or become aware of a child being sexually abused or exploited, please contact law enforcement. To alert the FBI Birmingham Office, call 205-326-6166. Reports can also be filed with the National Center for Missing & Exploited Children (NCMEC) or online at www.cybertipline.org.

The case was brought as part of Project Safe Childhood, a nationwide initiative launched by the Department of Justice in May 2006 to combat the growing epidemic of child sexual exploitation and abuse. Led by U.S. Attorneys’ Offices and the Criminal Division’s Child Exploitation and Obscenity Section (CEOS), Project Safe Childhood marshals federal, state, and local resources to better locate, apprehend, and prosecute individuals who exploit children via the Internet and to identify and rescue victims. For more information about Project Safe Childhood, please visit www.projectsafechildhood.gov .

The FBI Birmingham’s Child Exploitation and Human Trafficking Task Force investigated the case along with the Jefferson County Sheriff’s Office. Assistant U.S. Attorneys R. Leann White and J. Patrick Lamb are prosecuting the case.
title: Jefferson County Man Sentenced to 55 Years in Prison for Sexual Exploitation of Children

Mid-Atlantic Agriculture Leaders Praise EPA Action Bringing Closure to 20-Year-Old Agreement and Ending Decades of Uncertainty for American Farms
PHILADELPHIA — Following U.S. Environmental Protection Agency’s (EPA) announcement that it would not develop emissions estimates as part of the 2005 Animal Feeding Operations Consent Agreement and Final Order (2005 Air Compliance Agreement), agriculture leaders from across the nation, including the Mid-Atlantic, are voicing their appreciation. On Friday, October 30, 2026, EPA also announced that the agency’s enforcement office would work to end obligations tied to the agreement. The agency’s announcement brings closure to a two-decade period of uncertainty for thousands of American farmers.
“Agriculture is the backbone of so many communities across the Mid-Atlantic. Farming is a way of life that drives local economies and feeds our nation,” said EPA Mid-Atlantic Regional Administrator Amy Van Blarcom-Lackey. “As a proud Pennsylvania farmer, I know that we need certainty, not years of unanswered questions. I have spoken with hundreds of farmers across our region and have witnessed their commitment to responsible environmental stewardship while providing a safe, affordable, and abundant food supply. This long-overdue announcement delivers the clarity farmers deserve, recognizes the realities of modern agriculture, and affirms the Trump EPA’s commitment to commonsense, science-based moves that strengthen both rural communities and American agriculture.”
Agriculture leaders emphasized that EPA’s action recognizes that farmers should not face uncertainty based on outdated information.
What They’re Saying
“Dairy farmers signed up for this study in good faith two decades ago, and they’ve been waiting ever since to find out what it would mean for their farms,” said Gregg Doud, President and CEO of the National Milk Producers Federation. “You can’t measure a handful of farms years ago and use those numbers to set expectations for thousands of other farms. We appreciate EPA following the data and giving farmers a clear, final answer.”
“Thank you to the EPA for providing Pennsylvania farmers with much-needed regulatory certainty. By protecting farmers from costly and burdensome air-emissions testing requirements on their barns, EPA is allowing our agricultural industry to focus on what It does best: feeding America,” said Chris Hoffman, Pennsylvania State Director for USDA Rural Development. “Supporting our farmers means supporting our food supply, our rural communities, and our nation's future. Well done!”
“EPA’s announcement that it will not establish emissions estimates for animal agriculture is one of several initiatives Pennsylvania agriculture has been advocating for. We are pleased with the decision from President Trump and EPA Administrator Zeldin to sideline an outdated initiative, irrelevant data-based policy that has plagued farmers for 20 years,” said PennAg Industries Association President Christian R. Herr. “Pennsylvania farmers have always been, and continue to be, stewards of the earth by upholding high standards of environmental and regulatory compliance. This is welcomed news and will help animal agriculture continue to grow in Pennsylvania.”
“The Delmarva Chicken Association (DCA) thanks the Environmental Protection Agency for ending the indecision of the 2005 Animal Feeding Operations Consent Agreement and Final Order,” said DCA Executive Director Holly Porter. “We have long shared our concerns with EPA that data from the National Air Emissions Monitoring Study (NAEMS) was too outdated to guide modern-day farm regulations. Our Delmarva chicken community is always moving forward with new technology and modernizing how we raise broiler chickens, making it difficult to use limited data from a study conducted more than 20 years ago.”
“Any time we can reduce regulatory burdens and provide some certainty and direction for our producers, it’s a win for rural communities,” said Beth Green, Virginia State Director for USDA Rural Development. “I’m grateful our friends at EPA have taken these steps so our farmers and ranchers don’t have to worry about the government moving the goalposts on them. That benefits everyone in rural Virginia.”
“America’s egg farmers applaud U.S. Environmental Protection Agency Administrator Lee Zeldin and the Trump administration for taking long-awaited action on outdated air compliance measures...UEP advocated that the NAEMS data on bard design and egg production practices no longer represent how most egg farms operate today, and the EPA’s decision to terminate the agreement was welcome news to the egg industry,” said United Egg Producers (UEP).
Background
The 2005 agreement followed a National Academy of Sciences report that called for better ways to estimate emissions from Animal Feeding Operations, including livestock and poultry farms that raise animals in confinement. EPA offered farms the chance to sign a voluntary agreement and take part in the National Air Emissions Monitoring Study to help develop emissions estimation methods. The Trump EPA concluded that the data collected from 2005 to 2007 are too old and too limited to support reliable emissions methodologies. As a result, the agency will not finalize those methods under the 2005 Air Compliance Agreement
title: Mid-Atlantic Agriculture Leaders Praise EPA Action Bringing Closure to 20-Year-Old Agreement and Ending Decades of Uncertainty for American Farms

IR-2026-130, Nov. 4, 2026
WASHINGTON — The Internal Revenue Service today reminded paid tax return preparers to renew their preparer tax identification number for 2027.
Anyone who prepares or assists in preparing federal tax returns or claims for refund for compensation must have a valid preparer tax identification number (PTIN). PTINs must be renewed each year, and current PTINs expire Dec. 31, 2026.
“The PTIN program helps the IRS identify legitimate paid preparers and reinforces the responsibility that comes with preparing federal tax returns,” said IRS Chief Executive Officer Frank J. Bisignano. “ IRS appreciates the time and effort that tax practitioners take each year to comply with the requirement to renew or obtain a PTIN.”
Renew PTINs online
The fastest way to renew a PTIN is online through the IRS PTIN System. Online renewal generally takes about 15 minutes.
To renew:
- Access the PTIN system on IRS.gov.
- Sign in to PTIN account and select “Renew my PTIN.”
- Review and update account information.
- Submit the application and pay the $18.75 fee, which is nonrefundable and nontransferable.
Once completed, applicants receive confirmation of their PTIN renewal.
Tax professionals who prefer to renew by mail can submit Form W-12, IRS Paid Preparer Tax Identification Number (PTIN) Application and Renewal. Paper applications can take about six weeks to process.
Other PTIN account features
The online PTIN system offers more than renewal. Tax professionals can use their accounts to:
- Check their completed continuing education.
- View the number of Form 1040 returns filed using their PTIN.
- Review communications from the IRS Tax Professional Management Office.
- Track their progress in the IRS Annual Filing Season Program.
Tax professionals should also keep their contact information current to ensure they receive important PTIN communications.
Annual Filing Season Program
Non-credentialed tax return preparers may also consider participating in the voluntary Annual Filing Season Program. Preparers who meet the program’s continuing education and other requirements receive a Record of Completion, are included in the IRS Directory of Federal Tax Return Preparers with Credentials and Select Qualifications and may have limited representation rights. More information is available through the Annual Filing Season Program on IRS.gov.
Reminder for enrolled agents
PTIN renewal is separate from enrolled agent renewal. Enrolled agents whose Social Security numbers end in 7, 8, or 9, as well as those without an SSN, are in the current enrollment renewal cycle, which runs through Jan. 31, 2027. Enrolled agents should also renew their PTINs for 2027.
title: IRS reminder: Tax professionals should renew their PTINs for 2027

A man who downloaded hundreds of photos and videos of child pornography was sentenced today to 12 years in federal prison.

Damon Wesley Powers, age 44, from Osage, Iowa, received the prison term after a July 1, 2026, guilty plea to one count of receipt of child pornography.

Evidence at a prior hearing showed that law enforcement officers searched Powers’s house in Osage in June 2025. Agents found child pornography on his phone, including depictions of prepubescent children. Powers had also stored hundreds of additional photos and videos of child pornography in a cloud‑based account. In an interview with law enforcement officers, Powers admitted that he had sent and received child pornography.

Powers was sentenced in Cedar Rapids by United States District Court Judge Leonard T. Strand. Powers was sentenced to 144 months’ imprisonment and was ordered to pay $24,350 in special assessments and restitution to victims. Powers must also serve a five-year term of supervised release after the prison term. There is no parole in the federal system.

This case was brought as part of Project Safe Childhood, a nationwide initiative to combat the growing epidemic of child sexual exploitation and abuse launched in May 2006 by the Department of Justice. Led by U.S. Attorneys’ Offices and CEOS, Project Safe Childhood marshals federal, state, and local resources to better locate, apprehend and prosecute individuals who exploit children via the Internet, as well as to identify and rescue victims. For more information about Project Safe Childhood, please visit Justice.gov/PSC .

Powers is being held in the United States Marshal’s custody until he can be transported to a federal prison.

The case was prosecuted by Assistant United States Attorney Devra T. Hake and investigated by the Iowa Division of Criminal Investigation Cyber Crime Bureau, the Internet Crimes Against Children Taskforce, and the Osage Police Department.

Court file information at https://ecf.iand.uscourts.gov/cgi-bin/login.pl .

The case file number is 26-CR-2015.

Follow us on X @USAO_NDIA.
title: Osage Man Sentenced to 12 Years in Federal Prison for Receiving Child Pornography

INDIANAPOLIS- A former United States Postal Service letter carrier, Destinee Ruffin, 29, of Indianapolis, has been sentenced to six and a half years in federal prison, followed by two years of supervised release, after pleading guilty to Conspiracy to Commit Bank Fraud and Theft of Mail. This case was brought as part of the Trump Administration’s Task Force to Eliminate Fraud.

According to court documents, Ruffin was employed as a letter carrier at the Bacon Station Post Office. Between April 2020 and May 2022, Ruffin used access to both incoming and outgoing mail to steal checks, which she then sold to co-conspirators.

In spring 2020, as the federal government issued Economic Impact Payment (EIP) checks to taxpayers, the USPS OIG received a complaint from a Bacon Station customer who never received theirs. Additional complaints soon followed. When agents reviewed the affected addresses and matched them to delivery routes, they discovered all missing checks were assigned to the same mail carrier, Destinee Ruffin.

In one example, Ruffin and McMullen exchanged 38 Cash App transactions totaling over $10,000 in payments from McMullen to Ruffin for stolen checks. Using the stolen checks, McMullen sought individuals on social media who were willing to deposit altered checks into their bank accounts. These individuals provided debit cards, PINs, or online banking credentials. McMullen altered the payee information on the stolen checks, deposited them, and later withdrew funds or demanded payment through Cash App or Zelle. In total, McMullen fraudulently negotiated 36 checks stolen from Bacon Station, worth approximately $235,632.

Ruffin sold even more stolen checks to Young. Young established trusted mid-level conspirators, primarily Eric Hollis (Hollis) and Kendall Thompson (Thompson), who deposited stolen checks into various accounts and recruited/ acquired account holders. Young would also list many of the stolen checks for sale on the internet-based application titled “Telegram.”

Investigators uncovered the scheme by mailing controlled Treasury checks with recorded serial numbers and tracing them back to Ruffin’s delivery route.

In April 2024, officers executed a search warrant on Ruffin’s vehicle, residence, person, and electronic devices. They discovered thousands of stolen checks valued at over $20 million that Ruffin had stolen but not yet sold. Stolen mail was found in her vehicle, on shelves, in closets, on the floor, stacked in corners, and even in the bathroom.

In total, Ruffin supplied Young with more than $12 million in stolen checks and provided McMullen with stolen checks worth more than $235,000.

For the intended recipients, the impact was severe. One victim explained that after mailing a $1,618 check to Sheet Metal Workers Local Union No. 20 Welfare and Benefit Fund—needed to maintain her retired husband’s health insurance—she learned the payment never arrived. She discovered the theft when she appeared for a scheduled surgery and was told her insurance had been terminated, forcing the procedure to be canceled. The United States Attorney’s Office estimates that approximately 6,500 victims were affected by this widespread fraud scheme.

Three of Ruffin’s co-conspirators have already been sentenced for their roles in the scheme. The final co-conspirator, John Young, is scheduled to be sentenced on December 3 rd , 2026.

“Destinee Ruffin’s crimes were not isolated acts of theft; they represented a sweeping scheme that touched thousands of households and eroded a fundamental public trust. By stealing millions of dollars’ worth of checks from the mail, Ruffin and her co-conspirators disrupted critical benefits, jeopardized family finances, and caused real harm to individuals who depended on timely delivery for essential needs,” said Tom Wheeler, United States Attorney for the Southern District of Indiana. “Today’s sentence reflects our commitment to protecting the integrity of the U.S. Postal Service and all government institutions, and to ensuring that those who exploit them for personal gain are held fully accountable.”

“The Treasury Inspector General for Tax Administration (TIGTA) aggressively investigates individuals who attempt to exploit U.S Treasury refund checks meant for hard working taxpayers for their own private gain,” said TIGTA Special Agent in Charge Kelly Moening. TIGTA’s mission is to protect the integrity of our nation’s tax administration system. We are committed to working with our law enforcement partners to ensure that those who violate federal laws are prosecuted to the fullest extent possible.

The U.S. Postal Service – Office of Inspector General, the United States Postal Inspection Service, and the Treasury Inspector General for Tax Administration investigated this case. The sentences were imposed by U.S. District Court Judge Sarah Evans Barker.

U.S. Attorney Wheeler thanked Assistant U.S. Attorney Adam Eakman, who prosecuted this case.

FORT BUCHANAN, Puerto Rico — Civilian employees and leaders from U.S. Army Garrison Fort Buchanan participated in a Building Strong and Ready Teams (BSRT) workshop Nov. 4 at the installation's Community Club to strengthen trust, improve teamwork and enhance organizational effectiveness in support of military readiness.
The workshop focused on the "speed of trust" concept, emphasizing how integrity, effective leadership and strong professional relationships help organizations operate more efficiently while reinforcing the Army's commitment to taking care of its people.
Col. David L. Brewer, Fort Buchanan garrison commander, opened the workshop by connecting trust directly to the installation's mission of supporting Soldiers and military formations.
"As you build trust in your organization, you're able to speed up your operations, and you're able to create more value for those individuals that we're serving," Brewer said.
Brewer explained that the installation workforce creates value by delivering services and resources that enable military readiness.
"We build value for the Soldiers, the formations that are operating and building readiness on our installation," Brewer said.
The commander also highlighted the importance of trust during leadership transitions, emphasizing that strong relationships help organizations adapt to change and achieve results faster.
He identified integrity as a fundamental leadership expectation, reminding employees that trust takes time to establish but can disappear in seconds.
"It's your integrity; you own it," Brewer said.
Installation Chaplain Farlin Reynoso facilitated the workshop, emphasizing the influence supervisors and directors have on organizational culture and employee development.
"You influence way more than you think," Reynoso said.
Reynoso also outlined plans to expand the training to employees throughout the installation, extending its benefits beyond senior leaders and supervisors.
For Eileen Santiago, an administrative assistant with the Directorate of Plans, Training, Mobilization and Security, the workshop offered an opportunity to reflect on trust and strengthen relationships with colleagues.
"It was motivating. It made me think about why we trust people, systems, family and friends," Santiago said.
She also valued the opportunity to interact with coworkers outside their daily work environment.
"Sharing time with coworkers outside the office was enriching. It allowed us to see other people's perspectives," Santiago said.
The workshop demonstrates how the Army in Puerto Rico takes care of its people by investing in professional development, strengthening workplace relationships and fostering an organizational culture built on trust and accountability.
With an annual budget exceeding $500 million, Fort Buchanan supports about 15,000 active-duty personnel, Soldiers of the Army Reserve and Puerto Rico National Guard, Marine Corps Reserve members and Navy Reserve personnel, providing infrastructure and services that enable forces to train, mobilize and deploy worldwide.
To stay connected with Fort Buchanan news and events, download the My Army Post app, select Fort Buchanan and activate notifications.
title: Fort Buchanan advances civilian employee readiness through trust-focused training

NEWARK, N.J. – A Bergen County, New Jersey man was sentenced to 20 years’ imprisonment for receipt and possession of multiple images of child sexual abuse, U.S. Attorney Robert Frazer announced.

Corey Hipscher, 55, of Lodi, New Jersey previously pleaded guilty yesterday before U.S. district Judge Wiliam J. Martini in Newark federal court to an Information charging him with receipt and possession of child pornography.

According to documents filed in this case and statements made in court:

From 2020 to August 2023, Hipscher communicated with a minor victim located outside of the United States using a social media platform. Hipscher encouraged the minor victim to send Hipscher images and videos of the minor victim engaging in sexually explicit conduct. Hipscher also began an online romantic relationship with the minor victim’s mother which he used to arrange for the minor victim and the minor victim’s family to visit him in New Jersey. During the visit, he sexually assaulted the minor victim and took sexually explicit photos of the minor victim and the minor victim’s sibling.

In addition to the prison term, Judge Martini sentenced Hipscher to 15 years of supervised release.

U.S. Attorney Frazer credited FBI Newark’s Child Exploitation and Human Trafficking Task Force, under the direction of Special Agent in Charge Stefanie Roddy in Newark, with the investigation leading to the charges. U.S. Attorney Frazer also thanked the Lodi Police Department and the Bergen County Prosecutor’s Office.

This case was brought as part of Project Safe Childhood, a nationwide initiative to combat the growing epidemic of child sexual exploitation and abuse launched in May 2006 by the Department of Justice. Led by U.S. Attorneys’ Offices and the Child Exploitation and Obscenity Section (CEOS) in the Justice Department’s Criminal Division, Project Safe Childhood marshals federal, state and local resources to better locate, apprehend and prosecute individuals who exploit children as well as to identify and rescue victims. For more information about Project Safe Childhood, please visit www.projectsafechildhood.gov

U.S. Attorney Frazer has announced proactive steps to connect with New Jersey’s families and communities, bringing training opportunities and resources through direct outreach. Organizations and community members interested in arranging prevention programming or learning more about available resources can contact the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the District of New Jersey at USANJ.CommunityOutreach@usdoj.gov . Moreover, prevention resources are available through the Department of Justice's Child Exploitation and Obscenity Section Prevention webpage and the Department of Homeland Security’s Know2Protect Campaign.

The government is represented by Assistant U.S. Attorney Sean Nadel of the Cybercrime Unit in Newark.

Fact Sheet

Office of the Spokesman

November 4, 2026

Today, the Department of State is designating two individuals and one entity that have been involved in efforts to help the Iranian regime obtain man-portable air-defense systems (MANPADS).

These designations continue a sustained U.S. campaign against Iran’s military procurement networks involving MANPADS. They follow actions on May 8, June 10, and July 15, 2026. Together, these actions close off more of the channels Tehran uses to try to rebuild its arsenal and raise the risk for third-country brokers and suppliers. Today’s action also supports enforcement of the UN arms embargo on Iran restored in September 2025. Those restrictions bar UN Member States from supplying such weapons to Iran.

The United States will keep exposing the networks that arm Iran’s military and the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps and will keep denying the regime the resources that sustain its destabilizing activities.

All three targets are being designated pursuant to Executive Order (E.O.) 13949, which targets certain persons with respect to the conventional arms activities of Iran. Designations Pursuant to Section 1(a)(iii) of E.O. 13949

(U) MOHAMMED ALI TOLIBOV ( TOLIBOV ) is the Chief Executive Officer of Armory Alliance and has contributed to Armory Alliance’s efforts to procure weapons on behalf of Iran. Armory Alliance is a Belarus-based entity that has acted as an intermediary between China-based companies and Iran and has been involved in efforts to facilitate the purchase of hundreds of MANPADS. Armory Alliance was previously designated pursuant to E.O. 13382 and E.O. 13949. TOLIBOV was previously designated under E.O. 13382.

(U) VANGUARD TACTICAL SUPPLY LIMITED ( VANGUARD ) is a Nigeria-based entity that has been involved in efforts to facilitate the procurement of Chinese-origin MANPADS for Iran via false end-users. VANGUARD was previously designated under E.O. 13382.

(U) ALISHER DOMULLODZHANOV ( DOMULLODZHANOV ) is a Russia-based individual who has been involved in efforts to facilitate the procurement of MANPADS for Iran.

Sanctions Implications

As a result of today’s sanctions actions, and in accordance with E.O. 13949, all property and interests in property of the designated persons described above that are in the United States or in possession or control of U.S. persons are blocked and must be reported to the Department of Treasury’s Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC). In addition, all entities that are owned, directly or indirectly, individually or in the aggregate, 50 percent or more by one or more blocked persons are also blocked.

All transactions by U.S. persons or within (or transiting) the United States that involve any property or interests in property of designated or otherwise blocked persons are prohibited unless authorized by a general or specific license issued by OFAC or exempt. These prohibitions include the making of any contribution or provision of funds, goods, or services by, to, or for the benefit of any blocked person and the receipt of any contribution or provision of funds, goods, or services from any such person.

The power and integrity of U.S. government sanctions derive not only from the U.S. government’s ability to designate and add persons to the Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons (SDN) List, but also from its willingness to remove persons from the SDN List consistent with the law.

Petitions for removal from the SDN List may be sent to: OFAC.Reconsideration@treasury.gov . Petitioners may also refer to the Department of State’s Delisting Guidance page.
