text:
The last week of October is Red Ribbon Week, and this year, White Sands Missile Range’s Army Substance Abuse Program turned White Sands School into a safe space to ask questions and learn. The dedicated ASAP team visited classrooms, delivering age-appropriate lessons on drug prevention, healthy choices, and the importance of staying drug-free. Students actively participated in activities and eagerly shared their perspectives.
Lively discussions blossomed as students opened up about peer pressure, friendship, and ways to make positive decisions both in and out of school. To top it off, the team handed out vibrant bracelets, pencils, and other fun swag, giving each child a lasting keepsake and a daily reminder of the commitment to a drug-free lifestyle.
The 2026 theme is “Make a Difference. Be a Hero. Stay Drug Free.” The team brought activities and real-life scenarios to classrooms, ensuring students of all ages understood why it matters to say no to drugs. Their hands-on approach made a big impact, sparking thoughtful conversations and empowering students to be heroes in their own lives.
Red Ribbon Week honors Special Agent Enrique “Kiki” Camarena. Camarena served in the U.S. Marine Corps for two years in 1968, then joined the Drug Enforcement Administration.
Camarena was detailed to go to Mexico, where he remained on the “trail of the country’s biggest marijuana and cocaine traffickers,” according to the DEA. However, in 1985, Camarena was tortured and murdered by drug traffickers whom he was investigating in Mexico.
title: ASAP Empowers Students to Be Heroes During Red Ribbon Week

text:
SALT LAKE CITY, Utah — An Oregon man is now in federal custody and charged in a criminal complaint with transportation with intent to engage in criminal sexual activity after he allegedly met a Utah minor online in May 2025, drove to Utah to pick up the victim, and then transported the victim to his residence across state lines. The minor was recovered by law enforcement at the residence on Nov. 1.

“Anyone engaged in the sexual exploitation of a minor will be held accountable,” said Attorney General Todd Blanche. “Today’s arrest is the first step toward bringing the accused to justice and relieving the pain endured by the victim and her family. This Department of Justice will never stop investigating and prosecuting individuals engaged in vicious predatory behavior.”

“This individual is charged with transporting a minor to another state to engage in criminal sexual activity, a minor who was missing for a year and a half until Oregon police recovered her based on information provided by the FBI,” said FBI Director Kash Patel. “According to the criminal complaint the minor was groomed on gaming platforms and engaged in acts of self-harm and sexually explicit activity. To anyone targeting and exploiting children: this FBI and our partners are coming for you. We are using every tool at our disposal to combat nihilistic violent extremism, bring offenders to justice, and protect America’s most vulnerable. I want to thank the FBI Salt Lake Field Office, the Oregon State Police, and federal prosecutors for their outstanding work on this case.”

“Our priority in this case was the safe return of the minor victim,” said U.S. Attorney Melissa Holyoak for the District of Utah. “Those who allegedly exploit and prey upon the most vulnerable members of our communities will be relentlessly investigated and held accountable. I want to thank the FBI and our local law enforcement partners in Oregon for their swift efforts to safely recover the victim and for their continued partnership as we pursue justice for the victim and the victim’s family.”

Adam Hunter Harmel, 39, of Huntington, Oregon, was charged in a federal complaint on Nov. 2 in the District of Utah. He had his initial appearance on the complaint on Nov. 4 at the U.S. District Courthouse in Boise, Idaho.

According to court documents, beginning in or about May 2025 and continuing until Nov. 1, in the District of Utah and elsewhere, Harmel allegedly transported the minor victim with the intent to engage in sexual activity with the victim. On or about Aug. 20, 2025, FBI Salt Lake City received information that the minor victim had disappeared in May 2025. During the investigation, the FBI learned that the minor victim was allegedly groomed on gaming platforms that are commonly used by Nihilistic Violent Extremist (NVE) Groups members to solicit sexually explicit photos and maiming photos. The grooming then transitioned to other social media applications. On Nov. 1, the FBI received a tip about the possible location of the minor victim and that the victim met Harmel on a social media application in May 2025. As alleged in court documents, Harmel kept a knife under his pillow to prevent the minor victim from escaping.

The case is being investigated by the FBI Salt Lake City Field Office in conjunction with the FBI Joint Terrorism Task Force. Valuable assistance was provided by the Oregon State Police.

Assistant U.S. Attorney Jawayria Z. Auchter for the District of Utah and Trial Attorneys Justin Sher and James Donnelly of the National Security Division’s Counterterrorism Section are prosecuting the case.

A complaint is merely an allegation, and all defendants are presumed innocent until proven guilty beyond a reasonable doubt in a court of law.
title: Utah Minor Recovered by Law Enforcement After Oregon Man Allegedly Transported the Victim to Engage in Criminal Sexual Activity

Coast Guard offloads over $27 million in cocaine at Port Everglades
Southeast Public Affairs - SoutheastPublicAffairs@uscg.mil
MIAMI — U.S. Coast Guard Cutter Tahoma’s crew offloaded approximately 3,622 pounds of cocaine and four detainees, Wednesday, in Port Everglades.
The offload is from two interdictions resulting in the seizure of the illicit narcotics and the apprehension of four detainees in the Caribbean Sea.
Federal agents took custody of the four detainees, pending further investigation.
“This interdiction was due to the coordinated efforts of Joint Interagency Task Force - South, U.S. Customs and Border Protection, Coast Guard Southeast District, along with our international partners throughout the Caribbean Sea,” said Lt. John Colucci, commanding officer of William Trump. “I’m incredibly proud of the crew of CGC William Trump in their ability to carry out this high-risk mission in a safe, efficient, and professional manner. Their success directly prevented illicit narcotics from reaching our shores and disrupted the operations of transnational-criminal organizations throughout the western hemisphere."
The following assets and crews were involved in the interdiction operations: 
- Coast Guard Cutter Diligence
- Coast Guard Cutter William Trump   
- USS Minneapolis-Saint Paul
- U.S. Coast Guard Tactical Law Enforcement Team – Pacific, LEDET 105 
- A Royal Netherlands Navy maritime patrol aircraft 
- A U.S. Customs and Border Protection maritime patrol aircraft 
- Joint Interagency Task Force – South
- Southeast District watchstanders
The offload highlights the Coast Guard’s continued efforts to interdict illicit narcotics, disrupt transnational criminal organizations and prevent dangerous drugs from reaching American communities.
The U.S. Coast Guard works alongside local, state, federal and international partners to detect, deter and disrupt maritime drug trafficking. Through persistent operations and coordinated law enforcement efforts, Coast Guard crews help protect the nation’s maritime borders and prevent illicit narcotics from entering the United States.
Coast Guard Cutter Tahoma is a U.S. Coast Guard cutter responsible for conducting maritime law enforcement, search and rescue, and other missions in support of the Coast Guard’s national security and maritime safety objectives.

Oahu, Hawaii – Caring for Hawaii’s coastline takes more than one organization. It takes neighbors, community partners and people willing to work together toward a common goal. The spirit of service brought U.S. Army Garrison Hawaii and community organizations together on October 24th to conduct a coordinated cleanup at Dillingham Army Beach, highlighting the importance of partnerships in addressing shared environmental and public safety concerns.
“I am extremely proud of our U.S. Army Garrison Teams who partnered with our community to make a huge difference in such a short amount of time,” said Col. Rick Luce, Commander of U.S. Army Garrison Hawaii. “Being able to work side-by-side with the City and State, not to mention the local non-profit organizations who provide the services for the homeless and houseless is a tremendous honor and duty for our team,” Luce said.
The effort was about more than removing debris. It demonstrated how collaboration across government agencies and community organizations can address shared challenges while creating opportunities for service and civic engagement.
Among the participating organizations was Hawaii Youth Challenge Academy, a program that helps young teens and adults develop leadership, discipline, life skills and a sense of personal responsibility.
For the Army, that connection is particularly meaningful. Service is a value shared by military members and the young people preparing to become future leaders in their communities.
The cleanup also highlighted the importance of established partnerships with HDOT and Hala Toa Mui Contractors. Working alongside the Army and other participating organizations, the partners supported a coordinated effort to address mounting debris and environmental concerns along the coastal property.
According to HDOT, approximately 30 tons of debris were removed from six encampment sites during the four-hour operation. Crews also collected two five-gallon buckets of hazardous medical waste.
The operation involved the Honolulu Police Department, Surfrider Foundation, Kealahou West Oahu and the garrison’s Directorate of Public Works Environmental Division and Directorate of Emergency Services Military Police.
Beyond the immediate cleanup, the effort illustrated the importance of maintaining relationships with organizations that share a commitment to Hawaii’s communities and natural resources.
For USAG Hawaii, stewardship does not end at the installation boundary. Working with state agencies, youth programs and local organizations helps address concerns that affect both the military and civilian communities.
The Dillingham Army Beach cleanup was one example of how those relationships can translate into action – bringing different organizations together in service of a shared home.
title: Beyond the fence: Army and community partners work together to clean up Dillingham Army Beach

CONCORD – A federal Bureau of Prisons (BOP) inmate was sentenced today in federal court for escaping a Manchester halfway house, U.S. Attorney Erin Creegan announces.

Daniel Irving, 35, was sentenced by U.S. District Judge Steven J. McAuliffe to an additional 6 months in prison. On July 15, 2026, Irving pleaded guilty to escape from federal custody. He was previously serving an eight-year sentence for conspiracy to distribute methamphetamine when he was transferred from a federal prison to the Hampshire House halfway home in Manchester. In October 2025, Irving tested positive for cocaine and was instructed to return to Hampshire House for discipline. Irving instead cut off his GPS monitor and ran. He was at large for four months until the U.S. Marshals captured him in late February 2026.

“Our system trusted the defendant to follow the rules by releasing him to a halfway home,” said U.S. Attorney Creegan. “Mr. Irving violated that trust and will now face additional time in federal prison. We will continue to work with our state and federal law enforcement partners to impose accountability on individuals who have shown themselves to be a danger to our communities and make sure they complete their sentences. Any attempt to escape will result in clear consequences.”

“We are incredibly proud of the U.S. Marshals Service team that worked diligently to apprehend Mr. Irving,” said Acting United States Marshal for the District of New Hampshire Katherine Burns. “Our unwavering commitment to enforcing court orders is an important part of holding those engaged in the justice system accountable for their attempts to circumvent it.”

The United States Marshals Service led the investigation. The Goffstown Police Department and the Manchester Police Department provided valuable assistance. Assistant U.S. Attorneys Matthew Vicinanzo and Alexander S. Chen prosecuted the case.
title: Federal Inmate Who Fled From Halfway House Sentenced to Additional Prison Time

CFTC and USDA Sign MOU to Protect Integrity of American Agricultural Markets
November 04, 2026
WASHINGTON — The Commodity Futures Trading Commission and the U.S. Department of Agriculture today announced their signing of a Memorandum of Understanding intended to safeguard the integrity of U.S. agricultural markets.
The MOU will allow the CFTC and USDA to harmonize policies and practices to better share information and increase access to risk management tools. The agreement will also assist both agencies with monitoring and identifying structural or potential systematic risks, among other things.
“For decades, America’s agricultural community has relied on our markets to hedge risk, manage uncertainty, and plan for the future,” said CFTC Chairman Michael S. Selig. “I’m proud that the CFTC and USDA have formalized this partnership through an MOU that will strengthen protections for America’s farmers, ranchers, and producers while expanding opportunities to manage risk through more efficient data sharing. I commend Secretary Rollins for her partnership and commitment to a more coordinated regulatory approach that safeguards the integrity of our markets and ensures they continue serving the agricultural community that feeds and clothes our nation.”
“Faster and more transparent data sharing between USDA and CFTC is critical to helping our farmers and ranchers navigate an ever-changing market,” said USDA Secretary Brooke Rollins. “This MOU builds upon USDA’s ongoing data modernization efforts and allows our agencies to collaboratively identify risks and improve responses to market events. Breaking down barriers between government agencies to deliver for our customers is a hallmark of this administration and I am looking forward to the successes this MOU will bring.”
-CFTC-
title: CFTC and USDA Sign MOU to Protect Integrity of American Agricultural Markets

Acting Secretary of the Navy Appoints Rear Admiral Jonathan Rucker to Lead Portfolio Acquisition Executive (PAE) Maritime
04 November 2026
WASHINGTON — Acting Secretary of the Navy Hung Cao announced today that Rear Adm. Jonathan Rucker has been appointed Portfolio Acquisition Executive (PAE) Maritime. PAE Maritime is the Navy organization responsible for delivering surface ships to the Fleet.
“President Trump has given me a clear mandate: build the Golden Fleet,” said Cao. “Admiral Rucker is the right leader at the right time to bring accountability to and accelerate our American shipbuilding system.”
Rucker has served as the Director of Design and Construction for Direct Reporting Portfolio Manager, Submarines since April 2026, where he has been responsible for the design and construction of all submarines. Prior to this, Rucker served as the Program Executive Officer (PEO) for Attack Submarines, Program Manager of the COLUMBIA Class Submarine Program and Program Manager of the Unmanned Maritime Systems Program.
As PAE Maritime, Rucker is charged with leading the Navy’s surface ship acquisition efforts across the shipbuilding enterprise. He will work with the Deputy Chief of Naval Operations for Warfighting Requirements and Capabilities, Navy Warfare Centers, shipyards, and industry partners to move ship programs through requirements, design, construction, delivery, and operational sustainment in the Fleet.
“We owe it to our Sailors and Marines to deliver the ships they need at speed with capability and quality to ensure they maintain our competitive advantage,” said Rucker. “I am eager to build the Fleet America needs now.”
Rucker brings operational experience and more than two decades of Navy acquisition experience to PAE Maritime. He deployed to Iraq during Operation Iraqi Freedom, serving as Chief Engineer in charge of jamming systems supporting counter improvised explosive device efforts. In addition to his leadership positions as PEO and program manager, he served as Lead Ship Coordinator, Supervisor of Shipbuilding, Groton and Military Assistant for the Undersecretary for Defense for Acquisition, Technology, & Logistics.
Rucker holds a bachelor’s degree in electrical engineering from Duke University, a Master of Business Administration degree from the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill, and a Naval Engineer degree and master’s degree in electrical engineering from the Massachusetts Institute of Technology.
title: Acting Secretary of the Navy Appoints Rear Admiral Jonathan Rucker to Lead Portfolio Acquisition Executive (PAE) Maritime

CAMP HUMPHREYS, South Korea – When an unexpected water outage hit the installation over the Chuseok holiday weekend, Sept. 25–26, 2026, the crisis became an immediate test of operational readiness.
For Master Sgt. Tyler Smith and a team of Soldiers working alongside Department of Public Works personnel, restoring flow meant working around the clock to put the community’s needs first while reinforcing the installation's resilience and mission-ready posture.
As a contracting support noncommissioned officer with the 906th Contracting Battalion, Master Sgt. Tyler Smith is accustomed to negotiating with vendors, managing pricing, and placing orders through formal contract mechanisms. But nothing quite prepared him for the holiday weekend, when the utility failure shut down critical operations across the installation, leaving Soldiers and families without running water.
"The initial reaction is the expected time frame of how long it's going to take to be repaired," Smith said. "The hours kept passing, and then have to start making phone calls to vendors, and there is not much traction because, like I said, they're on holiday."
With vendors unresponsive due to the holiday, Smith and his team quickly realized waiting wasn't an option. Securing the massive order of 100 portable latrines meant working late into the night to coordinate delivery and strategic dispersion across the installation.
Amidst the chaos, Smith stepped in as a vital bridge between the Emergency Operations Center, the 2nd Infantry Division, and outside suppliers, connecting agencies and personnel who had never worked together before.
Smith noted that the biggest hurdle was the grueling schedule, dealing with late-night emergency meetings, waiting for updates, and pushing through the sheer exhaustion of the operation.
"The biggest hurdle, I would say, was the late night,” Smith said. "Waiting for those updates and... processing things on the back end, so I guess just dealing with being tired. It was pretty stressful.”
Though the situation demanded long hours and stressful coordination against holiday roadblocks, Smith and the rest of the response team ultimately succeeded in getting the critical infrastructure back online.
Working alongside the Department of Public Works ensured base operations quickly returned to standard capacity and that families and Soldiers received the assistance they needed during the outage.
Reflecting on the recognition, Smith noted that as leaders promote, accolades often slow down because they are focused on looking out for everyone else. Receiving an award from an external garrison command, he said, made the acknowledgment feel especially meaningful.
"It was a pretty good feeling that not only did it not come from my own command, but that the garrison reached out to an external organization and provided that recognition," Smith said.
Ultimately, the crisis proved that readiness is not just about scheduled training exercises, but about how quickly a joint team of Soldiers and civilians can pivot when an unexpected emergency strikes. For Smith and the rest of the personnel behind the scenes, restoring the water supply meant more than just fixing base infrastructure; it meant ensuring the Camp Humphreys community could get back to the mission without missing a beat.
title: Going Above and Beyond: Soldier Recognized for Water Outage Assistance at Camp Humphreys

DORAL, Fla. — U.S. and Colombian armies officially launched Exercise Southern Vanguard 2027 on Nov. 2, bringing together approximately 800 military personnel to strengthen interoperability, readiness, and bilateral security cooperation. The 41st iteration of the annual exercise is hosted by the Colombian Army, sponsored by U.S. Southern Command (SOUTHCOM) and led by U.S. Army Western Hemisphere Command (USAWHC), with approximately 350 U.S. military personnel and more than 400 Colombian Army soldiers participating.
The exercise aims to strengthen soldiers’ skills, improve their ability to operate together in challenging environments, and enhance mutual readiness. Colombia’s role as host underscores the importance of the U.S.-Colombia security partnership and regional military cooperation.
“American and Colombian soldiers operating with shared purpose, mutual trust, and professional discipline,” said Brig. Gen. Peter L. Gilbert, USAWHC G-4 Deputy Chief of Staff. “You will sweat together, you will learn together, and you will build bonds that can only be forged through shared hardships and shared accomplishment.”
Following the opening ceremony, U.S. and Colombian soldiers will conduct combined training focused on jungle exercises and counter-improvised explosive device tactics. The exercise also includes a command post and field training exercise, with broader training objectives spanning maritime interdiction, ground security, cyber defense and interagency cooperation. These activities will promote knowledge-sharing, strengthen interoperability and improve combined readiness.
“I extend a warm and fraternal greeting to all officers, non-commissioned officers, soldiers and international partners participating in the Southern Vanguard 2027 exercise,” said Brig. Gen. Edilberto Cortés, Chief of the Force Generation Staff
of the Colombian National Army. “This presence demonstrates the shared commitment of our nations to strengthen collective readiness and consolidate the ties of cooperation that support our strategic and historical relationship.”
Building on more than 200 years of diplomatic relations, the United States and Colombia continue to strengthen their military partnership through combined training and professional knowledge-sharing. Southern Vanguard 2027 aims to improve readiness, reinforce interoperability, and support peace, stability, and security across the Western Hemisphere.
title: U.S. and Colombian armies officially launch joint exercise to strengthen readiness and regional security

HOHENFELS, Germany — Soldiers assigned to the 1st Infantry Division and deployed in support of Operation Atlantic Resolve participated in exercise Combined Resolve 27-01 at the 7th Army Training Command’s Joint Multinational Readiness Center in Hohenfels, Germany, from Oct. 4 through Nov. 4, 2026.
Combined Resolve is a recurring U.S. Army Europe and Africa exercise that provides rotationally deployed forces the opportunity to train in a demanding, realistic environment across the European theater.
“As the regionally aligned division headquarters, we are providing the higher command, or HICOM, element,” said Maj. Taylor Mextorf, chief of the 1st Infantry Division Analysis and Control Element. “We provide the command signals a division would have, offer resources and coordination, and enable the brigade to receive the best tactical-level training possible on this terrain during its rotation.”
The HICOM element provides a division-level command framework for the brigade training in the field. It replicates key division staff functions and gives the rotational unit the opportunity to operate within a broader battlefield structure.
“From an intelligence perspective, much of our discussion has focused on the process of handing off information to support situational awareness: what the enemy is doing, the decisions they are making, what that means for us, and how our command can respond in support of targeting throughout the battlefield framework,” Mextorf said.
Mextorf said the HICOM element helps provide the fidelity of a full division staff to an armored brigade combat team operating in a relatively confined training area. The framework includes neighboring units competing for resources and support, creating a more realistic operational environment for the brigade.
The Joint Multinational Readiness Center provides brigade-level units the opportunity to train as they fight, achieve mission-essential training objectives, and consolidate lessons learned across diverse terrain. The training helps formations strengthen warfighting proficiency, refine tactics and procedures, and improve readiness.
Large-scale combat operations exercises such as Combined Resolve require detailed preparation, including weeks or months of training before the rotation and continued process refinement throughout the exercise.
Earlier this year, the 1st Infantry Division executed a warfighter exercise focused on adaptability in an evolving operational environment.
“That was the culminating event after about a year’s worth of training progression, from CPX 0 through CPX 3,” Mextorf said. “It was the crawl-walk-run training methodology at a higher echelon.”
“We established our structures and refined them through the CPX progression,” Mextorf said. “Once we reached the headquarters exercise, we settled on what worked best for us. We brought all that refinement into this exercise to continue building lethality and readiness.”
The JMRC combat training center exercise series supports NATO’s Eastern Flank Deterrence Initiative by helping validate regional plans, strengthen warfighting readiness, and employ emerging capabilities that support deterrence and defense across the European theater.
“For an armored brigade combat team whose objective is to destroy the enemy by fire, maneuver, and shock effect, there is no better way to do that than getting an entire brigade in a place where it can maneuver, synchronize, integrate with higher headquarters, and bring in enabling effects and capabilities,” Mextorf said. “They can truly exercise that on this terrain.”
title: 1st Infantry Division Provides Higher Command Element for Combined Resolve 27-01

ABINGDON, Va. – A man who used Snapchat to sexually exploit a pair of middle school girls from Southwest Virginia, was sentenced yesterday to 25 years in federal prison.

Justin Steven Boileau, 31, a former resident of Reston, Va. who also spent time in Merritt Island, Fla., pled guilty in February 2026 to two counts of sexual exploitation of children.

“Protecting children from online threats is a clear prosecution priority in the Western District of Virginia,” First Assistant United States Attorney Robert N. Tracci said today. “We will continue to work with our partners at the FBI, as well as state and local law enforcement, to seek accountability for online sexual predators.”

According to court documents, Boileau used the messaging app Snapchat to entice two minor females from Southwest Virginia – Minor Victim One and Minor Victim Two– to engage in sexually explicit conduct for the purpose of producing visual depictions of such conduct. Additionally, law enforcement has confirmed Boileau enticed at least 9 other minors to produce CSAM in other jurisdictions.

Specifically, in the fall of 2023, Boileau began conversing with Minor Victim One via Snapchat. At the time, Boileau was in his late 20s and resided in Reston, Virginia. Minor Victim One was twelve years old at that time and lived in Russell County, Va. Boileau portrayed himself online as a hockey player named ‘Josh’ and began conversating with Minor Victim One in an explicitly sexual manner. These conversations continued over the course of several months through the early part of 2024. During these conversations, Boileau asked Minor Victim One for sexually explicit depictions of herself. At Boileau’s request, Minor Victim One sent, among other things, nude photos and videos of herself. Boileau also sent images to Minor Victim One of what he claimed to be his penis.

Additionally, in early 2024, Boileau used Snapchat to converse with Minor Victim Two, a twelve-year-old minor who lived in Russell County, Va. As with Minor Victim One, Boileau’s conversations with Minor Victim Two were sexual in nature. At Boileau’s request, Minor Victim Two sent him nude pictures and pictures of herself masturbating. Boileau also directed his minor victims to write messages on their bodies when they produced CSAM images for him.

Boileau knew both Minor Victim One and Minor Victim Two were minors when he requested these images and videos.

The case was investigated by the Federal Bureau of Investigation and the Russell County, Virginia Sheriff’s Office.

Assistant United States Attorney Carrie Macon is prosecuting the case for the United States.

The case was brought as part of Project Safe Childhood. In 2006, the Department of Justice created Project Safe Childhood, a nationwide initiative designed to protect children from exploitation and abuse. Led by the U.S. Attorneys’ Offices and the DOJ’s Child Exploitation and Obscenity Section, Project Safe Childhood marshals federal, state, and local resources to locate, apprehend, and prosecute individuals who exploit children, as well as identity and rescue victims. For more information about Project Safe Childhood, please visit www.projectsafechildhood.gov/ .
title: Former Reston Man Sentenced to 25 years For Sexual Exploitation of 12-year-old Girls

Earlier today, at the federal court in Central Islip, an indictment was unsealed charging Nicholas Del Franco, the owner and operator of purported financial services companies in New York and California, with seven counts of wire fraud, in connection with numerous overlapping advance fee and prepaid interest fraud schemes targeting businesses, real estate developers, and individuals in search of financing. Del Franco was arrested this morning and is being arraigned this afternoon before United States Magistrate Judge Anne Y. Shields.

Joseph Nocella, Jr., United States Attorney for the Eastern District of New York, and James C. Barnacle Jr., Assistant Director in Charge, Federal Bureau of Investigation, New York Field Office (FBI), announced the charges.

“As alleged, Del Franco engaged in years-long overlapping schemes designed to steal millions of dollars from borrowers who believed they were paying required fees and upfront interest to secure loans,” stated United States Attorney Nocella. “Now that his repeated lies are exposed, Del Franco will be held accountable for his egregious conduct, and his victims will see some measure of justice.”

"Borrowers deserve transparency and honesty when entering into loan agreements, not deception and fraud. Nicholas Del Franco allegedly exploited the lending process for personal gain, and the FBI will continue to investigate those who seek to undermine our financial system," stated FBI Assistant Director in Charge Barnacle.

As set forth in the indictment and other filings, from approximately November 2023 to the present, Del Franco, the owner and operator of Quattro Capital LLC and Ares 2811 Corporation, engaged in advance fee and prepaid interest fraud schemes targeting prospective borrowers in search of financing. His victims, over a dozen of whom have been identified to date, included businesses, real estate developers, and individuals. As part of these schemes, Del Franco falsely claimed to be a legitimate loan broker with access to substantial funding sources and lines of credit, including banks and private lenders, and purported to offer prospective borrowers multi-million-dollar loans with highly attractive terms for construction, real estate development, and business expansion.

These schemes included: (1) a line of credit advance fee scheme, whereby Del Franco falsely claimed to have access to a $100 million line of credit from a financial institution insured by the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation, to which prospective borrowers would be given full access in exchange for an upfront escrow payment of $5 million; (2) a “family office” funding prepaid interest scheme, whereby Del Franco falsely claimed to represent a wealthy family whose “family office” was seeking to extend multi-million dollar loans for various construction and infrastructure projects, but required borrowers to make an upfront payment of a percentage of the full loan amount as prepaid interest; and (3) a private investors prepaid interest scheme, whereby Del Franco falsely asserted that he represented several wealthy private investors seeking to fund multi-million dollar loans for construction and infrastructure projects, but required borrowers to make an upfront payment of a percentage of the full loan amount as prepaid interest.

In each scheme, Del Franco fraudulently induced the victim borrowers to pay him money purported to be advanced fees or prepaid interest before receiving the promised loan. After the prospective borrowers paid the upfront funds, however, the loans and access to lines of credit never materialized. Instead, Del Franco stole the money for himself. In total, Del Franco defrauded over a dozen prospective borrowers of more than $5 million in connection with his schemes.

The charges in the indictment are allegations and the defendant is presumed innocent unless and until proven guilty. If convicted, Del Franco faces up to 20 years’ imprisonment on each of the seven counts.

If you or someone you know is a victim of this scheme, please call the FBI tip line: 1-800-CALL-FBI (1-800-225-5324).

The government’s case is being handled by the Criminal Section of the Office’s Long Island Division. Assistant United States Attorney Michael R. Maffei is in charge of the prosecution.

The Defendant :

NICHOLAS DEL FRANCO (also known as “Nicholas Thomas”) Age: 39 Point Pleasant, New Jersey

E.D.N.Y. Docket No. 26-CR-305 (AYS)
title: Purported Loan Broker Indicted for Advance Fee and Prepaid Interest Fraud Schemes

text:
FORT HUACHUCA, Ariz. — Throughout 2026, the U.S. Army Information Systems Engineering Command conducted engineering initiatives to improve Army readiness and support the joint services. As a subordinate command of the U.S. Army Communications-Electronics Command under the Army Materiel Command, USAISEC delivered systems engineering, modernized secure communications, expanded institutional capabilities, and strengthened military installation resilience worldwide. Through a combination of technology solutions, workforce development, and organizational realignments, USAISEC supported Department of War operations across multidomain environments.
Strategic realignments
This year, major realignments and portfolio consolidations expanded the USAISEC area of responsibility to include communications security and information distribution functions. These changes strengthened accountability, centralized expertise, and positioned USAISEC to deliver more integrated, responsive support to DoW organizations worldwide:
- Army Media Distribution Center: USAISEC acquired the AMDC mission, integrating the lifecycle management and worldwide delivery of mission-critical technical manuals, publications, and forms into the command’s technology portfolio.
- Communications Security Logistics Activity: In a historic realignment that divided CSLA logistics and operations support under two separate commands, USAISEC gained the Central Office of Record functions, Tier 1 operations for cryptographic key distribution, and COMSEC account field assistance. These capabilities now comprise the USAISEC Communications Security Directorate.
Super intelligence innovations
During 2026, USAISEC accelerated the adoption of past artificial intelligence and emerging SI frameworks to transform operational data into actionable intelligence and strengthen Army resilience. These initiatives demonstrated how USAISEC is using SI-enabled decision support and integrated data to strengthen secure communications, protect critical infrastructure, and enable faster, more informed decisions across the U.S. Armed Forces:
- Communications Security Operations Center: By leveraging SI, USAISEC shifted COMSEC account oversight from labor-intensive, reactive administration toward a centralized, data-driven model. The CSOC consolidated data to improve visibility of COMSEC account health, compliance, risk mitigation, and cryptographic materiel requirements. This overview gave commanders actionable information while preserving their responsibility for decision-making based on personal experience and situational awareness.
- Joint Task Force-Southern Border: The USAISEC Data Science Team partnered with the JTF-SB Operations Research Analysis Team to revolutionize data utilization across the DoW and the Department of Homeland Security. Operating within Palantir’s Maven Smart System platform, USAISEC data scientists constructed automated data pipelines and SI-driven regression and Bayesian models to forecast detection trends and identify critical capability gaps. This effort shifted U.S. southern border operations from delayed historical reporting to event-driven forecasting with high statistical confidence.
- Project Installation Resiliency and Mission Assurance: USAISEC advanced Project IRMA at Fort Huachuca to turn fragmented utility and infrastructure information into a scalable, near-real-time, decision-support capability. Through working groups with Army installation sustainment, local garrison, and public utility partners, USAISEC refined operational technology network architecture, system design, and infrastructure requirements to create localized pilot projects intended to validate the platform before enterprise expansion. Project IRMA development integrated SI and machine learning to provide a consolidated view of utility infrastructure health to garrison commanders while analyzing energy demands and sustainment costs. To expand project awareness, USAISEC demonstrated IRMA capabilities at the 2026 National Cyber Summit.
Army transformation support
Throughout the year, USAISEC supported Army Continuous Transformation by developing construction standards and supporting cybersecurity or lifecycle sustainment requirements. These initiatives strengthened military resilience across the joint services:
- Military construction standards: USAISEC served as a telecommunications engineering authority for the joint services, contributing field expertise to help shape MILCON standards. Working in conjunction with the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, Naval Facilities Engineering Systems Command, and Air Force Civil Engineer Center, USAISEC co-authored Unified Facilities Criteria (UFC 3-580-01) for inside and outside plant infrastructure. USAISEC continues to work with USACE to update Unified Facilities Guide Specifications: UFGS 33 82 00 for outside plant cabling and UFGS 27 10 00 for building telecommunications cabling systems. The DoW implemented these mandatory standards for MILCON projects across all the armed services.
- Risk Management Framework as a Service: By utilizing the RMFaaS model, USAISEC helped Army and joint organizations maintain cybersecurity compliance, secure operational and information technology systems, and sustain mission readiness despite increasingly complex standards and shortages of qualified personnel. RMFaaS provided organizations with cybersecurity subject matter experts who performed critical compliance functions and supported the full RMF lifecycle. This effort allowed other commands to maintain current authorities to operate, focus on core missions, respond to evolving threats, and strengthen installation resilience.
Workforce development investments
Recognizing that engineering expertise remains the foundation of technical dominance, USAISEC invested in activities to promote future recruits, technical development, and professional growth for civilian and military specialists during 2026:
- Community outreach: To strengthen its impact across southern Arizona, USAISEC participated in science, technology, engineering, arts, and mathematics, or STEAM, programs designed to cultivate future technical talent. Through hands-on demonstrations, technical workshops, and real-world engineering challenges, USAISEC interacted with local middle and high school students to encourage their interest in engineering careers. These engagements fostered community partnerships while reinforcing the Army’s pipeline for future engineers.
- COMSEC training: USAISEC conducted the first hybrid symposium that provided online and in-person training opportunities for the COMSEC community. Through the Central Office of Record Corner, the command offered additional online COMSEC training about automated cryptographic key accounting, risk mitigation, and emergency destruction protocols to personnel across the U.S. Armed Forces.
- Technical seminars: Through an academic partnership, USAISEC hosted several in-person Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers Talks at Fort Huachuca and attended collaborative events at Arizona State University. These lectures provided engineers with critical insights into technical subjects, such as supply chain modernization, agentic SI, data analytics, quantum computing decryption attacks, cyclic redundancy checks, and antenna radiation patterns and measurements.
Looking ahead to 2027
As USAISEC concludes an extraordinary year of achievement, the command remains positioned to meet the operational demands of tomorrow. Through disciplined execution, innovative SI integration, meticulous infrastructure standardization, and an unwavering commitment to its people, USAISEC will continue to build, defend, and sustain the resilient information architecture that enables the U.S. Army to deploy, fight, and win across any domain.
Headquartered at Fort Huachuca, Arizona, USAISEC delivers responsive, resilient communication and information systems engineering to empower multidomain operations across the globe. For more information about the capabilities and services USAISEC provides, email inquiries to USAISEC@army.mil.

Medicare Outpatient Final Rule Expands Surgical Options, Lowers Out-of-Pocket Costs for 340B Drugs
A new Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) rule will expand outpatient surgery options, lower out-of-pocket costs for imaging services and 340B drugs, and strengthen oversight of select services. The rule also updates 2027 payment rates for hospital outpatient departments and ambulatory surgical centers (ASCs).
“CMS is committed to spending taxpayer funds wisely and efficiently, so America’s seniors can continue getting the care they need,” said CMS Administrator Dr. Mehmet Oz. “By right-sizing payments and rooting out waste, today’s reforms will drive affordability in Medicare for current beneficiaries while ensuring it will still be there to serve their children and grandchildren.”
CMS is updating payment rates for drugs purchased under the 340B Drug Pricing Program to better reflect what hospitals pay for these medications. A CMS survey found that hospitals acquire 340B drugs at an average cost significantly below the Average Sales Price (ASP) — consistent with findings from the Medicare Payment Advisory Commission (MedPAC) and industry reports showing that Medicare payments have substantially exceeded 340B drug acquisition costs.
By better aligning payments with documented acquisition costs, CMS estimates this policy will save people with Original Medicare an estimated $1.1 billion in drug costs and save taxpayers an additional estimated $4.35 billion in drug expenditures, reducing total drug spending by approximately $5.45 billion in 2027 alone. Beneficiaries who receive a qualifying drug in the hospital outpatient department are expected to save an average of $900 in drug costs in calendar year (CY) 2027. This policy ensures that hospital drug discounts are passed directly to the Medicare beneficiaries who receive the drugs and to American taxpayers.
People with Medicare often face different copayments for imaging services depending on where they receive care. CMS is extending its policy of paying the lower Physician Fee Schedule equivalent rate, rather than the Outpatient Prospective Payment System (OPPS) rate for imaging without contrast services, including certain bone density scans, x-rays, ultrasounds, CT scans, and MRIs, performed at off-campus provider-based departments. This policy already applies to clinic visits and drug administration services at those locations. CMS estimates the change would save beneficiaries and taxpayers a total of $260 million in CY 2027 and over $9 billion from CY 2027 to CY 2036.
The rule also continues to phase out the “Inpatient Only” procedure list, which will allow more services to be delivered in outpatient settings, and it also continues to expand the ASC covered procedures list by several hundred surgical procedures. These changes give physicians more flexibility to choose an appropriate care setting and give patients more outpatient surgical options while maintaining patient safety. The expanded policies will often lower beneficiaries’ cost-sharing obligations.
CMS also finalized a proposal that allows hospital accrediting organizations with CMS-approved “deeming authority” to assess hospital compliance with certain Emergency Medical Treatment and Labor Act (EMTALA) administrative requirements as part of routine accreditation and reaccreditation surveys. This integrates EMTALA administrative oversight into the existing deeming framework.
To address unnecessary increases in certain botulinum toxin-related services, CMS will add eight additional botulinum toxin injection codes to the list of hospital outpatient services requiring prior authorization. Hospital outpatient department claims for these eight codes rose 42.8% from 2017 to 2024, an average of 4.6% per year, while overall hospital outpatient service volume fell 8.3%. CMS found no clinical or coding explanation for the increase. U.S. Department of Justice reports have also documented fraudulent billing, misbranded products, and improper payments involving botulinum toxin services. Medicare will continue to cover medically necessary injections, including treatment for chronic migraines and certain other conditions, when a physician documents the need.
The final rule supports the Trump Administration’s broader goal of improving Medicare by promoting affordable care, patient choice, and responsible stewardship of taxpayer dollars.
Review the Calendar Year 2027 Hospital Outpatient Prospective Payment System (OPPS) and Ambulatory Surgical Center Final Rule on the Federal Register at: www.federalregister.gov/public-inspection/.
View the fact sheet on the final rule at: https://www.cms.gov/newsroom/fact-sheets/calendar-year-2027-hospital-outpatient-prospective-payment-system-opps-ambulatory-surgical-center-0.

ASHEVILLE, N.C. – Shawnenna Caroline Roland, 41, of Cherokee, an enrolled member of the Eastern Band of Cherokee Indians, appeared in federal court today and pleaded guilty to child abuse, child neglect, and assault in Indian Country, announced Russ Ferguson, U.S. Attorney for the Western District of North Carolina.

“There is no excuse for treating a helpless child this way,” said U.S. Attorney Russ Ferguson. “Roland relentlessly assaulted and abused a child entrusted in her care, causing the child serious and lasting harm. This is disgusting behavior that will land you in federal prison.”

According to plea documents, between May 6 and May 20, 2024, Roland repeatedly assaulted a child resulting in serious bodily injury, including permanent and protracted loss and impairment of the child’s mental and emotional function. Plea documents show that Roland assaulted the victim on multiple occasions, hitting the victim with “switches,” banging her fist on the victim’s fingers, and striking her multiple times. According to court documents, on May 20, 2024, Roland banged the victim’s head into a wooden couch frame. Roland did not seek immediate medical attention for the victim. First responders came to Roland’s residence where they found the victim unresponsive, after another minor in the home called 911. The victim was flown by helicopter to the hospital and received treatment for traumatic brain injury. Court documents show that a bone scan performed at the hospital revealed several healing fractures throughout the victim’s body, including on the victim’s right arm, pelvis, and both hands. The victim’s nose was also broken, and the victim had sustained multiple bruises and abrasions, in addition to having torn ligaments in the neck and a fractured sacrum.

Roland remains in federal custody. At sentencing, she faces a sentence of up to 395 months in prison. A sentencing date has not been set.

U.S. Attorney Ferguson thanked the FBI and the Cherokee Indian Police Department for their investigation of the case.

Assistant U.S. Attorney Alex M. Scott of the U.S. Attorney’s Office in Asheville is prosecuting the case.
title: Cherokee Woman Pleads Guilty to Inflicting Serious Bodily Injury on a Child in Indian Country

Tallahassee, Florida –Christy Cody Holgate, 49, and Kim Demetrius Benson, 53, both of Tallahassee, Florida, have been sentenced in federal court after pleading guilty to conspiracy to commit mail theft, and multiple counts of mail theft. Holgate was sentenced to over three and a half years in federal prison. Benson was sentenced to two years’ imprisonment. The sentences were announced by John P. Heekin, United States Attorney for the Northern District of Florida.

U.S. Attorney Heekin said: “These defendants sought to enrich themselves by stealing the mail, but now they’ll see the inside of a federal prison cell. My office is committed to aggressively prosecuting anyone who tampers with, steals, or diverts the U.S. Mail to ensure our citizens can continue to rely upon the U.S. Postal Service to quickly, safely, and securely deliver the mail.”

Court documents reflect that between August 5, 2025, and December 5, 2025, the defendants broke into multiple apartment complex mailboxes through use of United States Postal Service (USPS) mail key that permitted access to the mail of complex residents. Through investigation, the U.S. Postal Inspection Service and Tallahassee Police Department documented multiple thefts of hundreds of pieces of mail. They also obtained video surveillance which captured the break-ins. Upon their arrest in December 2025, the two were found in a vehicle containing bags of stolen mail items along with stolen debit and credit cards, as well as a USPS mail key. Together, the defendants conspired to steal U.S. Mail, which, according to a confession by Holgate, was then sold to another individual for money to purchase illegal drugs.

This case was jointly investigated by the Tallahassee Police Department and the United States Postal Inspection Service. The case was prosecuted by Assistant United States Attorney Eric K. Mountin.

The United States Attorney’s Office for the Northern District of Florida is one of 94 offices that serve as the nation’s principal litigators under the direction of the Attorney General. To access public court documents online, please visit the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of Florida website. For more information about the United States Attorney’s Office, Northern District of Florida, visit https://www.justice.gov/usao-ndfl .

CMS Finalizes CY 2027 Physician Fee Schedule to Shift from Sick Care to Healthcare and Curb Waste
WASHINGTON, D.C.—NOVEMBER 4, 2026—The Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) is prioritizing prevention, strengthening primary care, cracking down on duplicate billing, and reinforcing fiscal stewardship across Medicare. A new final rule advancing payment policies under Medicare Part B modernizes physician payment structures to reward health maintenance and coordinated primary care rather than disjointed, volume-based intervention. Through targeted enhancements to the Medicare Shared Savings Program (Shared Savings Program) and fee schedule recalibrations, CMS is shifting the health system’s focus from reactive sick care to proactive healthcare.
“Medicare should reward clinicians for keeping people healthy,” said HHS Secretary Robert F. Kennedy, Jr. “Under President Trump’s leadership, we are putting prevention and primary care at the center of Medicare, closing payment loopholes, and cracking down on waste. This rule directs resources toward coordinated care that puts patients first. We are changing what Medicare pays for to change what our health system delivers.”
“For too long, fee-for-service payment has rewarded volume over value, fueling a reactive system of sick care,” said CMS Administrator Dr. Mehmet Oz. “This final rule breaks from that status quo. By ending duplicate billing and closing costly loopholes, we are protecting taxpayers and directing Medicare dollars to clinicians doing the hard work of keeping patients healthy.”
Modernizing Quality Reporting and Statutory Mandates
Marking a decade of progress under the Quality Payment Program, CMS will officially sunset the traditional Merit-based Incentive Payment System (MIPS) reporting option beginning with the CY 2031 performance period. Clinicians will have through CY 2030 to transition to the MIPS Value Pathways (MVPs), which already cover approximately 98%of clinicians, or Advanced Alternative Payment Models. This reflects two additional years of transition time compared to the proposed rule. The rule also finalizes three new MVPs focused on diabetes, hypertension, and hospitalists, and requires clinicians to report at least one specialty-specific “Core Measure” starting in CY 2027.
Additionally, the Calendar Year (CY) 2027 Medicare Physician Fee Schedule (PFS) rule finalizes two new billing codes dedicated to Advance Care Planning and codifies noncitizen Medicare eligibility criteria established by the Working Families Tax Cuts legislation.
Expanding and Strengthening Accountable Care Organizations
Accountable Care Organizations (ACOs) are vital to improving primary care and helping beneficiaries live healthier lives. Data shows that patients aligned with an ACO are less likely to experience uncontrolled diabetes or hypertension and are more likely to receive recommended preventive care. In performance year 2024, 75% of the 476 participating ACOs earned shared savings totaling $4.1 billion, while generating net savings for the Medicare Trust Funds of approximately $2.5 billion compared to projected spending benchmarks.
The Shared Savings Program has generated savings for the Medicare Trust Funds for eight consecutive performance years, and to build on this progress, the final rule:
- Permits ACOs to Eliminate Patient Cost-Sharing: Starting April 1, 2027, approved ACOs may reduce or eliminate Part B cost-sharing for many items and services for assigned beneficiaries, directly lowering out-of-pocket costs for essential care.
- Incentivizes Growth: CMS increases shared savings rates for eligible ACOs, provides new incentives for first-time participants, and sets more predictable spending targets.
- Cuts Red Tape: The rule simplifies electronic health record reporting requirements, streamlines patient notice mandates, and removes outdated administrative hurdles.
Restoring Payment Integrity and Curbing Waste
CMS is recalibrating fee schedule valuations to reflect the true complexity and resources of modern care and closing loopholes that allow users to game the system:
- Ending Duplicate Billing: When an office visit and minor procedure occur on the same day, CMS will reduce payment by 20% for the lower-cost service, reducing duplication in payment by patients and the Medicare program for clinical work already covered in the procedure’s valuation.
- Closing Windfall Loopholes: The rule corrects an incentive payment loophole, preventing an estimated $2.38 billion in unintended windfall payments over the next decade.
- Improving Rate Accuracy: CMS is streamlining outdated steps from its rate-setting formula, leading to greater simplicity and transparency for clinicians and patients while allowing payment policy to adapt to changes in healthcare delivery.
CMS Expands Access to Preventive Care and Wellness in Support of MAHA Initiative
CMS is finalizing critical coding and payment expansions to strengthen preventive care and wellness across the nation. CMS is establishing national payment pathways for health and well-being coaching under general supervision, introducing dedicated billing for shared medical appointments with flexible time-based add-on codes, and boosting valuations for smoking cessation and behavioral health assessments.
Additionally, the agency is finalizing separate billing for the dedicated clinical time required to diagnose, treat, and counsel patients experiencing vaccine adverse effects, reinforcing our commitment to patient trust and robust clinical support. These pivotal updates ensure Medicare resources directly support proactive, patient-centered care and improve health outcomes for Americans.
Ambulatory Specialty Model
CMS is also finalizing refinements to the Ambulatory Specialty Model — a CMS Innovation Center model launching Jan. 1 that holds specialists accountable for the quality and cost of care associated with the longitudinal management of two common chronic conditions, heart failure and low back pain, to slow disease progression and reduce avoidable hospitalizations and low-value procedures.
For more information on the CY 2027 Physician Fee Schedule Final Rule, which is effective Jan. 1, 2027, visit the Fact Sheet for Calendar Year (CY) 2027 Medicare Physician Fee Schedule Final Rule.
For a fact sheet on the updates on the Shared Savings Program, visit: https://www.cms.gov/newsroom/fact-sheets/calendar-year-cy-2027-medicare-physician-fee-schedule-final-rule-cms-1848-f-medicare-shared-savings.
To view the final rule on Federal Register, visit: https://www.federalregister.gov/d/2026-22743.

OKLAHOMA CITY – Scott Maule, Civil Division Chief for the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Western District of Oklahoma, has been nationally recognized for excellence in leadership and management by the Executive Office for the United States Attorneys (EOUSA), announced U.S. Attorney Robert J. Troester.

Maule was formally recognized during the 2026 Director’s Awards ceremony on October 28, 2026, held at the Department of Justice in Washington D.C., where he received the Director’s Award for Excellence in a Managerial or Supervisory Role, an honor recognizing outstanding leadership, management, and service within the Department of Justice. Maule was one of just seven managers selected from U.S. Attorney’s Offices across the country to receive the award.

Civil Division Chief Scott Maule receives the Director’s Award for Excellence in a Managerial or Supervisory Role. Pictured from left to right are Acting Deputy Attorney General Trent McCotter, Scott Maule, EOUSA Director Francey Hakes, and U.S. Attorney Robert J. Troester.

“Scott is an exceptional leader whose dedication, professionalism, intellect, and commitment to public service make our office stronger every day,” said U.S. Attorney Robert J. Troester. “His ability to lead by example and navigate complex legal matters reflects the best of the Department of Justice. The people of the Western District of Oklahoma are well served by Civil Chief Scott Maule.”

Maule is a 19-year veteran of the U.S. Attorney’s Office and has served as Chief of the Civil Division since 2019. He has also served as the healthcare fraud coordinator, civil rights coordinator, and the discovery coordinator for the Civil Division. From 2021-2026, Maule was selected to serve on a national Civil Chief’s Working Group where he was at the forefront of addressing the most difficult legal and policy issues facing the Department of Justice. From 2021-2026, he also served as a member of a national eLitigation Working Group helping lead the Department’s efforts to prepare for and address the ever-emerging technical, policy, and practice issues involving eLitigation. Over his 19-year career, Maule has represented the United States and its agencies, officials, employees, and agents in a wide range of both affirmative and defensive cases at the trial and appellate level in federal and state courts. Maule received his Bachelor of Arts degree from the University of the South (Sewanee) in 1999, and his J.D. from the William & Mary Law School in 2002.

The award was presented by the Director of EOUSA. EOUSA provides oversight, general executive assistance, and direction to the 94 United States Attorneys’ offices around the country. For more information on EOUSA and its mission, visit http://www.justice.gov/usao .
title: Western District of Oklahoma Civil Division Chief Honored with Prestigious Department of Justice Award

Seattle – A 40-year-old Pierce County, Washington man was sentenced late yesterday in U.S. District Court in Seattle to 15 years in prison for attempted enticement of a minor and production of images of child sexual abuse, announced Acting U.S. Attorney Charles Neil Floyd. Randy Lee Young came into federal custody April 24, 2025. He was arrested November 16, 2024, after allegedly communicating with someone he thought would provide her young daughters to him for sexual assaults. When Young arrived at the proposed meeting place in Marysville, Washington, he was arrested. Forensic review of his cell phone found images of child sexual abuse that he had produced.

At the sentencing hearing U.S. District Judge Lauren King praised the victim’s “truthfulness and assistance with law enforcement” and conveyed “hope todays sentencing brings you a sense of some closure” as “the only blame here lies with Mr. Young and Mr. Young alone.”

“The community is safer with this defendant off the street,” said Acting U.S. Attorney Neil Floyd. “Mr. Young made his intentions clear while communicating with the undercover officer. Then when he was arrested law enforcement discovered a 13-year-0ld had already been victimized. This lengthy sentence is the appropriate result.”

“Not only did Mr. Young demonstrate he was willing to travel across Washington state to exploit children, but his phone also contained videos of him actually abusing a child on multiple occasions,” said W. Mike Herrington, Special Agent in Charge of the FBI Seattle field office. “We hope this sentence will protect the youth of the Pacific Northwest from Mr. Young for a long time and sends a strong message to other would-be predators that they cannot hide behind supposed anonymity online. The FBI and our partners will pursue these offenders and hold them to account for the lifelong harm they have inflicted on our children.”

According to records filed in the case, Young began communicating with a law enforcement officer who was posing as the mother of 8 and 11-year-old daughters. Between November 8 and 15 2024, Young communicated with the law enforcement officer via text messaging multiple times. Ultimately Young drove from his residence in Pierce County to the location in Marysville where he was arrested. Young was held in the Snohomish County Jail until the federal charges were filed.

Young gave permission for law enforcement to review his cell phone. On the phone investigators found images of sexual abuse of a minor. The investigation revealed that in October and November 2024, Young met a minor online, traveled to her hometown in southwest Washington seven times and videotaped sex acts with the 13-year-old. Text messages reveal that the victim had told Young her age.

In her victim statement, the mother of the 13-year-old said, “He stole more than her innocence. He stole her sense of safety, her ability to trust, and parts of a childhood that she cannot get back…. As her mother, one of the hardest parts has been knowing that I cannot go back, that I cannot undo what happened, and that I cannot give her back the innocence and sense of security that were taken from her.”

In asking for the 15-year sentence, prosecutors wrote to the court, “The defendant chatted with the undercover officer about his intentions for eight days before showing up to act on his desires. He was provided opportunities to disengage and instead doubled down by informing the undercover he wanted to follow through with his ‘fetish’…. (T)here are simply too many individuals wired to abuse children to ever eliminate child exploitation, it is vitally important that these would-be offenders understand the steep cost of acting on their deviant desires. The law must send a clear and unmistakable message of specific and general deterrence – that society simply will not and cannot tolerate such perverted abuse – and those that engage in it, will be met with lengthy custodial sentences.”

Juge King ordered Young to be on supervised release for 20 years following his prison term. A separate hearing in February 2027 will determine the amount of restitution owed to Young’s victim.

The case is being investigated by the FBI Seattle’s Child Exploitation and Human Trafficking Task Force, with assistance from the Renton Police Department.

The case is being prosecuted by Assistant United States Attorney Cecelia Gregson.

The Justice Department is committed to combating child sexual exploitation. These cases were brought as part of Project Safe Childhood, a nationwide initiative to combat the epidemic of child sexual exploitation and abuse launched in May 2006 by the Department of Justice. Led by U.S. Attorneys’ Offices and CEOS, Project Safe Childhood marshals federal, state, and local resources to better locate, apprehend, and prosecute individuals who exploit children via the internet, as well as to identify and rescue victims. For more information about Project Safe Childhood, visit www.justice.gov/psc .
title: Pierce County man sentenced to 15 years in prison for sex crimes involving minors

Fact Sheet

Office of the Spokesman

November 5, 2026

Today, the Department of State is designating eight entities and two individuals, and identifying five vessels as blocked property, to further the Trump Administration’s comprehensive push to end the Cuban regime’s malign activities, both in Cuba and across our hemisphere. This action includes targets associated with the Cuban regime’s oil shipping networks, Cuban elites, state-owned import and technical-support entities, and China-based suppliers of the regime’s military forces.

All Department of State targets sanctioned today have been designated pursuant to Executive Order (E.O.) 14404, which authorizes sanctions on foreign persons determined to meet specified criteria related to repression in Cuba and other threats to U.S. national security and foreign policy.

Additionally, today the Director of the Department of the Treasury’s Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) issued a determination pursuant to E.O. 14404 that authorizes sanctions against any foreign person operating or having operated in the manufacturing, technology, electronics, and marine sectors of the Cuban economy. The identification of these new sectors targets the regime and those who enable it, not the Cuban people. The United States continues to authorize humanitarian trade, including food, medicine, and medical devices, and supports the free flow of information to the Cuban people.

Cuban Regime’s Illicit Revenue Networks

Cuba’s ruling elite hoards the island’s energy and shipping resources for its own enrichment, leaving the Cuban people to contend with blackouts, fuel shortages, and a stagnant economy. To keep this system running, the regime relies on a web of offshore intermediaries. Today, the Department of State is designating part of an extensive shipping network moving crude oil and petroleum products for the Cuban regime.

GUILLERMO FAUSTINO RODRIGUEZ LOPEZ CALLEJA (GUILLERMO) is part of an extensive network of maritime shipping companies moving petroleum products to and from Cuba. GUILLERMO is being designated pursuant to Sec. 2(a)(i)(A) of E.O. 14404 for operating in or having operated in the energy sector of the Cuban economy.

CAROIL TRANSPORT MARINE LTD (CAROIL) , a Cyprus-based company that manages Cuban-flagged crude oil tankers that have transported energy products in Cuba. Treasury previously designated CAROIL on September 24, 2019, pursuant to E.O. 13850. CAROIL is being designated pursuant to Sec. 2(a)(i)(A) of E.O. 14404 for operating in or having operated in the energy sector of the Cuban economy. The following vessels are being identified as property in which CAROIL has an interest:

ESPERANZA (IMO: 9289166): CAROIL is the commercial manager. Treasury previously identified ESPERANZA as blocked property of CAROIL on December 3, 2019.

GLORIA C (IMO: 9540273): CAROIL is the commercial manager. TENTACOOL COMMERCIAL INC, is the registered owner.

MARIA CRISTINA (IMO: 9502453): CAROIL is the commercial manager and registered owner. Treasury previously identified MARIA CRISTINA as blocked property of CAROIL on September 24, 2019.

TENTACOOL COMMERCIAL INC (TENTACOOL) , a Panama-based company and the registered owner of the GLORIA C. TENTACOOL is being designated pursuant to Sec. 2(a)(i)(A) of E.O. 14404 for operating in or having operated in the energy sector of the Cuban economy.

INTERNACIONAL MARITIMA SA , a Cuba-based company and the registered owner of the ESPERANZA. INTERNACIONAL MARITIMA SA is being designated pursuant to Sec. 2(a)(i)(A) of E.O. 14404 for operating in or having operated in the energy sector of the Cuban economy.

PETROLEOS MARITIMOS DEL CARIBE S.A. (PETROMARCA) , a Cuba-based company and the ship manager and operator of two Cuban-flagged petroleum product tankers. PETROMARCA is being designated pursuant to Sec. 2(a)(i)(A) of E.O. 14404 for operating in or having operated in the energy sector of the Cuban economy. The following vessels are being identified as property in which PETROMARCA has an interest:

EMILIA (IMO: 9242209): PETROMARCA is the commercial manager and registered owner.

LOURDES (IMO: 9259692): PETROMARCA is the commercial manager.

Cuban Elites

Regime insiders and their family members continue to profit from the Cuban regime’s control of the island’s economy, including through opaque networks tied to Grupo De Administracion Empresarial S.A. (GAESA), the Cuban military’s business conglomerate. Today, the Department of State is designating the daughter of the previously designated GAESA President.

ANY RODRIGUEZ LASTRES (LASTRES) , the daughter of the sanctioned GAESA President Ania Guillermina Lastres Morera. LASTRES is being designated pursuant to Sec. 2(a)(i)(I) of E.O. 14404 for being an adult family member of ANIA GUILLERMINA LASTRES MORERA, a person whose property and interests in property are blocked pursuant to this order. LASTRES also previously served as the Commercial Director of U.S.-designated Terminal De Contenedores De Mariel S.A.

State-Owned Entities of the Cuban Regime

The Cuban regime relies on a web of state-owned enterprises that control the island’s technology resources and direct revenue to the state rather than to the Cuban people. Today, the Department of State is designating the following two Cuban state-owned entities pursuant to Sec. 2(a)(i)(B) of E.O. 14404 for being owned, controlled, or directed by, or having acted or purported to act for or on behalf of, directly or indirectly, the Government of Cuba.

EMPRESA IMPORTADORA Y EXPORTADORA DE PRODUCTOS DE LA ELECTRONICA Y LAS COMUNICACIONES (CUBAELECTRONICA) , a Cuban state-owned importer of supplies and equipment for Cuba’s electronics industry.

EMPRESA COMERCIALIZADORA DE SERVICIOS TECNICOS Y TECNOLOGICOS (TECNOSIME) , a Cuban state-owned entity that conducts commercial, labor, and promotional activities that generate revenue for the Cuban state.

Chinese Companies’ Support to the Cuban Military

As the Department’s July 20 report Cuba: The Capital of 21st Century Communism noted, the Cuban regime’s continuing partnerships with China and Russia have supplied Cuba with military hardware, surveillance technologies, and other security capabilities. Today, the Department of State is taking aim at Cuba’s foreign backers by designating two China-based corporations that have supplied the Cuban regime with components and equipment to sustain the Cuban military. The transfer of this equipment involved the Cuban company Sociedad Mercantil Duna S.A., which was designated by the Department of State on August 6, 2026 , and has been involved in the import of military-related equipment from China and Russia to Cuba.

The following entities are being designated pursuant to Sec. 2(a)(i)(D) of E.O. 14404 for having materially assisted, sponsored, or provided financial, material, or technological support for, or goods or services to or in support of, the Government of Cuba.

CHINA NATIONAL ELECTRONIC IMPORT AND EXPORT COMPANY (CEIEC) , a China-based state-owned enterprise that exports defense electronics, security systems, and construction engineering services. Additionally, CEIEC contracted with the Cuban arms procurement entity Sociedad Mercantil Duna S.A. to export components intended for military equipment used by the Cuban Ministry of Revolutionary Armed Forces (MINFAR) in 2026. CEIEC was previously designated by the Department of the Treasury pursuant to E.O. 13692 on November 30, 2020 , in relation to its support for the Maduro regime’s efforts to restrict internet service and conduct digital surveillance and cyber operations against political opponents.

BEIJING H&C TECHNOLOGIES CO., LTD , a China-based subsidiary of China Electronics Technology Group Corporation (CETC) International Co., Ltd. (CETCI) that sells surveillance and security equipment. Additionally, BEIJING H&C TECHNOLOGIES CO., LTD worked with the Cuban arms procurement entity Sociedad Mercantil Duna S.A. to export military equipment to Cuba in 2026.

Sanctions Implications

As a result of today’s sanctions actions, and in accordance with E.O. 14404 of May 1, 2026, “Imposing Sanctions on Those Responsible for Repression in Cuba and for Threats to U.S. National Security and Foreign Policy,” all property and interests in property of the designated persons described above that are in the United States or in possession or control of U.S. persons are blocked and must be reported to OFAC. Additionally, all entities that are owned individually or in the aggregate, 50 percent or more by one or more blocked persons are also blocked.

All transactions and dealings by U.S. persons or persons within (or transiting) the United States that involve any property or interests in property of designated or otherwise blocked persons are prohibited unless authorized by a general or specific license issued by OFAC or exempt. These prohibitions include the making of any contribution or provision of funds, goods, or services by, to, or for the benefit of any blocked person and the receipt of any contribution or provision of funds, goods, or services from any such person. Foreign persons that engage in transactions with persons designated pursuant to E.O. 14404—or that operate or have operated in the electronics, energy, defense and related materiel, manufacturing, marine, metals and mining, financial services, security, or technology sector of the Cuban economy, as identified in and determined pursuant to E.O. 14404—are themselves at risk of sanctions. Non-U.S. persons, including foreign financial institutions, should proceed with caution in any dealings with a party sanctioned under this authority. Actions to return assets to a sanctioned party or transfer them to another jurisdiction for potential use by the target expose non-U.S. persons to significant sanctions risk. All property and interests in property of persons that are blocked pursuant to the Cuban Assets Control Regulations (CACR) continue to be blocked. The CACR prohibits persons subject to U.S. jurisdiction from dealing in property in which Cuba or a Cuban national has an interest, unless authorized or exempt.

The power and integrity of U.S. government sanctions derive not only from the U.S. government’s ability to designate and add persons to the Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons (SDN) List, but also from its willingness to remove persons from the SDN List consistent with the law. The ultimate goal of sanctions is not to punish, but to bring about a positive change in behavior.

Petitions for removal from the SDN List may be routed through OFAC’s Reconsiderations Portal . Petitioners may also refer to the Department of State’s Delisting Guidance page.
